stories.Headline: MiTAC Computing unveils full-stack infrastructure to scale agentic AI for enterprises
stories.Summary:
MiTAC Computing Technology Corporation unveiled a comprehensive AI infrastructure ecosystem at the SC26 event in Chicago on November 17, 2026. The company is a subsidiary of MiTAC Holdings Corporation and is a global leader in high-performance server solutions. They used Booth 4615 to demonstrate how full-stack innovation overcomes compute, thermal, and data bottlenecks for enterprise AI. This new ecosystem aims to scale agentic AI by addressing the exponential surge in inference workloads. MiTAC collaborated with AMD, Canonical, DDN, Intel, NVIDIA, and Rafay to deliver these scalable AI factory architectures.

The G8825Z5 server uses AMD EPYC 9575F or 9755 processors and AMD Instinct MI350X GPUs for the prefill stage. The G4520G6 decode server uses Intel Xeon 6 processors and eight Skymizer HTX301-4S cards with 256 GB of memory each. This setup provides 2 TB of aggregate memory to run the 2.8-trillion-parameter Kimi K3 model on premises. The upcoming ORv3 44OU Helion solution will scale up to 32,768 AMD Zen 6 CPU cores for hyperscale environments. A 52U rack integrates 12 G4826Z5 servers with 96 AMD Instinct MI355X GPUs for 50 percent higher density.

Rick Hwang is the President of MiTAC Computing Technology and he is responsible for these new infrastructure developments. He stated that scaling agentic AI requires cohesive infrastructure rather than fragmented systems to be successful. Hwang believes that MiTAC provides the foundational full-stack solution necessary to make sustainable AI factories a reality. The company uses proprietary MiCoreView software to grant deep telemetry and unified visibility across the entire data center. This software binds the ecosystem together to manage the various pods and hardware components effectively.

The system affects enterprises by allowing them to provision each stage of their workload while keeping inference on premises. Canonical Ubuntu provides the certified operating system layer to ensure seamless deployment and enterprise-grade reliability for users. DDN Infinia ensures monumental data streams are processed with low latency to prevent accelerator data starvation for clients. Rafay empowers organizations with dynamic GPU-as-a-Service orchestration to eliminate idling and maximize the return on investment. ZutaCore partners with MiTAC to provide waterless two-phase direct liquid cooling for chips exceeding 4,000W thermal design power.

MiTAC Computing has delivered energy-efficient server solutions based on industry expertise that dates back to the 1990s. The company specializes in AI, HPC, cloud, and edge computing across barebones, systems, racks, and cluster levels. They have a worldwide presence with end-to-end capabilities ranging from research and development to global support. The current innovations build on a vision announced by AMD Chair and CEO Dr. Lisa Su last month. MiTAC has unified its brand with Intel DSG and TYAN server products to provide integrated hardware and software.

Attendees can visit Booth 4615 at McCormick Place from November 17 to 19 to see the rack-scale innovations. The company offers various platforms like the G4827Z6, G2610Z6, and TN85-B8261 for customized enterprise and edge AI deployments. Management servers like the R1917GC and R1610Z6 coordinate complex clusters and provide single-socket performance for cloud-native workloads. Multi-node servers include the M2810Z6 for hyper-converged infrastructure and the liquid-cooled C2611Z6 for OCP ORv3 racks. The articles leave open the specific release dates for the upcoming Helion Agentic AI Rack solution.

stories.Headline: Meta runs JiTTests in production to catch risky code changes before merge
stories.Summary:
Meta has moved its Catching Just-in-Time Tests, known as JiTTests, from a research prototype into its production infrastructure, according to a report published on 16 November 2026. JiTTests is an LLM-based system that writes executable tests designed to fail on a risky code change, so that a failing test becomes concrete evidence that a diff changed behavior. The Meta team reports that JiTTests caught 74 privacy SEVs at the diff stage in the first half of 2026, and the method is described in the FSE 2026 research paper titled "Just-in-Time Catching Test Generation at Meta." The system runs on Meta backend code with hundreds of millions of lines, and the research paper analyzes 22,126 generated tests. The system runs overnight on spare capacity and selects the previous day's risky diffs using a mechanism similar to Meta's Diff Risk Score.

Two diff-aware workflows produce candidate tests: the dodgy diff workflow assumes every diff is buggy and treats it as a mutant of its parent, while the intent-aware workflow first infers what the diff should do from its code, title and summary, then lists risks and builds a mutant for each. An LLM-as-Judge ensemble scores each failing test using the test code, failure trace, diff and inferred intent, and a Rule-Based False-Positive Killing Environment called RubFake adds deterministic checks that flag patterns such as reflection, broken mocks and not-implemented exceptions. A human-on-the-loop step decides whether to contact an engineer based on the combined ranking, and the rule-based and LLM assessors cut human review load by 70%. The research team reports that diff-aware methods produced 4x more candidate catches than hardening tests and 20x more than tests that failed by coincidence. The intent-aware workflow produced weak catches in 6.4% of its tests and on 7.9% of diffs, while dodgy diff scored 2.5% and 4.0%, and Meta's earlier ACH mutation-guided hardening scored 0.8% and 1.6%.

Engineers report a 60% true-positive rate at full scale, which is self-reported, and privacy SEV occurrence is down 20%. The initial deployment confirmed only 8 of 41 reported catches, or 19.5%. The judge models named in the paper are Llama3.3-70B, Gemini 3 Pro and Claude Sonnet 4, and the system is not publicly available. Meta formalized the details in its 2025 paper "Harden and Catch," and the team concedes that executing code takes more computational steps than having an LLM or agent read the diff and leave comments. The team argues the approach catches bug classes that LLM or agent review can miss, and the bottom line the report gives is executable proof of a bug before merge, with the caveat that the numbers are internal and self-reported.

stories.Headline: OpenAI adds computer-use agents and over 20 plugins to ChatGPT for Healthcare
stories.Summary:
OpenAI announced on November 16, 2026, that it is expanding ChatGPT for Healthcare with advances in computer-use agents, improved trusted clinical search, and more than 20 new healthcare plugins. The computer-use agents can navigate existing healthcare software by reading screens, clicking, typing, and moving between applications. OpenAI said it is working with healthcare organizations including Abridge, Ambience, Cigna Healthcare, and CVS Health to process referrals, move documents between systems, and bring together information care teams need. The announcement was reported by HCI Innovation Group on Nov. 17, 2026, in an article by Pietje Kobus-McAllister. The updates are intended to help healthcare organizations reduce time spent navigating disconnected software and streamline workflows from referral management and documentation to insurance verification and care coordination.

The computer-use agents include access controls and audit logs, and organizations can set which applications agents can access and which steps require human review. To support HIPAA-compliant workflows involving protected health information, organizations must use eligible services covered by their BAA with OpenAI, apply required security and retention settings, and extend protections to connected systems. Content shared with ChatGPT for Healthcare is not used to train models. In a blind evaluation, physicians reviewed responses to real-world clinical questions across multiple specialties, including multi-turn conversations, and in over 1300 reviews rated the updated experience more highly across all eight dimensions evaluated, including factual correctness, safety, actionability, and source authoritativeness. All of the more than 20 new plugins are available today in ChatGPT for Healthcare, including through ChartGPT, which brings ChatGPT into the EHR workflow.

The plugin list includes Aiva, Amion, Assort Health, Availity, Extend, Elation Health, Ferry, IMO Health, MCP Server, Infinitus, Relay, K Health, Luma Health, Metriport, Notable Integration Specs, Oracle HDI Overview, PenguinAI Medical Coding, Photon, Redox, Stedi, Subsalt, Trizetto, Turquoise, and UpToDate Expert AI. Elation Health's read-only beta plugin lets primary care practice managers use ChatGPT to identify patients scheduled for the following day who have gaps in insurance, registration, or contact information, and staff receive a list of issues to review and address in Elation's electronic health record before patients arrive. Kyna Fong, co-founder and CEO of Elation Health, said AI earns its place in primary care by helping the people who use it, and that the company earns it by being thoughtful about its use, maintaining control, and using it to make stronger systems. Infinitus is bringing its Relay agents into ChatGPT to support benefits verification and prior authorization workflows, and users can initiate a benefits verification, check the status of a prior authorization and identify next steps, or submit batch requests using a spreadsheet. Ankit Jain, CEO of Infinitus, said the next chapter of AI in healthcare won't be defined by how much information it can surface but by what it can actually accomplish.

The Elation beta is initially available to a limited group of Elation practices, and the company said the approach is designed to keep administrative work with AI while leaving clinical decisions and patient outreach under the control of practice teams. Relay is available to existing Infinitus customers using ChatGPT for Healthcare, and the integration is designed to let healthcare and life sciences organizations access Infinitus agents without leaving ChatGPT. Jain said healthcare is full of complex, interconnected workflows that require more than answering questions, requiring navigating systems, taking action, and following through, and that bringing Infinitus agents into ChatGPT combines frontier AI with specialized healthcare capabilities while maintaining the safeguards healthcare demands. The plugins let teams bring more of their work into the same conversation, including reviewing patient records and hospital protocols, preparing prescriptions for clinician review, coordinating patient outreach, checking insurance eligibility, and analyzing healthcare costs and operational performance. The new plugins join ChatGPT's broader ecosystem of plugins supporting work across industries, from healthcare data and research to documents, presentations, and software development.

OpenAI said healthcare teams need to piece together information from the EHR, hospital policies, scheduling systems, and payer portals to deliver care and manage operations. With ChatGPT for Healthcare, OpenAI is bringing the tools teams already use and the medical evidence they need into one platform to help them spend less time navigating systems and more time caring for patients. In a demo, a clinician uses Voice in the ChatGPT app to ask for help following up on an MRI request, and the agent reviews the chart and drafts an order and patient reply for review. The articles give examples including a care coordinator using Luma Health to find tomorrow's appointments that still need confirmation and TriZetto to check insurance eligibility, and a primary care physician using Metriport to find a discharge summary and UpToDate to check follow-up monitoring. Other examples include an inpatient nurse using AIVA for a hospital's inpatient pump policy and Amion to find the covering endocrinologist, a care navigator using IMO Health, Stedi, and Turquoise Health to compare MRI sites, and a referral manager using Assort Health and Ferry Health for referral review.

ChatGPT for Healthcare customers have computer-use agents in ChatGPT Work and Codex and improved trusted clinical search available today, subject to workspace settings, and workspace administrators can enable new healthcare plugins. Individual clinicians have computer-use agents in ChatGPT Work and Codex and improved trusted clinical search available today, and select plugins are also available. ChatGPT for Clinicians is free for eligible, verified clinicians in the U.S. to review medical evidence and prepare clinical documentation, and both products offer customers a Business Associate Agreement with OpenAI to support HIPAA-compliant workflows. Computer-use agent capability is available in the OpenAI API, ChatGPT Work, and Codex, and customers can purchase ChatGPT for Healthcare directly or through an AWS Marketplace private offer by contacting the sales team. OpenAI said it is continuing to invest in the plugin ecosystem and inviting more healthcare companies to build with it.

stories.Headline: Hackers steal Uber drivers license data via Fireworks AI credentials
stories.Summary:
Uber is notifying drivers that hackers stole personal information, including driver's license details, after attackers used stolen internal credentials at AI inference vendor Fireworks AI to reach Uber data. The breach notices were filed with state attorneys general and reported by TechCrunch on November 13. A third-party service provider notified Uber on October 9 that hackers had stolen its internal credentials and used them to access Uber's account with the provider. On October 13, Uber determined that the hackers had accessed its data, including personal information belonging to drivers. Uber confirmed to Gizmodo that the compromised provider was Fireworks AI, a startup that helps developers access and use open AI models.

State filings count at least 7,870 people in three states, a floor that will rise because Uber has not disclosed a national total. Massachusetts counted 2,567 people notified, South Carolina's Department of Consumer Affairs listed 3,430 affected residents, and Rhode Island counted 1,873. Illinois residents were also affected but that count was pending, and California drivers were notified without a published figure. A notice dated November 10 was filed with California's attorney general. Uber is offering affected drivers free credit monitoring and fraud assistance through Cyberscout, and drivers have 90 days from the date of their notification letter to sign up.

Fireworks told Uber on October 9 that hackers had broken in and stolen internal credentials, which the attackers then used to reach Uber's data. An Uber spokesperson tied the notices to a security incident at third-party vendor Fireworks.ai. Fireworks confirmed to TechCrunch that it identified unauthorized access affecting customer data but did not answer specific questions about the incident. Fireworks links the intrusion to a financially motivated criminal group that sells tokens obtained through unauthorized access to AI models, and no known group has claimed the theft of Uber's data. Uber said it immediately cut off its data connections with Fireworks after learning of the breach.

Fireworks says more than 10,000 companies use it, with Uber among its customers. Fireworks says it identified the activity at 12 p.m. ET on October 6, and that the attacker captured environment variables, including API keys and tokens stored as secrets, in evaluation jobs for a limited number of customer accounts. It says it began notifying affected customers on October 7, told identified affected customers at 9 p.m. ET on October 9, and published its public bulletin at 1 a.m.

ET on October 10. That bulletin said Fireworks had not detected evidence of unauthorized access to personal information within its security perimeter or control, based on its investigation at that time. Fireworks says it detected no impact to Inference, its Training SDK or Nexus, all of which run with zero data retention by default. On October 23, a third-party cloud provider that hosted Fireworks research-and-development machines had its own security incident, and on October 24 an unauthorized party used that access to reach Fireworks development machines and run an unauthorized workload. Fireworks says the exposed data included resource metadata, billing information such as addresses, invoice and payment history, account balances and credit usage, and incomplete model weights and datasets for some customers, while payment card numbers were not stored and so were not affected.

As of October 25, it had found no further evidence of successful unauthorized access to the customer-facing platform, and it is working with Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42. Fireworks disabled self-serve dataset uploads and downloads for batch inference and dataset-based training while it investigates. Fireworks said it notified law enforcement and has been working with cybersecurity firm Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 to conduct forensic analysis. Fireworks told Notion on the evening of November 2 that a small dataset had been accessed by malicious actors, and Notion disconnected from Fireworks and deleted its data there the next morning. On November 6 Fireworks said potential customer data may have been accessed, and on November 8 it confirmed a new dataset.

That dataset included Notion AI chat transcripts from the Insights feature, tied to fewer than 1% of workspaces, and for most affected workspaces the transcripts cannot be tied to a user, workspace or company. Notion says this was not a breach of its own systems; it disabled Insights, stopped serving open-weight models through Fireworks, and told affected customers to rotate any credentials pasted into Notion AI. The Register, citing Bloomberg, reported that Fireworks is also working with customers including Cursor and Harvey to assess the impact. Uber's 2016 incident exposed names and license numbers of around 600,000 U.S. drivers, stored on a third-party cloud-based service.

State attorneys general alleged Uber failed to notify affected people promptly, and Uber agreed to a $148 million settlement with all 50 state attorneys general in 2018. The 2022 leak of employee data through the vendor Teqtivity, which affected more than 77,000 employees, was another vendor-origin incident. TechCrunch counts the current incident as Uber's second known breach this year, after an Uber Freight intrusion that an extortion gang claimed. In August, a hacking group claimed to have stolen nearly 1 million files from Uber Freight, the company's logistics subsidiary, and Uber Freight confirmed that attackers had gained unauthorized access.

stories.Headline: US stocks drop as investors sell AI shares before Nvidia earnings report
stories.Summary:
United States stock markets fell sharply on Monday, November 16, 2026, as investors sold off artificial intelligence shares. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 739.38 points, or 1.41 percent, while the S&P 500 fell 145.08 points, or 1.92 percent. The Nasdaq Composite Index experienced a larger decline of 626.52 points, which represents a 2.5 percent drop. This market volatility occurred just before Nvidia was scheduled to release its quarterly financial results.

The downturn affected nine of the eleven primary S&P 500 sectors, with technology and communication services falling 2.98 percent and 2.82 percent. Nvidia shares decreased by 4.12 percent following the recent resignation of chief executive officer Jensen Huang. Other chipmakers saw significant losses, as Intel, Micron, Marvell, and Arm each dropped more than 6 percent. Advanced Micro Devices fell 5.58 percent, Broadcom dropped 3.92 percent, and Dell Technologies and Oracle fell nearly 7 percent and 5 percent.

David Kelly, the chief global strategist at J.P. Morgan Asset Management, stated that there are many doubts regarding technology. He suggested that investors should diversify their holdings in artificial intelligence because the trade is entering a more volatile phase. Meanwhile, Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh noted that staff are modeling three different scenarios for how artificial intelligence might reshape the economy. These possibilities range from a productivity boom to rising unemployment or a disappointing payoff that lowers share prices.

The market is now awaiting the initial public offering of Anthropic, which is expected to price on Wednesday and trade on the Nasdaq on Thursday. Economic data showed the New York Federal Reserve's Empire State manufacturing index fell to 7.8 in November from 25.5 in October. Traders currently believe a quarter-point interest rate increase at the December meeting is nearly certain. Other news included a rise in Tyson Foods shares and a decline in West Texas Intermediate crude oil prices.

stories.Headline: Samsung and SK Hynix gain bargaining power as Nvidia faces leadership turmoil
stories.Summary:
Nvidia's board launched an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang on November 9, 2026, causing the company's shares to fall by 4.3 percent. This leadership vacuum has shaken the AI semiconductor supply chain while creating new opportunities for South Korean memory suppliers Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix. Anonymous employees launched a website called Stand With Jensen to petition for the return of the former chief executive officer. This petition gathered roughly 110,000 signatures, including 60,000 shareholders and 5,000 employees, to demand that Huang be reinstated and treated fairly. Silicon Valley figures like Elon Musk, Tim Sweeney, and Garry Tan also joined the signature drive to support the former leader.

The situation involves high-bandwidth memory, known as HBM, and requires a diversified customer base to increase the bargaining power of the memory suppliers. Samsung Electronics signed a priority HBM4 supply deal with AMD in March and partnered with Anthropic to manufacture its own AI chips. SK Hynix holds a near-monopoly on memory supply for Google's in-house Tensor Processing Unit chips, which Google has begun selling externally. Other companies deploying self-developed chips in data centers include Amazon with Trainium and Microsoft with the Maia 100 chip. US lawmakers are now pressing for tighter controls on AI chip exports to China following the allegations involving Jensen Huang.

Erwin Cummins, a senior research staff engineer at Nvidia, stated that Huang's leadership was the driving force that brought employees to the company. Lee Ji-hwan, CEO of Aurora Investment Advisory, said memory demand is not significantly affected whether Nvidia wobbles or rivals like AMD and Google replace it. Kim Young-gun of Mirae Asset Securities diagnosed that Samsung and SK Hynix can strengthen bargaining power through the diversification of their customers. Brad Gerstner and Gavin Baker said on X that facts must be verified and an investigation must determine if Huang serves shareholders. These experts believe that the shift from AI training to the inference phase will continue to underpin the demand for memory.

Dylan Patel, CEO of SemiAnalysis, said that Google and others might take significant market share because Huang is the only executive who can secure production. Major customers of Nvidia are reducing their dependence by developing application-specific integrated circuits, which is a trend that benefits the memory industry. Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix are affected by these shifts, as well as by the potential for tighter US export curbs to China. A fake letter impersonating Vice President Ian Buck and Chief Scientist Bill Dally circulated on X, demanding the resignation of the entire board. This fraudulent document was a modified version of the open letter from when OpenAI CEO Sam Altman was ousted in 2023.

The background shows that SK Hynix had about a quarter of its revenue coming from Nvidia during the previous year of business operations. The memory industry views the current reshuffle as an opportunity because more diversified chip design companies create a more stable demand base. The rise of competitors like AMD and Google is reshaping the supply chain as they target gaps in the market built by Nvidia. AI infrastructure investment is not expected to shrink, but the center of gravity is moving from the training phase to the inference phase. The trend of rising HBM content in advanced application-specific integrated circuits provides a tailwind for the South Korean memory companies.

Next, investors must watch trading volume and foreign flows to see if Samsung Electronics can enter a full-fledged uptrend in its share price. Market observers believe that the negotiating power of memory companies will rise further if the structure of diversified chip design takes hold. The industry must determine if the market can absorb the selling volume from investors who bought Samsung shares at past high prices. The articles leave open whether the independent investigation into Jensen Huang will result in his permanent removal or his eventual reinstatement. It remains uncertain how the push for tighter China chip curbs will specifically impact the future revenues of Samsung and SK Hynix.

stories.Headline: Deezer launches AI music filter in eight countries next month
stories.Summary:
The French music streaming platform Deezer will launch a new AI music filter next month. CEO Alexis Lanternier announced this feature to Reuters on Monday, November 17, 2026. The tool allows listeners to remove fully AI-generated songs from their search results. This decision follows a survey showing that 80 percent of users want clear labels. The filter will not apply to tracks created with some AI assistance.

The feature will be available before the end of 2026 for users in eight countries. These nations include the United States, Canada, Brazil, UK, France, Netherlands, Germany, and Japan. The tool detects models like Suno and Udio, using patents published in June 2026. Deezer already excludes AI tracks from recommendations, playlists, and charts since the beginning of 2025. The company now receives nearly 90,000 fully AI-generated tracks every single day.

CEO Alexis Lanternier stated that an overwhelming majority of listeners still want transparency regarding AI music. He noted a significant gap between what listeners think is in their playlists and reality. Lanternier believes listeners who enjoy AI songs form weaker connections with the artists behind them. He argued that AI music brings value to users and should still be remunerated. He wants to protect songwriters and minimize negative effects from generative AI.

An Ipsos survey of 9,000 adults found that 72 percent of users want AI recommendations labeled. Sixty percent of respondents believe fully AI-generated tracks should not be included in major charts. Sixty-nine percent of people believe that 100 percent AI-generated music threatens the livelihood of artists. Sixty-seven percent of people fear that AI could diminish creativity in music production. Many users in the United States showed growing concern about AI in music.

Deezer detected and tagged over 13.4 million AI tracks during the year 2025. Internal data from 53,000 new October subscribers showed 57 percent had AI tracks in libraries. This contradicts the 74 percent of users who believed their playlists were free of AI. In 2025, up to 85 percent of streams from AI tracks were found to be fraudulent. AI-generated music currently accounts for between 1 and 3 percent of total streams.

Deezer is now licensing its AI detection technology to the wider music industry to reduce fraud. The company will continue gathering intelligence through its annual barometer to improve the fan experience. A study suggests nearly 25 percent of creators' revenues are at risk by 2028. This risk could amount to as much as 4 billion euros by that time. The articles leave open how other streaming platforms will respond to these transparency measures.

stories.Headline: Hitachi validates agentic AI platform that cuts chiplet design candidates by over 90%
stories.Summary:
Hitachi's Research and Development Group announced on November 12, 2026, that it had completed and empirically validated a foundational design platform for semiconductor chiplet package design. The platform combines autonomous agentic AI with ultra-fast surrogate physics models to streamline advanced semiconductor packaging. The announcement followed preliminary technical disclosures presented by Hitachi researchers at the 35th IEEE Conference on Electrical Performance of Electronic Packaging and Systems, known as EPEPS 2026. That conference was held in Fort Worth, Texas, from October 18 to 21, 2026. In verification trials using a heterogeneous package with three distinct chiplet types, Hitachi demonstrated that its agentic AI pruned the candidate design space by more than 90%.

Engineers provide high-level targets, thermal design power limits, footprint boundaries and cost goals in natural language, and the agentic AI structures these prompts into formal design-for-manufacturing rules. The system integrates procurement constraints, bill-of-materials availability and vendor lead times to discard unviable component pairings early. The engine concurrently evaluates candidate layouts across electrical performance, thermal dynamics and mechanical stress using accelerated AI surrogate models. Electrical performance covers signal latency, return loss and power impedance, thermal dynamics covers hotspot dissipation and junction temperatures, and mechanical stress covers warpage and shear strain from thermal expansion coefficient mismatches. Hitachi also announced on the same day a technology that uses quantum-inspired CMOS annealing to create a supply-demand plan covering more than 500 generators up to 36 hours ahead in 60 minutes.

Hitachi's Research and Development Group is responsible for the platform, and the company positions it as a foundational technology within its Lumada 3.0 digital transformation framework under its One Hitachi initiative. Hitachi aims to provide edge AI semiconductor engineering services across mobility, energy and robotics. Hitachi plans to conduct Proof-of-Concept engagements with commercial chip vendors, fabless design firms and packaging OSAT providers through late 2026 and 2027. Research teams are also extending surrogate models to support higher die counts, emerging optical interconnects and standard specifications from the UCIe consortium. Both the chiplet technology and the annealing technology remain at the verification stage, and the company is moving toward practical application.

Writing for Mynavi TECH+ on November 13, 2026, technology writer Yukio Kobayashi emphasized that component volatility remains a critical obstacle in chiplet projects. Kobayashi noted that incorporating procurement availability into early automated screening directly targets a common source of project delays. Writing for EE Times Japan on November 16, 2026, semiconductor journalist Takatsuna Mamoto underscored the value of concurrent tri-physics analysis. Mamoto observed that optimizing trace latency often concentrates heat dissipation, generating coefficient-of-thermal-expansion mismatches that can crack solder microbumps. Japanese industry portal Dellows News noted on November 13, 2026, that the technology arrives as edge AI and automotive electronics shift rapidly toward modular silicon, and that for mid-sized semiconductor firms lacking large dedicated packaging teams, automated exploration tools help bridge substantial resource gaps.

Advanced semiconductor packaging has become the primary mechanism for computational scaling as monolithic silicon approaches photolithographic reticle limits and rising wafer defect costs. Disaggregating system-on-chip architectures into modular chiplets such as compute cores, high-bandwidth memory and analog I/O controllers enables process-node optimization for each die. Assembling multiple dies onto high-density substrates creates an explosive combinatorial search space in which engineers must evaluate thousands of spatial floorplans, inter-die bump patterns, routing layers and stackups. With leading-edge fabrication costs climbing at sub-3nm nodes, monolithic dies larger than 800 square millimeters face severe yield penalties. Industry consortia and commercial leaders including the Universal Chiplet Interconnect Express group have prioritized modular advanced packaging, while established commercial electronic design automation suites provide high accuracy for signoff verification but require hours or days of cluster compute time to evaluate a single package geometry.

Following validation on three-chiplet architectures, Hitachi is preparing broader industry rollouts. The articles leave open the results of the planned Proof-of-Concept engagements with commercial chip vendors, fabless design firms and packaging OSAT providers. The articles do not state when the platform will move beyond the verification stage to practical application. The articles do not give the outcome of efforts to extend surrogate models to higher die counts, emerging optical interconnects and UCIe standard specifications. The articles do not state the cost of the platform or when it will be commercially available.

stories.Headline: Claroc finds Grok Build exposes corporate data for thousands of users
stories.Summary:
Security firm Claroc discovered that Grok Build exposed sensitive corporate data through weak default security designs and poor data management. This vulnerability affected thousands of users including Fortune 500 companies and defense contractors. The breach occurred because the platform used randomized URLs that were easily collected by passive DNS services. SpaceXSI, the new name for xAI, operated the Grok Build agent that caused these leaks. The findings were reported by the technology publication Ars Technica on November 16, 2026.

The system used subdomains ending in grok.me, such as failing-chassis-traders, which granted access without a separate login. Claroc found 37,571 online subdomains, and 35,578 of these exposed data because the default setting was Anyone with the link. Exposed data included 24 SpaceXSI apps with a sales map of 594 companies and a confidential onboarding plan. A Peruvian construction company had medical records for 3,784 workers exposed, and Tesla leaked data on 22 mechanics. Other leaks included U.S. Navy contractor rosters, a U.S. IT services hardware bill of materials, and Norwegian-Finnish aerospace explosives dashboards.

Claroc notified SpaceX of these security gaps on November 8 but received no response from the company. Ars Technica reported that SpaceXSI removed links to 24 internal applications within hours of an email inquiry. Claroc stated that no separate access restrictions were implemented for applications created by other users of the platform. The security firm explained that hostnames in the URL structure allowed outsiders to discover applications in large numbers. They noted that the default sharing permission for published applications remained open unless users manually changed the settings.

Other vibe coding platforms like Lovable, Bolt, and Replit may also allow addresses to be discovered through passive DNS. Moltbook exposed 1.5 million authentication tokens and 35,000 email addresses by embedding a Supabase API key in JavaScript. Cal AI leaked 14.59GB of data, totaling 3.2 million user records, due to an unauthenticated Google Firebase backend. Red Access found 5,000 assets from Lovable, Base44, Replit, and Netlify that exposed medical, financial, and corporate strategy documents. Meta Muse also had 6,800 shared links exposed through passive DNS records before suspending the feature on October 20.

Vibe coding allows non-developers to generate business software using natural language, voice, or text prompts. This trend prioritizes speed and easy deployment over security safeguards, leading to public-by-default settings and weak access controls. Many users add customer information and internal documents to these apps without conducting any formal security reviews. A June report by the Cloud Security Alliance titled The Vibe Coding Governance Gap highlighted these systemic issues. The articles state that security is often treated as an optional feature rather than a fundamental requirement.

Platforms should make private access the default and improve URL structures to prevent discovery by passive DNS services. Companies must identify AI-created applications and require security reviews for those handling internal documents or customer information. Authentication mechanisms must stop relying solely on obscuring URLs to protect sensitive corporate and personal data. The articles leave open whether SpaceXSI will implement broader access restrictions for all third-party users of Grok Build. It remains unclear if other platforms mentioned by Claroc have already fixed their passive DNS vulnerabilities.

stories.Headline: Sharjah Digital Department launches Agentic AI Challenge to automate government operations
stories.Summary:
The Sharjah Digital Department launched the Sharjah Agentic AI Challenge to speed up the use of agentic artificial intelligence in government operations. This initiative follows the directives of HH Sheikh Sultan bin Mohammed bin Sultan Al Qasimi, the Crown Prince and Deputy Ruler of Sharjah. The event is scheduled to take place from December 8 to 10 to help automate various government services and operations. It is organized in partnership with Inception42, while Microsoft is participating as a collaborator for the duration of the challenge. The program aims to empower national talent to create innovative solutions that address real world challenges using new agentic AI technologies.

The challenge is open to the public and will include 30 participants who will work in teams of specialists and experts. These teams must develop prototypes of intelligent AI agents that can automate repetitive procedures and reduce the time for processing transactions. The program uses a design thinking approach and hands on learning under the guidance of trainers to create these practical solutions. It begins with an introductory session and three days of intensive work from 8 to 10 December in the city. The final prototypes will be presented to a specialized judging panel that will select the winning teams for the competition.

Sheikh Saud bin Sultan Al Qasimi, Director General of Sharjah Digital Department, said the Crown Prince set a clear strategic objective for them. He stated that the goal is to harness the potential of agentic AI in practical ways across various government institutions. He believes the true value of these technologies is their ability to streamline procedures and improve the quality of government services. He noted that the challenge is a practical step toward building sustainable government capabilities by combining operational experience with technical knowledge. He added that this will strengthen institutional integration and support the goals of the Sharjah Digital Transformation Strategy 2026 to 2028.

The project is designed to make a tangible difference to the lives of people by improving the overall customer experience. It affects national talent by providing them with the opportunity to develop solutions that enhance the efficiency of government operations. The initiative also aims to strengthen partnerships and integration between different entities to promote a sustainable digital transformation for the region. These efforts align with the human centred approach to digital integration that Sharjah has committed to for its citizens and residents. The challenge also supports the broader goals of the We the UAE 2031 Vision and the UAE National Strategy for AI.

The Sharjah Digital Transformation Strategy 2026 to 2028 aims to develop government services and improve the performance of various local institutions. This strategy provides the background for the current challenge to promote a sustainable digital transformation across the entire government sector. The UAE National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence 2031 also serves as a foundation for these technological advancements in the emirate. Additionally, the We the UAE 2031 Vision guides the strategic direction for integrating advanced technology into the national infrastructure and services. These frameworks emphasize the importance of strengthening digital capabilities to maintain a competitive and efficient government for the future.

The next step involves the introductory session followed by three days of intensive practical work for the thirty selected challenge participants. Teams will collaborate to turn specific challenges into practical solutions before presenting their final prototypes to the specialized judging panel. The panel will then evaluate the work to select the winning teams based on the quality of their AI agents. The articles do not state what rewards the winning teams will receive after the competition ends on December 10. stories.Headline: Ramaphosa leads South African delegation in Silicon Valley to study AI development and adoption
stories.Summary:
President Cyril Ramaphosa arrived in California in the United States of America on Saturday, 14 November 2026, for a working visit to Silicon Valley, where he is leading a high-level, multi-stakeholder South African delegation to gain insights into the global artificial intelligence ecosystem and to inform South Africa's approach to the development, adoption and application of AI. The delegation comprises representatives from government, academia, business, research institutions, technical experts and university students, which the Presidency says reflects the country's commitment to an inclusive, collaborative and multi-stakeholder approach to harnessing the opportunities presented by AI. The programme includes engagements with leading technology companies, investors, researchers, academics and AI experts, as well as technology demonstrations and knowledge exchanges, which provide an opportunity to explore developments in frontier AI, robotics, data infrastructure, cloud computing, digital innovation and the practical application of AI across various sectors. A key component of the visit is engagements with leading academic institutions, focusing on the implications of AI for technology, security, the economy, business and the labour market, as well as emerging developments in robotics and technological research.

The programme also features the South Africa AI Opportunity gathering, under the theme Building the African AI Economy: Infrastructure, Investment and Innovation, which brings together South African and international stakeholders to explore how South Africa can position itself as a competitive AI hub on the African continent. Discussions there focus on AI infrastructure, data centres, computing capacity, energy requirements, investment opportunities and the growth of a competitive start-up ecosystem, while other areas of engagement include the application of AI in government and industry, law enforcement and public safety, AI safety and security, governance, skills development and the future of work. The delegation also engages with technology and infrastructure companies to gain insights into emerging technologies, investment trends and developments shaping the global AI ecosystem, and these interactions seek to identify opportunities for investment, knowledge exchange, skills development and the strengthening of South Africa's technological capabilities. The Presidency says AI presents significant opportunities to improve productivity, strengthen public service delivery, stimulate economic growth and support the creation of new industries and employment opportunities, with potential applications in South Africa including health, education, criminal justice, public administration and public procurement.

The visit provides an opportunity to learn from countries and institutions at the forefront of AI development, understand the associated risks and challenges, and consider how South Africa can develop an enabling policy, regulatory and skills environment to support responsible AI adoption. It also promotes South Africa as an investment destination, showcases progress in economic reforms, including through Operation Vulindlela, and highlights opportunities for investment in the country's digital economy, research capacity and innovation ecosystem. South Africa seeks to harness the transformative potential of AI while safeguarding digital sovereignty, policy autonomy, data protection and responsible AI governance, ensuring that technological advancement contributes meaningfully to inclusive economic growth and development. The President is accompanied by the Ministers of Finance; International Relations and Cooperation; Science, Technology and Innovation; Trade, Industry and Competition; Communications and Digital Technologies; Electricity and Energy; Small Business Development; and the Presidency, as well as South Africa's Ambassador to the United States of America, and media enquiries are directed to Vincent Magwenya, Spokesperson to the President.

stories.Headline: Threat actors use AI agents to automate software exploit creation and execution without human intervention
stories.Summary:
Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant revealed that threat actors now use AI agents to carry out whole stages of live intrusions. These actors have automated the process of turning newly released software patches into working attacks without any human in the loop. This activity was observed during the past quarter, with some operations occurring at machine speed to scale attacks significantly. The researchers found that these autonomous frameworks can find and exploit simple vulnerabilities while changing tactics based on target responses. One specific operation used a multi-agent framework called exploit_agent to automate vulnerability discovery and exploitation for the first time.

The FBI issued a FLASH alert on November 13 warning that ARTEX was used since August 2026 against government and healthcare sectors. Other tools in use include CAIRN, CyberStrikeAI, PentAGI, HexStrike AI, ZeroHollow, and Agent Zero, alongside custom harnesses built by the threat actors. The exploit_agent framework targeted French websites in education, entertainment, and media by comparing web application code before and after patch announcements. Attackers also used the Jieyou phishing platform and targeted PaperCut NG/MF flaws in September, as well as PHP flaws CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. These tools allow low-skilled affiliates to customize phishing lures and interfaces using natural language commands through an integrated LLM chatbot.

Google researchers stated that the adoption of these frameworks represents a paradigm shift toward intrusions occurring at machine speed. They noted that while the underlying mechanics of intrusions remain the same, the speed and scale introduce a new challenge. The group explained that current frameworks trade stealth for velocity, leaving behind traffic and code traces that make them easier. They observed that threat actors use LLMs to rapidly weaponize patched n-day vulnerabilities by focusing on a finite set of materials. Researchers also found that influence operation actors have moved from testing LLMs to using them routinely for regional political campaigns.

Financially motivated actors and suspected China-nexus espionage outfits are experimenting with these tools, including one PRC-nexus group building its own framework. Victims of LLMjacking attacks saw cloud compute and LLM quotas stolen, with some fraudulent charges reaching one million dollars total. North Korean fake IT workers use LLMs to write resumes and sound authentic during interviews with various Western companies. A suspected cluster called MIDNIGHT NEPTUNE targeted cryptocurrency organizations in Europe and North America using AI-generated recruiter profiles with SynthID watermarks. These attackers used ClickFix lures and the SOMBERMEME backdoor, naming their GitHub Personal Access Tokens after Microsoft Copilot to blend in.

Vulnerability disclosures and exploits nearly doubled between January and August 2026, with zero-day exploits jumping to 22 in August alone. The 2025 average for zero-day exploits was only eight per month, showing a significant increase in the volume of attacks. Stolen LLM access is resold through underground storefronts called LLM Mixers, such as APIMart and JetNight, for between $0.10 and $25. These mixers sell frontier and jailbroken models per million tokens, while botnets generate millions of API calls in twenty-four hours. Influence campaigns in the Middle East and Europe used LLMs to copy local dialects and add intentional typos to avoid detection.

Next, researchers anticipate that increased sophistication in LLMs will lead to reduced human involvement and increased stealth in these automated operations. A contractor is currently building a platform to run 100,000 accounts through cloud phone farms to sell to foreign governments. These accounts undergo an automated aging period where LLMs simulate ordinary browsing before the accounts start pushing specific campaign messages. The articles leave open how defenders will counter the flood of non-functional, LLM-generated proofs of concept that appear after patches. It remains unclear how the security community will efficiently verify these hundreds of fake exploits without wasting critical time and resources.

stories.Headline: Huawei Horinger data center has 7 percent of the compute of SpaceX Colossus 2
stories.Summary:
Ben Cottier and Lynette Bye of Epoch AI analyzed Huawei's Horinger data center on November 12, 2026. They found the facility has roughly 7 percent of the compute of SpaceX's Colossus 2. The researchers used satellite imagery and public sources to reach this specific conclusion. They noted that Huawei is using China's abundant energy to build these large centers. The analysis suggests the facility will stay far behind Colossus 2 until at least 2028.

The Horinger campus in Inner Mongolia has three zones called West, South, and North. It has up to 286 megawatts of IT power capacity across four buildings. These buildings use Ascend 910C and 910B chips, totaling 105,000 and 8,000 units respectively. Colossus 2 is located in Tennessee and is the largest AI data center globally. The Horinger site is compared to the 1.8 million H100-equivalents expected for Colossus 2.

Epoch AI researchers estimated the compute by modeling the heat rejection of rooftop cooling equipment. They stated that the Horinger facility is likely one of the largest in China. The authors noted that US facilities extract 2.5 times more compute per unit of power. They explained that the 910C chip performs at around 0.76 of an H100 equivalent. They concluded that China's compute constraints are unlikely to ease in the next two years.

The report mentions that VNET Bayin Ulanqab and Huawei Wuhu might match Horinger's capacity. Users of these systems are affected by the gap in chip performance and efficiency. A commenter named Mira noted that cooling towers provide a physical audit of compute. Another person named Sam Quiring questioned if banned Nvidia chips were used at the site. These individuals highlighted the importance of performance per watt over simple megawatt capacity.

Huawei is China's biggest AI chip developer but faces strict US export controls on technology. The Horinger campus was built after villages were demolished to make way for the centers. The facility uses hypernode servers designed for large-model training and inference for various end users. Most of the chips used were sold by the end of March 2026. The researchers observed moving cooling fans and water vapor to confirm the buildings operate.

One building in the West zone should become operational by December 2026 to increase capacity. Three new buildings are planned, with one in the South zone expected by February 2028. This growth could increase the total AI compute of the campus by over 70 percent. The articles leave open whether the overall frontier of Chinese data centers will fall further. stories.Headline: A man surnamed Han admits using AI smart glasses to cheat on national accountant exams
stories.Summary:
A thirty four year old man surnamed Han admitted on Sunday that he cheated on national exams using generative artificial intelligence. He confessed on a YouTube channel that he used electronic devices to cheat during the first round of the tax accountant exam. Han also admitted to cheating on the second round of that exam and the first round of the certified public accountant exam. He turned himself in to the police after facing allegations that he used AI equipped smart glasses to commit fraud. This scandal has sent shockwaves throughout the nation and exposed a lack of safeguards against AI assisted misconduct in South Korea.

Han scored 397.5 out of 400 in the April first round exam, with perfect scores in three subjects and one missed finance question. Three months later, he scored 663 out of 800 in the second stage written examination and was named the overall top scorer. The Ministry of Finance and Economy moved to suspend his certification, while the Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency Public Crime Investigation Unit investigates. Policy Chief Ha Joon Kyung chaired a meeting on November 15, four days before the 2027 College Scholastic Ability Test. Two proctors were assigned to the classroom where Han took the test, but they did not detect his fraudulent behavior.

Prime Minister Han Seong sook called for comprehensive measures to protect the fairness and credibility of state examinations during a Monday meeting. She stated that those who worked hard to prepare for exams should not be disadvantaged by the cheating of other candidates. The Prime Minister added that such misconduct should not undermine public trust in competitive examinations and required measures before and after tests. Presidential chief of staff Lim Kwang hyun told reporters on Sunday that the government was working to find solutions for the crisis. A presidential official stated that the office is taking the matter very seriously because the college entrance exam takes place next week.

Kim Yong jae, the 2018 top scorer, said that earning a perfect score in even one subject is virtually impossible for candidates. He noted that candidates have only 80 minutes to answer 80 accounting questions, suggesting the top scorer was either a genius or cheater. The Financial Services Commission came under fire for failing to detect the cheating, while the public expressed growing concerns over exam integrity. Other national certification examinations were held before the tax accountant exam, raising questions about whether cheating occurred in those other tests. The scandal affects the credibility of state administered exams and the trust of students who prepare honestly for these competitive tests.

The articles state that the nation has focused too much on competing for AI leadership and too little on necessary institutional safeguards. There was a widespread belief that AI is inherently beneficial, creating a gap between technological ambition and the actual institutional preparedness. The editorial argues that after the fact responses are insufficient and that the nation is unprepared for the age of artificial intelligence. Proctors lacked the tools and technology needed to identify AI assisted cheating, making it impossible for them to notice the misconduct. The government has belatedly scrambled to introduce measures in response to the scandal as the college entrance exam approached on Thursday.

Officials are now discussing preemptive detection measures and advanced technologies capable of thwarting AI assisted misconduct before the nationwide college entrance exam. The Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education held a training session on November 11 regarding a smart glasses cheating prevention guide in Yongsan gu. The government is working to find solutions to ensure that no more AI assisted cheating occurs during the upcoming scholastic ability test. It remains questionable whether the nation is prepared to build the necessary infrastructure to detect such high tech fraud in the future. The articles leave open whether other national certification exams were compromised by similar AI tools before the confession of the man.

stories.Headline: Young South Koreans use AI to create fake funeral portraits as a prank
stories.Summary:
Young South Koreans are using generative artificial intelligence to create fake funeral portraits of themselves or their friends as a joke. This social media trend was reported on November 15, 2026, as a growing practice among the youth in Seoul. The prank involves posting these AI images on Instagram accompanied by memorial messages to trick people into thinking they died. Many of these posts are designed to look like genuine death announcements to confuse the people who see them. This trend has prompted various news reports to call for tighter regulation of the online platforms where they appear.

The posts feature black and white images styled as funeral portraits with phrases like Rest in peace or You will always be remembered. Some images include fabricated dates of death and dates of birth, along with white chrysanthemums and black ribbons for added realism. This specific practice has recently gained popularity among teenagers and people in their 20s as a prank among close friends. The images are shared on Instagram, which is the primary platform where this surge of AI generated content is occurring. These visual elements make the fake portraits very difficult to distinguish from real announcements of a person's passing.

Kim Si-deok is a professor in the department of funeral services at Eulji University who spoke to the South Korean media. He stated that younger generations are increasingly taking the significance of death and funeral traditions lightly through this specific social trend. The professor warned that this behavior trivialises death and urged online platforms to take steps to prevent such content from spreading. Meta, the parent company of Instagram, responded by saying it removes or restricts content that violates its community standards. The company told a local news outlet that it will continue working with outside organisations to maintain a safe environment.

Some people who are aware of the prank ask what food they should prepare for the fake memorial service in comments. Others are unaware that the posts are fake and offer sincere condolences, saying it is heartbreaking to see someone die young. Experts are affected by this trend and have called for stronger action from social media platforms to stop the practice. Meta noted that users can report manipulated images of private individuals, including minors, that are shared without their own consent. The company claims it promptly removes such content following a review to protect the users on its social platform.

The articles provide background on how generative AI is being used to create these deceptive images for social media entertainment. This trend is part of a broader context of AI use in South Korea, including fake chats and exam cheating. One mentioned case involved a man making over 100 prank calls to police to be sent to a jail. Another instance involved an actor named Lee Yi kyung whose lewd chats were created by an accuser using AI tools. These examples show a pattern of using artificial intelligence for deception or pranks within the South Korean society.

Meta will continue to review and remove manipulated images of private individuals that are reported by users on the Instagram platform. The company intends to keep working with relevant outside organisations to ensure that the social media environment remains safe. The articles leave open whether the calls for tighter regulation of online platforms will lead to new laws or rules. It is unclear if the trend among teenagers and people in their 20s will decrease after these expert warnings. The reports do not state if any specific legal actions will be taken against those posting the fake portraits.

stories.Headline: Claire Gordon and authors propose a role-based faculty development framework for the AI era
stories.Summary:
Claire Gordon and eight other authors wrote a commentary about faculty development in the age of artificial intelligence on November 17, 2026. Their work drew on a Teacher Panel at the International Conference on GenAI and Pedagogical Innovations held in Hong Kong. This specific panel took place on May 22, 2026, at The Hong Kong Polytechnic University with Julia Chen as the moderator. The authors argue that university faculty development must move beyond generic technology training toward a more ecosystemic and role-based approach. They suggest that education should be a collective effort involving academic staff, students, external partners, and various professional specialists.

The proposed framework identifies seven roles for teachers, including ethical steward, learning architect, and human-centred educator, among other professional and technical roles. It requires support for curriculum renewal, assessment redesign, and AI policy literacy to address immediate pressure points regarding widespread AI use. The authors mention the Hong Kong University Grants Committee funded the project titled Exemplary learning, teaching and assessment practices in UGC-funded institutions. They emphasize that these complex roles do not need to be performed by a single individual teacher within the university. The framework also stresses the need for evidence-informed AI governance and connecting campus learning with the authentic world beyond the university.

The authors stated that AI literacy is necessary but insufficient without human-centred, ethical, professional, and disciplinary dimensions for university teachers. They argued that universities must renew the campus as a site for futures literacy and experimentation to better prepare graduates. The authors believe that faculty development should be discipline-sensitive and future-oriented to effectively reshape higher education and graduate preparation. They noted that AI is already challenging established assumptions about ethics, curriculum, and the general work of university teachers. The commentary concludes that institutional capacity for forward-looking governance is essential for managing the transition into the AI era.

Shannon Kane from the University of Maryland noted that some students use AI poorly, producing lesson plans that are essentially useless. Justin Reich of MIT's Teaching Systems Lab stated that domain knowledge is the only way to judge if AI output is good. Jennifer Kidd from Old Dominion University believes teachers must understand how AI works and the different ways it can impact learning. A survey of 268 teacher educators by the EdWeek Research Center found that some faculty do not support AI preparation. Additionally, nearly one quarter of prospective teachers surveyed reported that they do not want preparation for using AI in their work.

The EdWeek Research Center conducted its national survey of teacher educators during August and September of 2026 to examine AI preparation. A 2023 report by the International Society for Transforming Education found that 56 percent of new teachers lack technology confidence. George Mason University in Fairfax, Virginia, has implemented classes taught by Jered Borup to examine AI benefits and drawbacks in instruction. The American Association of Colleges of Teacher Education released an AI framework earlier in 2026 to help prepare novice educators for work. These articles highlight a long-standing struggle in teacher preparation regarding the effective integration of technology into classroom instruction.

Future research is needed to determine if AI tools can improve student learning or assist in the development of new teachers. It remains unclear if K-12 school district leaders will prize AI skills, as some districts ban the tools while others embrace them. The articles leave open whether AI should be a primary part of teacher-prep programs or secondary to the science of instruction. There is ongoing debate regarding how much time should be spent on AI versus developing a teacher's authentic professional voice. The long-term impact of AI on the role of the campus as a site of experimentation remains a point for exploration.

stories.Headline: Validix unveils Atomic Claim Architecture to govern and verify generative AI content
stories.Summary:
Validix, a Swiss company advancing governed claims for enterprise AI, unveiled its Atomic Claim Architecture on Nov. 17, 2026, according to PR Newswire. The announcement was published by The Manila Times on November 17, 2026, at 10 a.m. Validix AG is based in Zug, Switzerland. The Atomic Claim Architecture is a new patent-pending invention that changes how organizations govern content produced by generative AI. It is a secure governance layer, independent of and complementary to large language models.

The architecture constrains what large language models can generate and verifies content before it is released. The model itself is not modified, so organizations can apply the architecture to AI tools they already use or plan to deploy in the future. The architecture breaks evidence into Atoms, which are small, verifiable units of truth, each traceable to its source. Every claim is built from these Atoms, so it can be traced to the evidence behind it. If AI-generated content cannot meet this standard, it is withheld or sent for human review.

Validix provides continuous monitoring of the evidence, and if the underlying source evidence changes, every affected claim is flagged and sent to a human reviewer. Upstream control, pre-release checks and continuous monitoring of evidence sources form what Validix calls a Governed Claims Infrastructure. Lluis Pallarès, co-founder of Validix, said every organization using AI to communicate is putting its name behind what the technology says. Pallarès said that responsibility cannot be delegated to a language model. Pallarès said the architecture turns evidence into enforceable boundaries for what AI is allowed to assert and makes release a separate, controlled decision without requiring changes to existing AI models.

Pallarès said Validix is designed to accelerate expert review, not replace it, and that reviewers see the evidence behind every claim and keep the final say. In the pharmaceutical sector alone, companies have incurred more than $66 billion in recorded regulatory penalties and settlements globally since 2010, according to Violation Tracker Global. United States False Claims Act settlements and judgments exceeded $6.8 billion last year, according to the DOJ. Validix's first application, built for teams that create, review and monitor content in life sciences, is already in live use at a pharmaceutical company following a pilot project. Marketing and sales teams can verify communications through the Validix platform to check that the information is supported by current evidence.

Validix plans to launch its commercial platform in early 2027 and is opening a limited number of pilot partnerships across regulated industries. A video explainer on how the Validix Atomic Claim Architecture works is available at validix.ch/how-validix-works. HellerWeather released an upgraded version of its AI-powered Content Creator, a browser-based tool that uses forecast and climate data to generate first drafts for vertical videos, webcasts, digital shorts, blog posts, newsletter articles and other formats. Tim Heller, a meteorologist and chief developer of the application, said there is never a quiet weather day thanks to Content Creator. HellerWeather said the new feature is part of its broader AI Tool, which launched earlier this year.

HellerWeather said the browser-based system saves most meteorologists three to five hours of preparation time per week. Heller said it does not take a creative genius to write that today will be partly cloudy with a high of 78. Heller said allowing AI to take care of some of the necessary yet time-consuming work allows meteorologists to focus on tracking severe weather and producing more engaging content. Heller said more content means more revenue. The company said users enter a location and the system applies background prompts built from Heller's 35 years of on-air experience.

Heller said meteorologists keep full editorial control before anything is produced, published or shared. Heller said zero prompting does not mean zero input and that there is always a human-in-the-loop. HellerWeather said the AI Tool also serves as a meteorological and climate research assistant, with access to traditional forecast models and newer AI weather models, including Google's WeatherNext. The company said proprietary forecast confidence rankings and in-app alert-day notifications help weather teams finalize forecasts. HellerWeather said the same data powers more than 20 first drafts that meteorologists can use on air, online and on social media.

The company said the generated content appears in English and can be rewritten in conversational American Spanish, a feature added last summer. HellerWeather said the system is built for browser-based use, strict data privacy and hallucination prevention. The company said it does not require or store proprietary client data. Heller said his goal in building the application is to help his colleagues and coaching clients work more efficiently and communicate more effectively. Heller said Content Creator and the HellerWeather AI Tool do not replace meteorologists but empower them.

stories.Headline: ESMO launches a peer-reviewed journal on AI in oncology led by Jakob Kather
stories.Summary:
The European Society for Medical Oncology announced the launch of ESMO Artificial Intelligence and Oncology, a new peer-reviewed journal focused on artificial intelligence across cancer research and clinical care. The formal announcement took place on 16 November 2026 in Lugano, Switzerland. It coincided directly with the opening of the second edition of the ESMO AI and Digital Oncology Congress. The journal is dedicated to publishing data science investigations and educational content on the transformation of oncology through artificial intelligence. The launch establishes a dedicated scientific outlet intended to examine how machine learning technologies are transforming oncology research, diagnostic workflows, and therapeutic care.

The journal will feature original research reports, authoritative reviews, editorials, perspectives, professional correspondence, and news updates. Its subject coverage spans pathology, molecular profiling, diagnostic imaging, clinical decision support algorithms, drug development pipelines, clinical healthcare workflows, regulatory frameworks, medical education, and health economics. Prof. Dr. med. Jakob Nikolas Kather, MSc, will lead the publication as its Editor-in-Chief. Kather currently serves as the Hopp Foundation Professor of Artificial Intelligence in Medicine and is the Founding Director of the Institute for Medical AI at Heidelberg University Hospital.

The journal operates through a continuous online publication schedule and an established peer-review process. The European Society for Medical Oncology said the publication will provide an authoritative platform dedicated to the evaluation, validation, and real-world implementation of artificial intelligence applications across cancer care. The journal aims to promote methodological rigour, transparency, and multidisciplinary collaboration among oncologists, data scientists, and computational researchers. Kather said artificial intelligence is becoming a core technology within modern oncology. He added that the society has an essential role in offering a trusted forum for disseminating research and evaluating the benefits and potential risks of clinical AI systems.

Kather outlined an editorial vision centred on clinically relevant research and prospective validation studies of artificial intelligence tools. Kather said the publication will regularly feature educational materials designed to support the wider oncology community in understanding, interpreting, and applying artificial intelligence technologies in daily practice. This dual focus is intended to give clinicians and researchers practical guidance to navigate automated diagnostic and decision-making systems effectively. The society represents more than 50,000 oncology professionals worldwide, working to secure optimal outcomes for cancer patients.

By delivering educational resources and clinical evidence directly to members and the broader global cancer community, the organization seeks to empower healthcare providers to deliver high-quality patient care. The journal seeks to ensure that algorithmic innovations are thoroughly assessed before integration into oncology practice. The introduction of the journal expands ESMO’s existing institutional activities in the field of artificial intelligence, which encompass policy work, scientific and educational initiatives, and the annual AI and Digital Oncology Congress. These collective efforts reflect the society’s stated commitment to supporting the responsible development and application of AI tools to benefit individuals affected by cancer.

The newly launched journal serves as an extension of this mission, offering continuous peer-reviewed research to guide the safe, effective integration of artificial intelligence into cancer medicine. ESMO shared the launch on LinkedIn. The articles give no bibliographic details for the original publication and no DOI. The journal aims to accelerate the dissemination of scientific evidence, practical guidance, and educational resources.

The articles do not state a publication date for the journal’s first issue or any subscription or access terms. They do not name the other editors or editorial board members. They give no figures on the journal’s size, funding, or expected output. They do not say how the journal will be indexed or where it will be published.

stories.Summary:
India's Meganet Technologies Global filed draft papers on Monday for an initial public offering to raise 7.4 billion rupees, or about $78.62 million, according to Reuters. The company is an AI infrastructure provider that makes servers for high-performance computing, data centers and AI workloads. The offering will include fresh shares worth up to 1.4 billion rupees, while existing shareholders will sell shares worth up to 6 billion rupees through an offer for sale. The company supplies hardware to customers including the data center provider Yotta Data Services and the brokerage Motilal Oswal Financial Services. It has also built sourcing partnerships with technology providers such as Nvidia and AMD.

The filing sets out how the offering is split between new money for the company and a sale by existing shareholders, with the larger portion coming from the offer for sale. The fresh issue of up to 1.4 billion rupees is the part that would bring new capital into Meganet, while the 6 billion rupee offer for sale involves shares sold by current holders. The articles do not name the selling shareholders or say how the proceeds of the fresh issue would be used. The IPO arrives amid a surge in Indian companies looking to capitalize on the global AI race in the public markets, as well as a string of data center investments in the country through the year. The articles do not say when the issue is expected to open or list.

The articles do not identify a chief executive or other company official and carry no statement from Meganet about the filing, so no one is quoted on the record. Responsibility for the offering rests with the company, which filed the draft papers, and with the existing shareholders who plan to sell part of their holdings through the offer for sale. The articles give no further detail on the terms, the timeline or the regulatory steps ahead. More to follow.

The United States and nine allied nations formed a coalition to protect critical technologies associated with artificial intelligence. This strategic partnership was established to secure the supply chains and infrastructure necessary for advanced computing. The group intends to create a protective barrier against the influence of China in the technology sector. These nations are working together to ensure that sensitive AI models remain secure from foreign adversaries. The coalition is operating under a new framework known as the Pax Silica initiative to manage national security.

This effort requires the implementation of strict export controls on high-end semiconductors and specialized AI hardware. The partners are coordinating their policies to prevent the leakage of intellectual property to rival states. They are focusing on the protection of critical infrastructure that supports the development of large-scale AI models. The governments of the ten participating countries are responsible for overseeing these new security measures.

Officials stated that the collaboration is essential to maintain a technological edge over global competitors. They believe that fragmented policies would allow adversaries to exploit gaps in the global supply chain. The leaders emphasized that collective action is the only way to safeguard the future of democratic technology. More to follow.

US officials launched a fresh regulatory probe into Alibaba Group Holding regarding its cloud AI chip access. Regulators are looking into the specific relationships between Alibaba cloud partners and the CEO of Nvidia. They are assessing if these links facilitated the unauthorized use of advanced AI technology.

Business customers using Alibaba cloud infrastructure are affected because the probe touches a core service. These merchants and enterprises rely on the technology capabilities linked to the broader retail platform. If regulators close off remote access, Alibaba may need to rework how AI workloads are provisioned. The company might have to adjust which customers it serves from specific data centers. This could lead to higher costs or lower performance for some of its services.

Alibaba runs a large commerce ecosystem and provides cloud infrastructure for enterprises in China and abroad. The company uses T Head for chip shipments and maintains a large AI spending narrative.
