stories.Headline: Fed governor Barr warns AI borrowing boom poses ten risks to financial stability
stories.Summary:
Fed Governor Michael Barr gave a long speech on November 16, 2026, regarding AI investment risks. He detailed ten big, complex, and opaque threats to financial stability. These risks stem from a borrowing boom, circular financing, and high equity prices. The Federal Reserve also warned about these stability aspects in its latest Financial Stability Report. This report was released on the Friday preceding the governor's speech.

On-balance-sheet debt for the seven largest AI firms may exceed 800 billion dollars by year end 2026. Off-balance-sheet liabilities, including lease commitments and energy contracts, are estimated to exceed 3 trillion dollars. Smaller firms have over 100 billion dollars in circular financing from hyperscalers and GPU producers. These arrangements involve equity investments used to rent or purchase compute from the investors. Some firms also use collateral guarantees for asset-based financings to support their credit.

Governor Barr stated that investment losses could lower output growth through direct drops in investment. He noted that a significant repricing of AI investments could be amplified by complex financing. Barr warned that rapid deleveraging and self-reinforcing fire sales could occur due to high risk appetite. He mentioned that counterparty exposures could rise during periods of equity market volatility. The governor also cautioned that AI trading models might autonomously develop collusive behavior.

Unsophisticated investors are affected because financial complexity makes it hard to know where risk resides. Lower-credit-quality firms are impacted as their cost of capital has risen significantly in recent months. Hedge funds are mentioned as having high leverage that could lead to rapid deleveraging. Large dealers are involved because they provide leverage via prime brokerage services. The broader economy could suffer if wealth losses lower consumer and business spending.

The current boom is compared to the telecom investment cycle of the late 1990s and early 2000s. This earlier period was characterized by a similar boom and bust cycle of investment. The articles mention dark fiber as an example of excess capacity that took years to become useful. Some theoretical research shows that Q-learning trading algorithms can learn to manipulate markets through spoofing. These algorithms can create and exploit bubbles, which then destabilize the markets.

Specialized chips may depreciate quickly as newer technologies overtake them, making current capacity useless. It remains unclear if electrical infrastructure like substations and grid connections will find other uses. The Federal Reserve will continue monitoring exposures to counterparties with large positions in AI. The articles leave open whether smaller firms can replace supplier funding with revenue from customers. It is also unknown if the current debt levels will surpass those of the telecom boom.

Articles.Title: Top 10 Risks of the AI Boom to Financial Stability, according to Fed Governor Barr

stories.headline_source: Top 10 Risks of the AI Boom to Financial Stability, according to Fed Governor Barr

stories.Headline: Taylor Lane lists eight Best Buy holiday gifts including Meta AI glasses and Nespresso makers
stories.Summary:
Taylor Lane of SheKnows published a gift guide on November 15, 2026 at 7:37am EST listing eight holiday gifts to shop at Best Buy. The guide covers tech brands including JBL, Nespresso, Meta, Oakley and Brother. SheKnows noted it may receive an affiliate commission from purchases made through links on its website. The article said Best Buy makes holiday shopping easier with a wide selection of gifts from recognizable tech brands. It said options at different price points let shoppers buy gifts without looking in a dozen different places.

The JBL Cinema Soundbar 570 costs $180 and has 3.1-channel audio, a dedicated center channel and a subwoofer, with HDMI ARC and Bluetooth. The JBL Charge 6 Portable Wireless Speaker costs $200 and offers up to 28 hours of playtime, a waterproof, dustproof and drop-proof design, and a built-in power bank. The Nespresso Vertuo Pop+ Coffee and Espresso Maker costs $99, down from $129, a 23% discount, and the bundle includes an Aeroccino3 milk frother. The Nespresso Vertuo Creatista costs $700 and features an automatic steam wand and customizable milk texture and temperature settings. The Ray-Ban Meta Wayfarer (Gen 2) glasses with Meta AI cost $409, and the Oakley Meta HSTN Glasses with Meta AI cost $449 with up to eight hours of battery life and a charging case adding up to 48 more hours.

The Brother MFC-L2820DW Wireless All-In-One Laser Printer costs $280 and prints up to 34 pages per minute with automatic two-sided printing, a 250-sheet paper tray and a 50-page automatic document feeder. The Brother HL-L2405W Wireless Laser Printer costs $140 and prints up to 30 pages per minute with a 250-sheet paper tray, dual-band Wi-Fi and mobile printing. Lane wrote that the Nespresso Vertuo Creatista is at the top of her wish list this holiday season for a laundry list of reasons. Lane is a contributing commerce writer at SheKnows covering beauty, style and lifestyle, with over eight years of media experience. She previously served as a beauty writer at The Zoe Report and a fashion assistant at Glamour, and her work has appeared in StyleCaster, The FlowSpace, WWD, Forbes Vetted, Teen Vogue and InStyle.

The article said reviewers praise the Oakley Meta HSTN glasses for their secure fit and durable build, though some find the frames a little heavy for extended wear. It said the Ray-Ban Meta Wayfarer combines Ray-Ban's classic frames with hands-free features to capture photos and videos, listen to music and take calls without reaching for a phone. It said the JBL Charge 6 is a gift for music lovers who want to take their favorite soundtracks anywhere. It said the Nespresso Vertuo Pop+ suits smaller kitchens and its one-touch brewing system makes espresso, a full-size cup of coffee and iced options. It said the Brother MFC-L2820DW helps home offices and workdays run more smoothly and handles printing, copying, scanning and faxing.

The article said the gifts suit people who love the latest gadgets, want to upgrade their home or want to simplify their daily routine. It said the JBL Cinema Soundbar 570 brings immersive sound to movie nights at home with crisp sound and deep bass and a simple setup. It said the Oakley glasses suit anyone who loves the outdoors, traveling or staying active, with open-ear speakers that do not block out the world around you. It said the Brother HL-L2405W is essential for printing school assignments, shipping labels or work documents. It said the Nespresso Vertuo Creatista lets you enjoy favorite drinks without leaving home.

The article described the Ray-Ban Meta Wayfarer as one of Ray-Ban's most iconic styles that just got a tech upgrade, with Meta AI to ask questions and get information on the go. It said the Oakley glasses pair Oakley's sporty signature frames with hands-free technology and voice commands to access Meta AI. It said the Nespresso Vertuo Creatista features Nespresso's powerful Vertuo brewing system. It said the JBL Charge 6 delivers powerful sound and rich bass for backyard get-togethers and weekend trips. It said the Brother HL-L2405W reduces refills with its 250-sheet paper tray.

The article did not say when any of the gifts would go on sale or how long the $99 price for the Nespresso Vertuo Pop+ would last. It did not give availability dates for the Ray-Ban Meta Wayfarer, the Oakley Meta HSTN or either Brother printer. stories.Headline: GTIG AI Threat Tracker: Agentic Threat Activity Crosses a Significant Threshold
stories.Summary:
The Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant reported a critical inflection point in adversarial AI on November 16, 2026. Threat actors are now deploying autonomous multi-agent frameworks to execute multi-stage intrusions at machine speed. These adversaries include cyber criminals, espionage groups, and those conducting information operations. They use generative AI to compress attack timelines and scale their operations. This shift moves beyond basic prompting to fully automated offensive workflows.

The report identifies open source frameworks called ARTEX, CAIRN, CyberStrikeAI, and PentAGI used for automated intrusions. CAIRN targeted the US aerospace sector, while PentAGI scanned Asian organizations from August to October 2026. CyberStrikeAI uses a Go-based backend API, and HexStrike AI integrates with the Model Context Protocol. Other tools mentioned include ZeroHollow for exploit development and Agent Zero for autonomous code execution. These systems automate the reverse engineering of patches to weaponize n-day vulnerabilities.

Google stated they are committed to developing AI boldly and responsibly through a multifaceted defense strategy. They use a Google AI Threat Defense architecture and BeyondZero for continuous monitoring and responding at machine speed. The company hardens models against misuse and proactively disrupts the projects and accounts of bad actors. Mandiant Consulting released a hardening guide and architectural defense framework to counter LLM-enabled tooling. Google Security Operations also deployed specialized rulepacks to detect the use of ARTEX.

Financially motivated actors affect enterprises by stealing LLM credentials and cloud resources through a process called LLMJacking. These criminals resell access to high-performance AI models using underground proxy services known as LLM Mixers. State-sponsored groups and commercial Influence-as-a-Service vendors affect the public by producing synthetic media and localized personas. Cyber espionage groups target supply chains by manipulating autonomous coding assistant configurations to drop backdoors. These activities create a new defensive challenge by exploiting known weaknesses at extreme speed.

The articles note that zero-day exploits averaged 8 per month in 2025 and rose to 11 in 2026. This number spiked to 22 in August 2026, while overall disclosures nearly doubled between January and August. Previous quarterly research had only documented nascent adversary interest in these agentic capabilities. LLMs now automate labor-intensive phases like differential patch examination and dynamic protocol fuzzing. This automation reduces the window between the disclosure of a patch and its weaponized exploitation.

Threat actors will likely continue using these frameworks in global campaigns due to a low barrier to entry. Future operations are expected to move further along the autonomous scale toward fully agentic intrusions. While current tools trade stealth for velocity, future versions will likely increase in sophistication and stealth. The articles leave open how defenders will manage the increase in fake LLM-generated exploits. It remains unclear how quickly the industry can close the shrinking patch window for organizations.

Articles.Title: GTIG AI Threat Tracker: Agentic Threat Activity Crosses a Significant Threshold

stories.Headline: Malcolm Myers finds ten AI-exposed companies lose $206 billion in market value since 2021
stories.Summary:
Ten publicly listed companies operating in sectors exposed to artificial intelligence have collectively lost $206 billion in market value since the end of 2021, according to an analysis by Malcolm Myers, who works with marketplace and services platform businesses at EIV. The erosion in market value initially came despite relatively resilient revenue growth, as nine of the 10 companies recorded higher revenues between 2021 and 2025. Their combined revenue increased 47% from $22.2 billion to $32.7 billion over that period, even as investors questioned whether these businesses could withstand AI disruption. The disruption is now becoming visible in their financial performance, with revenue in the third quarter of 2026 declining 23% at Tripadvisor's hotels business, 25% at Fiverr's marketplace, 33% at Shutterstock and 40% at Chegg. The decline in valuations has been particularly pronounced across four segments that Myers noted in his analysis.

In price comparison and travel search, Tripadvisor has lost 77% of its market value since 2021, while LendingTree and TripAdvisor have declined 68% and 67% respectively, as these businesses largely depend on search traffic and referral fees. Booking.com, which facilitates the actual transaction, has gained 20% in contrast to those search-dependent platforms. Shutterstock has lost 97% of its value, while Wix and Adobe have declined 68% and 66% respectively, as AI increasingly enables users to generate content and applications on demand. Freelance marketplaces have faced similar challenges, with Fiverr losing 93% of its value and Upwork falling 72%, as businesses and consumers increasingly use AI to produce digital work they previously outsourced to freelancers. Chegg has lost 98% of its market value as large language models increasingly provide homework answers and educational assistance free of charge, Myers said.

Myers believes not all marketplaces face the same degree of risk, because platforms that aggregate unique supply, facilitate payments and manage fulfillment could prove more resilient as AI agents work alongside these businesses rather than replace them. He also sees an emerging opportunity in AI-native businesses that deliver completed outcomes instead of simply connecting customers with service providers or offering software to complete tasks. Examples include Corgi, which underwrites and issues insurance policies, Lawhive, which provides legal services through an AI-enabled law firm, and Mercor, which organises specialist work to deliver training data and evaluations. Mercor recently completed a $750 million Series D funding round at a $20 billion valuation, less than four years after its launch, and Myers believes the shift towards delivering completed outcomes could create some of the most valuable marketplaces and services businesses over the next decade.

stories.Headline: Bill Gross uses AI to generate business ideas to combat wealth inequality and national debt
stories.Summary:
Bill Gross shared his vision for AI entrepreneurship on November 17, 2026. He spoke during day three of the Web Summit 2026 conference. This event took place at the MEO Arena in Lisbon, Portugal. Gross is the Co-founder and Chairman of the tech incubator Idealab. He wants to use AI to help people start companies.

Idealab Studio is based in Pasadena, California, and offers 1.2 million AI-generated business ideas. Gross aims to create 100 million jobs to counter AI job losses. He believes the United States could support 30 million one-person companies. This goal mirrors the current number of one-person companies found in China. These free ideas come from analyzing thousands of news articles about consumer problems.

Gross said that a boom in entrepreneurship could offset the growing national debt. He believes that 30 million small, profitable companies would improve income equality. Gross described AI as a leveling tool that could democratize wealth distribution. He stated that this platform is likely his last company because of its impact. He intends to focus on this project for the rest of his life.

Fed data shows the top 1 percent of households own over 50 percent of the stock market. The top 0.01 percent own over 16 trillion dollars of 64.4 trillion dollars in assets. Census Bureau data shows business starts peaked at over 550,000 a month earlier this year. In October, a little over half a million new businesses were created. More than six in 10 Americans want to run their own companies.

Gross founded Idealab in 1996, which has seen 45 IPOs and acquisitions. He also founded the education software provider known as Knowledge Adventure. He made his personal fortune by building software before launching the AI platform. The platform uses AI to identify niche tech products and local issues like potholes. Users can take the free ideas and shift them for different markets.

Recent site data shows 130,000 visitors, with 28 percent coming from the United States. Other visitors came from Saudi Arabia, India, and Russia, with 80 percent being men. Between 50 and 60 percent of visitors are employed, while 8 to 15 percent are students. Gross hopes that people using the same ideas in different countries will eventually collaborate. The articles do not state when the 100 million job goal will be met.

stories.Headline: Minnesota doctors and lawmakers say AI healthcare oversight lags behind the technology
stories.Summary:
Artificial intelligence is already shaping care in Minnesota, but doctors and lawmakers say oversight is not keeping pace with how quickly the technology is changing. At Fairview, AI helps predict where ambulances may be needed, gives families real-time updates and creates electronic medical notes from doctor and patient conversations. The health system also uses AI to check the quality of MRIs before patients leave, according to KSTP. Dr. Sameer Badlani, Fairview’s chief digital and AI officer, said the tools let people get picked up sooner and dropped off sooner, with better use of the fleet and crew.

Badlani said AI is definitely evolving faster than regulations are, and Minnesota currently has no blanket law requiring healthcare providers to disclose every time AI is used. Rep. Peggy Scott, a Republican from Andover, said she wants stronger protections for Minnesota patients and has already tried to put guardrails around AI in healthcare. Asked whether there should be disclosure any time AI is being used, Scott said 100%. The Minnesota Medical Association said bias is one of the main concerns with AI in healthcare, and a task force led by Dr. Rebecca Thomas studied the issue for more than a year.

That task force determined there is an urgent need for more oversight of AI in healthcare. Thomas said the question of who would be responsible if artificial intelligence makes a harmful mistake is not straightforward right now. Fairview said patient recordings from the note-taking tool never leave its secure network, have restricted access and are deleted within a few weeks after they are converted into medical records. Fairview said it already notifies patients about AI and plans to add a notice to its online patient portal so patients can opt out of the note-taking tool.

Articles.Title: AI already plays key role in healthcare. It’s also evolving faster than Minnesota laws.

stories.Headline: Genpact launches Onyx platform for building and governing enterprise AI agents
stories.Summary:
Genpact announced on November 16, 2026 the availability of Genpact Onyx, an Agentic Operations platform for building, running, and governing AI agents in enterprise operations, and the company had unveiled the platform at its Agentic Operations Day in New York on November 12. The platform is powered by Genpact's Process Intelligence Core, which the company describes as operating knowledge codified from decades of running mission-critical work for global enterprises, so that agents start with context on how the work gets done rather than learning it from scratch. Genpact Onyx is the foundation for Genpact's proprietary agentic solutions, starting with the Genpact Accounts Payable Suite, and for custom solutions Genpact builds for clients. The platform embeds into a client's existing technology stack, connects to the client's data and AI foundations, and supports a choice of leading AI models across Genpact's partner ecosystem.

The platform's capabilities include a Process Intelligence Core codified across finance, risk, supply chain, banking, insurance, and procurement, with prebuilt workflows and agents so clients are ready on day one, drawn from doing the actual work and capturing edge cases, exceptions, and human decisions. A learning loop feeds reviewed exceptions and expert decisions back into the core so intelligence compounds over time, and earned autonomy lets agents start by proposing actions for a human expert to approve and take on more of the decision as they prove themselves. Built-in governance makes every agent action controlled, auditable, and traceable to the reason behind the decision, with guardrails and a responsible AI framework built into the platform, along with security and data isolation that meet enterprise standards. Genpact said the platform was launched at its third annual flagship event, held at Spring Studios in New York, where hundreds of clients, partners, and industry analysts attended a program of announcements, product demonstrations, and client presentations, and leaders from Advantage Solutions, Wesco, USA Today, and Ryan Specialty shared how they are putting Genpact's agentic solutions to work.

Balkrishan "BK" Kalra, President and Chief Executive Officer of Genpact, said the company runs mission-critical operations for many of the world's largest enterprises and that is where the return on AI is decided, adding that Genpact Onyx codifies three decades of process intelligence and makes it the foundation for Agentic Operations, with agents running the work and Genpact's experts owning the outcome. Priya Vijayarajendran, Chief Product and Platform Officer, said enterprises get value from AI when they turn operating knowledge into trusted execution rather than simply by adding more agents, and that Genpact Onyx grounds agents in how the work actually gets done, builds governance into every step, orchestrates across agents and human expertise, and lets autonomy be earned one decision at a time. Genpact describes Agentic Operations as a new operating model in which AI agents handle the volume of execution and its domain experts bring judgment and accountability, combining process intelligence, data and AI, a combined human and agent workforce, a partner ecosystem, and governance and security. Genpact said it uses the platform for its own agentic solutions, for custom client solutions in areas where it does not yet have an agentic solution, and for solutions delivered with technology partners.

stories.Headline: Geetanshu Gulati and Tim Han urge readers to practice preemptive skepticism online
stories.Summary:
The Daily Trojan published an opinion article titled "Everyone should practice a post-AI mindset" on Nov. 17, 2026, written by Geetanshu Gulati and Tim Han. The article argues that readers should employ "preemptive skepticism" as they search for humanity and truth online. It says our generation is living through a technological revolution, and that millennials and Gen Z are often called digital natives or digital pioneers. It states that millennials and Gen Z are the most digitally literate generations, and that everything is done with smartphones nowadays. It gives ordering morning coffee and logging into Netflix or a bank account as examples of smartphone tasks.

The article says the digital world's most daunting thing is its lack of physicality or security, and that there is no such thing as concrete or absolute certification. It says everyone uses the internet and anyone can input information and modify it however they want. It says real information can be modified to mislead audiences, and fake information can be appealing enough to bring out real emotions. It says that with the rise of artificial intelligence-generated content on everyday media platforms, this is easier than ever.

The article quotes Jelani Williams, a master's student studying digital social media, saying he has definitely seen a video he thought was AI. It quotes him saying there are a lot of times he is just skeptical immediately, more so than anything, and asking whether something actually happened. It describes the liar's dividend as a phenomenon in which realistic AI and advanced technology allow public figures to falsely claim that authentic, damaging evidence against them is manipulated. It says the public figure then usually shifts the burden of proof to others, demanding even more concrete evidence despite having just stubbornly rejected the initial facts. It says the internet is permanently changing in ways one can't easily imagine, prompting us to keep engaging, stay up to date and leave marks.

The article says people start acting overly intelligent, which makes the internet dangerous, and that one could easily fabricate false information to denounce another. It says the one attacked could also easily accuse them of falsehood without verification, just because it criticized them. It says that in a world where fake can be mistaken for real and real for fake, simple claims and first impressions do not shift the entire burden of proof onto those presenting them. It says we should evaluate sources, corroborate evidence and demand support for claims of manipulation. It quotes Jelani saying a claim would just have to be backed up really well, and that people have to be taught how to interpret things properly so they understand it is not real.

The article says guardrails are starting to be set up for AI transparency, and that the California AI Transparency Act requires generative AI providers to embed machine-readable disclosures in generated content and provide free diagnostic tools. It says Article 50 of the European Union's AI Act ensures AI systems are developed so users know if they are interacting with an AI system. It says Coalition for Content Provenance and Authority credentials set standards and function as digital labels showing their origin of creation. It says these laws and standards try to keep online content credible and transparent, yet their effectiveness depends on whether companies, platforms and creators follow through. It says these can only be social contracts that lose their meaning if not followed, and that even with penalties in place they are nothing more than retaliatory actions after the consequence that cannot guarantee prevention.

The article says one should practice "preemptive skepticism" for every single piece of content encountered, pausing to check where content comes from and what other evidence supports it before deciding whether to trust or dismiss it. It says one must recognize the liar's dividend of public figures and demand more of their denials. It says skills in actively searching for and verifying the origins of content are a necessary, if not vital, skill for an individual in the post-AI age. It says we are too passive in understanding the changes these technologies bring to our lives, and that not a lot of us get to the nitty-gritty of how they shape behavior and what responsibilities come with using them. It says we often approach new technology as consumers prioritizing convenience, and few of us try to bear the responsibility of deciding what uses are ethical and what limits one should set.

More to follow.

stories.Headline: Marc Andreessen predicts AI job losses will be limited in regulated sectors but growth will suffer
stories.Summary:
Venture capitalist Marc Andreessen, who co-heads Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh's task force on jobs and productivity, said on Monday, November 16, 2026, that artificial intelligence will have a dual effect on the job market. He predicted that job losses in sectors covered by government regulation will be largely insulated from major losses, but that those same regulations will limit economic and productivity growth. You might read that as good news, he said, because a revolution will not destroy all the jobs or kill everybody. You could also view it as very negative, he added, because productivity growth and economic growth simply may not grow very much.

Andreessen divides the economy into two categories of sectors, the first being fast-moving ones that see rapid technological and economic change along with rapid job turnover, such as consumer electronics and media entertainment. The second category is a combination of law and government, which is not structured to change rapidly and is typically characterized by extensive subsidization. He said the fastest-growing sectors will see their prices go down, while the slower-growing regulated or government-subsidized sectors will see their prices go up. Your iPhone is getting cheaper and the flat-screen TV on your wall is getting cheaper, he said, but college education is going to cost a million bucks, healthcare is becoming unaffordable, and good luck buying a house.

Andreessen is responsible for the prediction as co-head of the task force on jobs and productivity under Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh, and he set out the two-sector view himself in the remarks reported by Jennifer Schonberger of Yahoo Finance. The article gives no further comment from Warsh or from other members of the task force on the prediction. The report places the remarks against a backdrop of other warnings about AI and work, including Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's warning of 5% to 10% GDP growth with 10% joblessness, a combination he said is not one we have almost ever seen before. The article does not say what the task force will do next or when it will report.

stories.Summary:
A California federal judge denied SpaceXAI's request to separate itself from a proposed class action on November 16, 2026, according to a Law360 report by Aneeta Mathur-Ashton. The suit was brought by artificial intelligence users who accuse the leading AI platforms of violating antitrust law through their collaboration. The order keeps SpaceXAI, which the report identifies as Space Exploration Technologies Corp., inside the case rather than letting it proceed on its own. The judge issued the ruling in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California, where the case is pending.

The case information section lists the parties as Anthropic PBC, Google LLC, OpenAI OpCo LLC and Space Exploration Technologies Corp., with the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California named as the court. The law firms listed in the case information are Dechert LLP, Freshfields, Keker Van Nest & Peters and Willenken LLP. The articles do not state the size of the proposed class or any damages figure.

The judge is responsible for the ruling, and the articles do not name the judge or give any statement from the court. The articles also carry no comment from SpaceXAI, from the other companies named or from the plaintiffs' lawyers. The only description of the dispute is that AI users accuse the leading platforms of violating antitrust law through their collaboration. The articles do not say what the plaintiffs want the court to order or how the companies responded to the claims.

The context is a proposed class action in California federal court against several major AI platforms, and the ruling means SpaceXAI stays a party as the case moves forward. stories.Headline: FAA and ASI say the SMART AI system did not cause the ground stop
stories.Summary:
The airline ground stop that disrupted travel since Friday was not related to the FAA's new $875 million AI-powered system, according to government officials and the artificial intelligence company behind the technology. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said Friday there was no indication the communications issues that caused the ground stop were linked to the new computer system. The top officials at the Transportation Department and FAA reiterated that Saturday. The startup that designed the system, Air Space Intelligence, or ASI, said the ground stop was not caused by the SMART system, any product of ASI or its integration with FAA and ATC. The timing of the ground stop, so close to the national rollout of the Federal Aviation Administration's SMART system, raised questions about what the system does, its benefits and risks compared with the existing human system and what guardrails exist.

The SMART system is based in a single location near Washington where a team of experts analyzes flight schedules, weather forecasts and hundreds of other streams of data. That office sends recommendations to the FAA's command center, which relays them to air traffic controllers across the country for consideration. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford unveiled the system in September, calling it a cutting-edge tool that centralizes 200 data streams including weather patterns, flight paths, traffic flow and controller staffing metrics into one platform. SMART stands for Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes and Trajectories. The FAA says that during the initial test of the system in the Washington area this fall, it helped reroute 180 flights and saved an average of 10 minutes and 80 gallons of fuel per flight by diverting around weather or other issues.

The agency said one flight cut 42 minutes off its trip from Tampa, Florida, to Dallas thanks to the system's recommendations. SMART was expanded for use nationwide on Nov. 10 for the airspace of all 22 air traffic control centers, three days before the ground stop. According to a government fact sheet, SMART can predict where air traffic is headed and identify other routes before an area becomes too congested. The system can also help reopen restricted airspace faster and better manage airport arrivals. Currently, the FAA blocks off portions of airspace affected by weather as large, rectangular boxes, according to the fact sheet, which does not reflect how weather actually looks, with quick-moving thunderstorms and storm systems that are often irregular in shape, with narrow gaps or corridors that aircraft could safely fly through.

SMART gives the FAA and airspace operators a clearer picture of how weather will affect air traffic over time, allowing air traffic controllers to plan around storms and use available airspace instead of unnecessarily shutting down large areas. No other country has a working AI air traffic tool like the SMART system, according to Michael McCormick, a former FAA airspace manager and an associate professor at Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University. Eurocontrol, the European air traffic authority, has a system in testing and several manufacturers are prototyping similar tools. Last month, House Democrats sent a letter to the U.S. Government Accountability Office requesting an audit of the new software, raising concerns about safety and guardrails. The Oct. 13 letter said the nation's front line aviation safety workforce apparently had little to no input into SMART's development and had received limited training and information during the current deployment process.

The letter said the use of artificial intelligence within SMART has rightfully raised serious questions about its reliability and safety benefits, particularly on its potential to interfere with decision-making by experienced air traffic controllers or to hallucinate safety-critical information. SMART, however, is not, at least not yet, set up for AI to be in charge of flight control, and it makes recommendations to humans who do so. Mike O'Donnell, a former top FAA official who worked for the agency for 17 years and now does aviation safety consulting work, said the agency has got to make sure that this is just a tool in the toolbox and not the actual machine that's doing the work. O'Donnell said the FAA cannot afford to be wrong on this. He said there has got to be a way to verify and validate what the system is doing to make sure that it is not the wrong information.

O'Donnell cautioned against putting too much trust in AI until we know for sure that it has proven itself time and time again, and that is going to take a while. The AI system's launch comes amid a longstanding shortage of air traffic controllers around the country. The National Air Traffic Controllers Association has been raising concerns about this for more than a decade, telling Congress in 2015 that the shortage was at a crisis level. It said then that the FAA had missed its hiring targets for five years in a row. The union represents about 14,000 controllers, roughly 3,000 of them trainees. In an October interview with NPR, ASI co-founder and CEO Phillip Buckendorf said the SMART tool is designed for traffic managers who manage the entire U.S. airspace, and that the AI does the math and the computation, but it is ultimately up to the human operator whether to take the system's recommendation.

stories.Headline: Estee Lauder uses AI to develop new perfumes at its Paris innovation center
stories.Summary:
Artificial intelligence is increasingly being used to develop new perfumes, according to industry specialists, with a noticeable dose of AI emerging in new perfumes alongside hints of bergamot in the top notes and sweet iris as a follow-up. The US cosmetics giant Estee Lauder opened a perfume innovation center in Paris in 2025 that uses AI to mix savoir faire and cutting edge technology. The center helps Estee Lauder's billion dollars brands, which include Jo Malone of London, Kilian Paris, Le Labo and Tom Ford Beauty, according to Lucas Nanini, the group's vice president for fragrance innovation. Nanini tests some of the new formulas uncovered on visitors to the Maison des Parfums. The traditional world of perfumes has not been able to turn up its nose to new technology and algorithms, even though the industry insists that human sensorial expertise can never be fully replaced.

Nanini told AFP that AI will allow the company to work on what it calls "paradoxes," such as how to create an oil that is rich yet fine enough to be diffused. AI helps perfumers identify oils with properties that would take them years to develop by manual trial and error. Machine intelligence also helps with regulatory tasks, and Nanini highlighted the time it takes to check whether different countries allow each ingredient in a perfume. With a single click he can now verify whether an ingredient from the one thousand-plus used is legal in a specific country as well as the maximum concentration allowed. AI can also be used to find molecules to substitute for certain animal-derived ingredients, such as civet, taken from the glands of African civet and other cats in the species, which was traditionally used to give perfume a musky tone but has been phased out in the face of animal rights protests.

International Flavors and Fragrances, another major US player, estimates that AI cuts between 25 and 30 percent of the time needed to develop and make a perfume. IFF has developed its own AI tools using decades of internally collected data, and one suggests ingredients that complement each other and is used by IFF perfumer Tanguy Guesnet. Guesnet said every perfumer is searching for that "accord," that combination that will spark the emotion of tomorrow. The tool looks at the molecules in a single ingredient and suggests others with similar characteristics, so that mint essence, for example, which contains menthone, leads the tool to propose other ingredients that also include the compound. Guesnet said some pairings might seem obvious while others might appear a bit outlandish, but that is precisely the richness of the tool, which stimulates creativity and produces highly original combinations.

Not everyone is convinced by the AI revolution, however, and Guillaume Teule, co-founder of the French fragrance house Helius, insisted that he remains in control of how a scent develops and maintains his own vision. Teule said that much like in music, resonances and dissonances emerge when you start altering ingredients, and it is precisely these dissonances that are interesting and which only a human being knows how to leverage effectively. He said he does not believe any AI would have suggested "Angel," Thierry Mugler's so-called gourmand fragrance launched in 1992 and considered revolutionary because of its sweet notes. Teule commented that it was like a stone thrown into a pond when it was first released. With niche perfumes taking a bigger share of a growing market, enterprises like Givaudan of Switzerland and Robertet of France have heavily invested in tools to help them find new molecules.

The articles state that artificial intelligence is increasingly being used to develop new perfumes, according to industry specialists. They state that there may be a hint of bergamot in the top notes and sweet iris as a follow-up, but there is a noticeable dose of AI emerging in new perfumes. They state that the traditional world of perfumes has not been able to turn up its nose to new technology and algorithms, even though the industry insists that human sensorial expertise can never be fully replaced. They state that Estee Lauder opened its Paris perfume innovation center in 2025, and that Nanini tests new formulas on visitors to the Maison des Parfums. They state that IFF estimates AI cuts between 25 and 30 percent of development time, and that Givaudan of Switzerland and Robertet of France have heavily invested in tools to find new molecules.

The articles do not state what happens next beyond the continued use of AI in perfume development and the investments already made by Givaudan and Robertet. They leave open which specific new perfumes the Estee Lauder center has produced or will produce. They leave open how the regulatory checks Nanini described will be applied across the one thousand-plus ingredients in each country. They leave open whether Teule's view that only a human being can leverage dissonances effectively will be tested by future AI suggestions. They leave open how the substitution of molecules for animal-derived ingredients such as civet will proceed.

stories.Headline: UCIe Consortium releases 4.0 specification to integrate memory and improve chiplet system efficiency
stories.Summary:
The UCIe Consortium released version 4.0 of its chiplet interconnect specification on November 12, 2026. This new standard extends the role of the organization from connecting individual dies to coordinating complete systems. The update introduces standardized memory connectivity and improved power efficiency for multi-chiplet systems. It also adds new features for chiplet security and reliability in automotive applications. These changes address critical constraints regarding bandwidth, power, security, and reliability.

The UCIe.mem protocol provides approximately 2.5 TB/s of bandwidth per millimeter of die edge and 93.75% data efficiency. An optional power profile reduces link consumption by 30% to 80% at 64 GT/s under specific conditions. An enhanced bump map increases shoreline bandwidth density by 20% and area density by 10% at 48 and 64 GT/s. The specification includes Trusted Reporting of Chiplet State and bidirectional integrity-protected management channels for security. Automotive systems receive optional link-health monitoring and error notifications.

Debendra Das Sharma of Intel chairs the consortium and Samsung Vice President Cheolmin Park serves as the president. Sharma noted that available die-edge space, known as shoreline, is a major constraint in advanced multi-die processors. The organization collects membership dues and develops specifications to support interoperability among its members. It does not sell processors or report any product revenue, unit shipments, or average selling prices. Its commercial influence depends on semiconductor companies incorporating these specifications into shipping products.

Arif Khan of Cadence expects designers to combine these standardized interfaces with specialized fabrics at different system levels. Ashish Darbari of Axiomise identified verification across protocol boundaries as a continuing engineering challenge for the industry. Honda R&D and Mirise Technologies expressed support for the new automotive reliability additions. AI accelerator designers are affected because they can now scale memory capacity independently of compute silicon. ISVs and CIOs must monitor how these configurations affect model capacity and product availability.

The consortium began in March 2022 with founding companies Intel, AMD, Arm, ASE, Google Cloud, Meta, Microsoft, Qualcomm, Samsung, and TSMC. It incorporated in August 2022 and added Alibaba and Nvidia to its board, eventually exceeding 150 member companies. Intel and Synopsys demonstrated the Pike Creek cross-foundry test chip in 2023 to show progress. GUC announced a UCIe PHY implementation on TSMC N3P in March 2025 with 32 Gb/s per lane. Rebellions identifies its Rebel-Quad NPU as a UCIe-Advanced implementation.

AMD has outlined native UCIe 1.1 connectivity for Versal RF-series adaptive SoCs with production chiplets expected in late 2027. Future evidence of success will come from validated silicon, interoperable memory controllers, and commercial products. The articles leave open whether these efficiency claims will translate into system-level performance under production workloads. Industry observers will watch for silicon announcements and customer deployments during 2027 and 2028. Broad adoption is required to determine if these chiplets change AI processor economics.

stories.Headline: Pedro Pascal says filming Behemoth! gives him hope amid the AI boom
stories.Summary:
Tony Gilroy wrote and directed the Searchlight film Behemoth!, which stars Pedro Pascal and premieres in theaters on December 4. The movie focuses on a fight for humanity and explores if artificial intelligence can replace the humanizing element of cinema. Pascal plays Alex Serian, a former child prodigy cellist who returns home to Los Angeles to compose film scores. This story also follows the main character as he attempts to reconnect with his family through his musical work. The production serves as a lyrical love letter to the music of the movies according to a review.

The film features a cast including Olivia Wilde, Eva Victor, Will Arnett, Hank Azaria, Margarita Levieva, and Matthew Lillard. It requires a focus on organic storytelling to push back against the current boom of artificial intelligence in art. The plot centers on the city of Los Angeles where the protagonist returns to pursue his professional composing career. Searchlight Pictures is the studio responsible for releasing the movie on the specific date of December 4. Every department involved in the film worked with a purity of love despite not making money on the project.

Pedro Pascal told Vanity Fair that the experience of shooting the movie injected him with a tremendous amount of hope. He noted that the most expensive people were involved because of their talent and experience rather than for profit. Pascal believes there is a thrilling pushback occurring this year through movies that fight for humanity and storytelling. He stated that people want to be connected, tell each other's stories, and look after one another as humans. The actor was surprised that Gilroy made the film so intimate and healing instead of being mean.

Tony Gilroy stated that there is a clear natural resistance to the robot takeover in the music and film industries. He believes that people want humans and noted that the music scene has been dying for fifteen years. Gilroy suggested that people should blow up AI centers at the voting box by going and voting against them. He admitted that an algorithm could probably replace the emotional amplitude of movies, but this specific film is organic. The director is a two time Oscar nominee who champions the humanity of art over an over-reliance on AI.

The articles explain that the music scene has been struggling for fifteen years but is now grooving a little bit. This background sets the stage for a film that emphasizes organic human connection over the efficiency of artificial intelligence. The production involved highly experienced talent who worked together in a contagious environment of love for the creative process. The film was screened at the New York Film Festival where it received a positive lyrical review. These elements combine to create a project that resists the current trend of using AI in the arts.

The movie will officially premiere in theaters on December 4 to bring its message of humanity to the general public. Future developments regarding the fight for creativity and politics in cinema remain open as the AI boom continues growing. It is unclear what will happen next in the industry or what specific elements of cinema will return. The articles leave open whether the pushback against AI will successfully protect the humanizing elements of the movie business. The long term impact of this organic approach to filmmaking remains to be seen after the premiere.

stories.Headline: EU leaders postpone AI discussions to focus on Ukraine negotiations at Dublin summit
stories.Summary:
EU leaders gathered in Dublin on November 13 and 14 for a summit focused on artificial intelligence and regional security. The meetings were derailed when the Ukraine issue became the main focus after US envoys met with President Zelensky. European leaders shifted their attention to forming a negotiating team to speak with one voice to the outside world. The ninth European Political Community summit occurred Thursday, followed by an informal European Union leaders meeting on Friday. These high-level gatherings took place at the Convention Centre Dublin, which overlooks the River Liffey in Ireland.

The summit required a negotiating team consisting of EU institutions and five Coalition of the Willing countries, Britain, France, Germany, Italy, and Poland. Ursula von der Leyen proposed spending 30 billion euros, or 33.07 billion US dollars, to build seven AI gigafactories. She estimated that Europe actually needs at least 500 billion euros, or 551.10 billion dollars, to advance its broader technological ambitions. The 2023 Chips Act aimed for 20 percent of the global market, but the industry now declares this goal unattainable. Ireland held the rotating presidency of the Council of the EU during the second half of 2026.

European Council President Antonio Costa announced the formation of the negotiating team and said leaders would revisit AI in February 2027. Ursula von der Leyen outlined the gigafactory plans, while President Emmanuel Macron called for faster decisions and much greater investment. Macron and Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten will convene a meeting of European technology leaders in Paris on December 2. President Zelensky described recent talks in Abu Dhabi as serious and urged Europe to secure a regular place in negotiations. These leaders sought a greater say in decisions affecting the future of Europe and the security of the region.

Around 1,000 pro-Palestinian demonstrators marched toward the National Gallery of Ireland to protest military spending and the neutrality of Ireland. More than 5,000 Irish police officers managed security, causing road closures and transport restrictions that disrupted daily life in Dublin. The Irish Times noted that these security operations caused public disruption and raised questions about the costs of hosting gatherings. The Centre for European Policy Studies warned that relying on foreign chip suppliers could create new and dangerous technological dependencies. The Financial Times reported that productivity gains from AI in Europe have remained modest despite some new industrial activity.

The 2000 Lisbon Strategy aimed to build a competitive knowledge economy by 2010, but it failed and became the Europe 2020 Strategy. This second strategy also failed because subsidizing farmers and saving factories wins more votes than spending on long-term competitiveness. Europe now faces funding gaps for Ukraine and a 22nd round of sanctions, with more financial discussions coming soon. The region struggles with strategic anxiety and a lack of hard power in computing, chips, and advanced AI models. This pattern shows a tendency to retreat to coordination rather than committing real money to achieve clear strategic objectives.

EU leaders will return to discuss Ukraine financing needs at their next meeting on November 26 and 27. Territorial disputes and security guarantees for Ukraine remain unresolved, and the appointment of a single European envoy is still open. The future of the AI gigafactory plan remains stalled and tied to negotiations over the next long-term EU budget. The articles leave open whether Europe can maintain strategic autonomy without depending on any third party for its international role. It remains unclear if the 27 member states will agree to pay the funds needed for technological competitiveness.

stories.Headline: Physicist Nathaniel Craig and GPT-6 Astra propose a lattice definition of the Standard Model
stories.Summary:
Physicist Nathaniel Craig, a visiting scientist at OpenAI, worked with GPT-6 Astra on a candidate lattice definition of the Standard Model, as described in a guest post on OpenAI's science blog dated November 15, 2026. Craig leads the particle theory group at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and is a permanent member of its Kavli Institute for Theoretical Physics. In an October preprint prepared with the aid of GPT-6 Astra, Craig proposed a candidate definition on a lattice, a grid representing spacetime. Craig had a strategy for tackling the problem but had not been able to prove it worked in all the cases it needed to cover. Astra helped turn that strategy into a construction and took the lead in developing the detailed proof.

The Standard Model describes the known elementary particles and three of the four fundamental forces: the strong force, the weak force, and electromagnetism. Its success rests on agreement between theoretical calculations and experiments across eighteen orders of magnitude, from the low energies of hydrogen's 21-centimeter radio emission to the high energies of collisions at the Large Hadron Collider. For more than fifty years a foundational problem has remained: how to give the full theory a nonperturbative definition that does not treat its interactions as small corrections. Perturbation theory has let physicists predict the strength of the electron's magnetism to within a few parts in a trillion. For the full Standard Model in continuous spacetime, there is no nonperturbative definition, or even an understanding of whether the interacting theory is mathematically well defined.

Craig wrote that a promising alternative is to discretize spacetime into a grid of points known as a lattice, whose spacing defines the shortest distance the theory can resolve. Studying a finite grid allows a rigorous nonperturbative definition of the theory at a given spacing and enables calculations on a computer without perturbation theory. This approach, lattice field theory, has led to remarkable progress in understanding the strong force, including a quantitative understanding of the proton's mass from first principles. Craig explained that the Standard Model is a chiral theory, meaning it looks different under reflection in space, because the weak force treats left- and right-handed fermions differently.

He wrote that putting chiral theories on a lattice is profoundly challenging, since the most natural rules give a left-handed fermion a right-handed partner you never asked for, a problem called doubling. Craig described an analogy with light, in which a box with ordinary mirrors turns left-circular light into right-circular light, much as doublers appear when a left-handed fermion is put on the lattice. He wrote that chiral mirrors made of special films whose molecules line up in layers can send left-handed light back left-handed and let right-handed light pass through. Such chiral mirrors have been around for more than a decade, and the phenomenon even occurs in nature, in the shiny shells of some scarab beetles.

Decades ago, Paul Ginsparg and Nobel laureate Ken Wilson worked out the lattice rules analogous to the requirement that chiral mirrors reverse the rotation of the electric field upon reflection. Rajamani Narayanan and Herbert Neuberger built the analog of the chiral mirrors by finding the necessary definition of fundamental particles on the lattice, known as overlap fermions. Martin Lüscher showed how to tell the difference between left-handed and right-handed overlap fermions on the lattice, while Yoshio Kikukawa and collaborators explored how this might be used to describe weak interactions in the Standard Model. Craig wrote that one piece was still missing, which he identified as getting the phase right.

He explained the optical phase by imagining water waves rolling past the pilings of a dock, and the relative phase of two waves determining how much they add or cancel at the same point. In a box with chiral mirrors, left-circular light bounces back and forth, and after a lap the returning light meets fresh light from the laser going in the same direction. If their electric fields are in step, the light builds up inside the box, and if the fields are half a cycle apart, the returning light cancels some of the fresh light. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Unemployment Labs finds restricted Nvidia Blackwell chips in six Chinese AI models
stories.Summary:
A U.S. nonprofit research group found that Chinese AI models used restricted Nvidia Blackwell chips. Unemployment Labs published this report on November 12, 2026, regarding these findings. The analysis identified traces of these graphics processing units in models from four major companies. These companies include DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax, and Ant Group. The researchers used digital forensic techniques to identify these specific hardware fingerprints.

The analysis covered six models released since April, including DeepSeek V4-Flash, V4-Pro, and Ant Group Ling-3.1-Flash. Moonshot AI released Kimi K3 and K3.1-Pro, while MiniMax released the M3 model. DeepSeek V4-Flash and MiniMax M3 matched B200 and B300 series characteristics. The other four models matched GB200 and GB300 series, which combine Blackwell GPUs with Grace CPUs. These chips were launched in February last year, before the Rubin chip arrived in July.

Will DePue, a former OpenAI researcher leading Unemployment Labs, oversaw the forensic analysis. The researchers said they reproduced initialization patterns of DeepSeek V4-Flash on a B300 chip. They also reproduced the patterns of Kimi K3 using a rented GB200. The group estimated that 12,000 Blackwell GPUs were used in large-scale Chinese training projects. They stated that chip purchases and cluster construction could have cost over 500 million dollars.

Industry experts suggest Chinese firms may have remotely rented chips from data centers in Southeast Asia. Others believe the hardware was smuggled into China through various third country workaround routes. The report affects the U.S. government, which restricts these exports on national security grounds. The Donald Trump administration allowed limited H200 exports but blocked Blackwell and Rubin chips. These findings suggest a potential gap in the semiconductor export controls targeting China.

The report follows a scandal involving Alice Huang, who is suspected of being a Chinese spy. She allegedly used an affair with former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to smuggle advanced chips. These chips were reportedly diverted through a Singapore entity called Megaspeed and its Malaysian subsidiary. Jensen Huang was removed from his post on November 12 amid these internal company issues. This background adds attention to how China may have gained access to restricted hardware.

The researchers cautioned that their figures are rough estimates based on assumptions about GPU utilization. They stated the evidence does not prove where the chips were physically installed. The findings do not establish if the companies directly violated U.S. export control laws. It is unclear if Blackwell GPUs were used throughout the entire training process. The articles leave open whether the U.S. government will introduce additional circumvention measures.

stories.Headline: New Jersey governor Mikie Sherrill pushes state action on child safety and Big Tech privacy
stories.Summary:
New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill spoke with Nilay Patel on November 16, 2026, about recent midterms and tech policy. Sherrill believes her own election served as a preview for the huge Democratic victories seen in those recent midterm races. She started her campaign in November 2024, immediately after Donald Trump won the presidential election in that same month. The governor focused her campaign on the dual themes of accountability and affordability to connect with the voting public. She believes the Democratic Party is most powerful when it fights for working families through these specific policy goals.

The governor is now exercising state power to address child safety and Big Tech overreach because federal regulation is lacking. She is leading fights regarding online privacy, age verification, and data centers while also expecting more litigation against Big Tech. Sherrill mentioned a Meta settlement and the privacy implications of AI and Flock, which she believes require more public discussion. In India, Parliament enacted the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, to create a framework for protecting personal information. The Supreme Court of India previously recognized privacy as a fundamental right in the 2017 Justice K.S. Puttaswamy case.

Governor Sherrill stated that she feels fantastic about the midterms and believes New Jersey acted as a political bellwether. She said that voters were furious and wanted a leader to address the fear caused by Elon Musk's actions. Sherrill argued that corruption is tied to people's pocketbooks, citing Trump's alleged profits from an Iranian war and Russian diesel. She believes that being a strong leader requires being accountable and honest about government problems rather than sweeping them away. The governor also noted that the current era of politics makes it nearly impossible to hide information from people.

Nilay Patel noted that corruption appeared as a top issue in a Guardian poll and linked it to tech billionaires. He mentioned that influencer politics is rising, citing New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Abdul El-Sayed as key examples. The House Oversight Committee also used a hype reel style video to communicate, which Patel described as being incredibly effective. In Jammu and Kashmir, citizens using digital platforms for banking and education are affected by data collection and processing. These individuals leave digital trails including telephone numbers, locations, and financial details that can reveal intimate aspects of their lives.

Sherrill observed that voters were angry about tech billionaires who flip-flop between liberal and Trump values just to make money. She mentioned that Trump allegedly received payments from the UAE to open floodgates for high-end semiconductor chips despite Congress. The governor also discovered that the previous administration failed to clear non-citizens off the voter rolls in New Jersey. In India, the DPDP Act has sparked a debate over whether the law protects citizens or enables state surveillance. The region of Jammu and Kashmir has a specific history with internet restrictions that makes these digital rights very significant.

The Supreme Court of India will soon consider the DNPA challenge to clarify the relationship between privacy and freedom of expression. This legal process will determine if data protection can exist without weakening accountability or restricting the freedom of the press. Sherrill believes that being present on social media is a permanent fixture for politicians who want to reach the public. The articles leave open whether the DPDP Act can truly safeguard citizens against excessive governmental access to their personal data. It remains unclear if the new brand of influencer politics will continue to wield algorithms against their own corporate owners.

stories.Headline: Japanese manufacturers report higher profits as AI demand lifts earnings
stories.Summary:
Many publicly traded Japanese companies reported higher profits for the first half of the current business year ending in March. These financial gains occurred during the period from April to September and were driven by the ongoing artificial intelligence boom. Firms within the manufacturing sector performed particularly well as they capitalized on the robust demand for new technology. Several of these organizations have already revised their full-year earnings forecasts upward to reflect this growth. The current economic shift requires these companies to adapt their production and financial planning to meet the surging demand for AI.

This trend changes the outlook for the manufacturing sector by increasing the expected revenue for the remainder of the fiscal year. Every firm that closes its books in March must now account for these unexpected gains in their official reports. The surge in profits indicates a broader transition toward integrating artificial intelligence across various industrial applications. Yoshimitsu Goto, who serves as the Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of SoftBank Group, spoke about these developments.

He addressed the current business climate during an online news conference held on Tuesday to discuss the financial landscape. While the specific details of his remarks were not fully detailed, his presence highlighted the importance of the AI boom. He represents a major player in the technology sector that is closely monitoring these market shifts. The broader context involves a period of significant growth for Japanese firms despite growing uncertainty in the global market.

These companies are leveraging the AI boom to strengthen their positions against international competitors in the tech space. Future reports will likely determine if this profit trend continues through the end of the business year. Analysts are watching to see if other sectors beyond manufacturing will experience similar financial boosts. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Air Marshal Tejinder Singh highlights AI's role in future military capabilities at Pune seminar
stories.Summary:
Air Marshal Tejinder Singh, the Chairman of the Chiefs of Staff Committee, spoke about the strategic importance of Artificial Intelligence in shaping future military capabilities and operational preparedness, according to a Defence Ministry official. He made his remarks at a seminar held as part of a three-day Capsule on Science, Technology and Applied Research Programme at the Military Institute of Technology in Pune. The seminar carried the theme of AI versus AI as a new frontier of warfare and brought together tri-service leadership along with technology experts from academia and industry. Those present deliberated on the changing character of warfare in the AI era, the Integrated Defence Staff Headquarters said in a post on the social media platform X. The seminar included sessions by subject matter experts from the Armed Forces, academia and industry that covered emerging AI technologies, Sovereign AI, AI-enabled weapon systems, autonomous and counter-autonomous systems, human-machine teaming and decision superiority in multi-domain operations.

A key highlight was an event called Navonmesh, described as a meeting place for innovation and new ideas, where leading industry partners showcased cutting-edge AI technologies and innovative solutions along with their potential military applications. The seminar reinforced the importance of jointness, indigenous technological capabilities and collaboration between the Armed Forces, academia and industry in preparing for the evolving challenges of future warfare. Before the seminar, Air Marshal Tejinder Singh visited the National Defence Academy at Khadakwasla in Pune, where he reviewed key training infrastructure, the curriculum and forthcoming development projects aimed at further enhancing the training environment. The Integrated Defence Staff Headquarters said he also visited the outdoor tactical training site and interacted with cadets undergoing camp training, gaining insights into their training experiences and professional development. Addressing the cadets, he urged them to uphold the highest traditions of military ethos and to imbibe the core values of discipline, integrity and dedication while fostering a spirit of jointness.

He further urged them to strive for professional excellence and to prepare themselves to shoulder future responsibilities, carrying forward the legacy of what the statement called a distinguished cradle of military leadership. In a separate message, the Indian Air Force said on X that a exercise named AJHE26 was set to commence at Air Force Station Jamnagar from November 17 to 19, 2026. That exercise will bring together the Indian Defence Forces, the National Disaster Management Authority, the Indian Coast Guard and friendly foreign countries, according to the Indian Air Force message. The stated aim of the exercise is to strengthen joint preparedness and coordination in disaster response among the participating forces and agencies. The articles do not say what decisions, if any, followed from the seminar or the academy visit, and they give no further details on the outcomes of either.

stories.Headline: Microsoft removes WordPad from Windows 11 as users restore it manually
stories.Summary:
The author copied WordPad from a fresh Windows 10 installation to a Windows 11 26H2 PC, as reported by Windows Latest on November 15, 2026. Microsoft had removed WordPad from Windows 11 version 24H2, and the app is still missing in 26H2. The author said he recently updated his father's PC to Windows 11 26H2, and his father asked whether it had WordPad. When told Microsoft had deprecated it, his father sighed and said it was enough for him. The author saw someone on X complain about the new Notepad a few days earlier, and most replies favored the post.

Microsoft deprecated WordPad in September 2023, saying it was no longer being updated and would be removed in a future release of Windows. In March 2024, the company confirmed WordPad would be gone from all editions of Windows 11 24H2 and Windows Server 2025. Three files were removed: wordpad.exe, wordpadfilter.dll and write.exe, and Windows no longer has a built-in RTF reader. Microsoft recommends Word for rich-text documents like .rtf and .doc, and Notepad for .txt files. WordPad arrived with Windows 95 in August 1995, replacing Microsoft Write, and the Windows 95 Reviewer's Guide admitted it was not a full-blown word processor.

Microsoft's developer documentation mentions the three removed files, and Microsoft's old Knowledge Base article Q135079 lists tables, borders, shading and columns among the Word formatting that disappears in WordPad, calling it a design limitation of WordPad. Microsoft's support page says Notepad's Writing Tools are powered by GPT, which means users must sign in with a Microsoft account to use them. Microsoft's old WordPad help page warned that headers, footers or comments opened in WordPad and saved would be lost. Microsoft did test Office banner ads inside WordPad in a January 2020 Windows 10 Insider build, but they were hidden behind a feature flag. Microsoft never formally announced a change of plans about the Ignite features, but they seem no longer under development.

The author said the Copilot branding is gone from Notepad, the Writing Tools can be switched off, and formatting or tables isn't hurting anyone. He said he doesn't mind the new features and sometimes uses them, but WordPad has no account prompt or AI button and won't get any updates. He said a missing spell check hurts the most, especially when the new Notepad has it, and that for a resume or a document with tracked changes, Word or the free Word for the web is still the right tool. Notepad got a Create a table option for everyone in January 2026, but those tables, along with bold, italics, headings and lists, are stored as Markdown in a plain-text file. PCMag's Chris Hoffman wrote that Microsoft unveiled several major Windows features at Ignite last year, such as a way for AI agents to access Windows desktop apps, but many never made it out of Insider builds.

WordPad sat between Notepad and Word for almost three decades, and its Office-style ribbon came with Windows 7. The Home tab has fonts and sizes, bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, subscript and superscript, text highlighting and font colors, plus alignment, indentation, line spacing and bulleted lists. The Insert group lets you add pictures, date and time, and objects from other apps, and a ruler lets you drag paragraph margins. WordPad documents save as RTF by default, but it can also save .docx, .odt and plain text files. At Build earlier this year, Microsoft announced experimental tools including Microsoft Execution Containers (MXC) to safely sandbox OpenClaw agents, and at Ignite last year it debuted an on-device MCP server registry for Windows and a File Explorer MCP connector.

The author's archive has wordpad.exe, WordpadFilter.dll and an en-US folder with wordpad.exe.mui, and users copy them into C:\Program Files\Windows NT\Accessories and approve the administrator prompt. WordPad won't appear in Start menu search this way, so users pin it to the taskbar and set it as the default app for .rtf files from Open with > Choose another app. WordPad doesn't get security fixes anymore, so the author advises avoiding RTF or DOCX files from people you don't trust. Ignite runs from Nov. 17 to 20 at the Moscone Center in San Francisco, and CEO Satya Nadella will kick off the enterprise-focused event with a keynote.

The keynote starts at 10 p.m. in Dubai, 9 p.m. in Riyadh and 8 p.m. in Cairo, and the free digital pass is open to anyone, wherever they live.

stories.Headline: Anthropic ports AI model to AMD hardware in three days to reduce reliance on Nvidia software
stories.Summary:
Anthropic recently announced that its AI model could be ported to different hardware in just three days. This development occurred around November 15, 2026, according to reports from The Motley Fool. The AI lab used its Claude Mythos Preview model to achieve this rapid optimization. This move potentially weakens the market dominance of Nvidia by benefiting its rival, Advanced Micro Devices. The process allows AI models to run on alternative chips despite different software stacks.

The system requires porting Claude to run on AMD MI355 GPUs, with the model writing 100 percent of the kernels. This replaces a process that previously took a dozen engineers between six and 12 months to complete. Anthropic aims to create a fungible compute pool using Nvidia GPUs, AMD GPUs, Amazon Trainium, or Alphabet Tensor Processing Units. AMD's Helios system costs roughly 20 billion dollars per gigawatt, while Nvidia's Vera Rubin platform costs 40 billion. AMD also committed up to 5 billion dollars as Anthropic targets 2 gigawatts of AI chips.

Anthropic stated that its goal was to buy chips based on the best price performance regardless of the vendor. The company wants to use specific chips for the tasks they are best at, such as training or inference. This capability allows the lab to bring any AI chip up to speed within a few days. By reducing the complexity of switching hardware, Anthropic believes it can level the playing field for chipmakers. The lab's actions suggest a shift toward hardware flexibility for high performance computing workloads.

Nvidia may lose market share and be forced to lower prices, which would impact its sales and gross margins. Investors in AMD stand to gain significantly because the company can grow sales without taking a massive market share. European AI ambitions are also affected by a scandal involving Nvidia's now former CEO and an alleged Chinese spy. This reputational damage comes at a time when AMD is rolling out its new Helios system. Other affected parties include developers who were previously trained exclusively on the Nvidia CUDA software platform.

Nvidia built a wide moat using the CUDA software platform and the CUDA-X ecosystem of AI libraries and tools. The company seeded this software into universities and research labs to train a generation of AI developers. Most original AI code was written on CUDA and optimized specifically for Nvidia chips to ensure dominance. Nvidia also provided free GPUs and training to researchers to maintain its lead in the AI training market. This ecosystem created a situation where software written on CUDA did not run on competitors' chips.

Anthropic will continue to seek a fungible compute pool to optimize its costs and performance across various vendors. AMD may see significant sales growth if it captures a larger share of the AI semiconductor market. Nvidia still possesses the premier AI infrastructure solution and the best overall ecosystem for high performance computing. The company has also locked up a large supply of high bandwidth memory needed for all AI chips. The articles leave open whether Nvidia can maintain its lead despite the shrinking of its CUDA moat.

stories.Summary:
An AI financial analyst named ARTi launched in July to provide investment research. Hong Kong listed companies and family offices made strategic investments in the startup. The product was incubated from a family office business system in Hong Kong. It allows users to inquire about stock trends and quotes via chat. The tool can also generate investment research reports for its users.

Delin Holdings, listed as 1709.HK, made a strategic investment in the platform. C Capital provided 1.5 million US dollars in Pre-A round funding in June. This investment gave the company a pre-money valuation of 30 million US dollars. The product reached 70,000 users within four months of its official launch. It connects to communication platforms like WhatsApp instead of requiring a new App.

CEO Eason Zhang said the tool solves the problem of information overload. He stated that every investment judgment made by the AI must be verifiable. Zhang believes professional agents need specific data sources and financial analysis frameworks. He noted that general large models often prefer guessing over admitting uncertainty. The team uses multi-model collaboration to establish a system for result verification.

High-net-worth investors and beginners, including Hong Kong university students, use the service. Some users from Delin's wealth management business provide core customer feedback. These professional investors require continuous tracking and clear frameworks for their research. Many users have expressed a willingness to pay for these professional services. The product currently serves as a value-added service for certain high-net-worth clients.

Eason Zhang previously served as a strategic consulting partner at a global firm. He founded a fintech enterprise after leaving that consulting role in 2015. The startup combines Silicon Valley AI technology with Hong Kong financial business resources. CTO Steve brings experience from Silicon Valley entrepreneurship to the technical architecture. A chief scientist from a Silicon Valley laboratory serves as an expert consultant.

The company has started its Series A financing to grow the business. ARTi plans to launch a subscription model with various monthly paid packages. These tiers are designed at 20, 100, and 200 US dollars per month. Paid users will gain access to virtual trading functions and research services. The articles leave open when large-scale charging will officially begin for users.
