stories.Headline: Nvidia accepts CEO Jensen Huang's resignation and appoints CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO
stories.Summary:
Nvidia experienced a major leadership change when the board accepted the resignation of CEO Jensen Huang on November 11, 2026. The company officially announced this decision the following day, leading to the appointment of Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as the interim CEO. This shift is expected to weaken the dominance of Nvidia in the artificial intelligence semiconductor market. Consequently, Samsung Electronics is positioned to become the primary beneficiary as the industry moves toward a more diversified ecosystem.

The changing market requires a shift toward custom chips, known as application-specific integrated circuits, such as AWS Trainium and Google Tensor Processing Units. KB Securities projected in a November 16 report that non-Nvidia customers will account for 65% of Samsung Electronics high-bandwidth memory shipments by 2027. By that same year, Nvidia is expected to represent 38% of global demand for this memory, while Google will take 37% and AMD will take 13%. Other customers are projected to make up the remaining 12% of the global demand landscape.

Kim Dong-won, the head of research at KB Securities, stated that uncertainty regarding leadership at Nvidia will likely encourage customers to diversify their supply chains. He noted that the rush by Amazon, Google, and AMD to commercialize their own AI accelerators is accelerating this structural change. Kim further explained that while the leading figure may be gone, the overall empire of artificial intelligence will continue to grow larger. He expressed confidence that Samsung Electronics can grow because it maintains the broadest customer base outside of the Nvidia ecosystem.

This transition is occurring as Big Tech companies increase efforts to develop in-house chips and expand the AI inference market. Samsung Electronics is also pursuing growth through processing-in-memory technology, which was showcased via the LPDDR5X-PIM product at the FMS 2026 conference last August. LS Securities suggested that moving computing operations directly into memory could improve efficiency and increase the strategic value of these components. Industry observers are now watching to see if Samsung can successfully increase its market share during this period of diversification.

stories.Headline: LG Energy Solution unveils integrated power infrastructure for AI data centers at RE+ 2026
stories.Summary:
LG Energy Solution announced on November 15 that it would participate in the RE+ 2026 renewable energy exhibition in Las Vegas, Nevada. The event takes place from November 17 to 19 and focuses on stability, resilience, and intelligence for the artificial intelligence future. The company is using this platform to transition its public image from a battery manufacturer into a comprehensive energy platform company. Its exhibition space covers approximately 280 square meters, which represents a 20 percent increase over the previous year.

The company is unveiling an integrated power infrastructure for AI data centers that bundles a Battery Energy Storage System, Uninterruptible Power Supply, Battery Backup Unit, and Energy Management System. Other displays include the JF3 AC Link using American lithium iron phosphate batteries, which increases energy density per site unit by about 26 percent. The exhibit also features sodium-ion batteries combined with solid-state transformers, a JP6 UPS rack system, and a cylindrical 2170 BBU. Additionally, the firm is highlighting its North American production capacity of over 50 gigawatt-hours and its specialized subsidiary, Vertech.

Company representatives are promoting their ability to handle everything from design and construction to operation and asset management through the AEROS Suite software platform. They are also showcasing their recent selection as a partner for the DSX Ready BESS program managed by Nvidia. Experts from the firm will lead sessions on system integration and preparation strategies specifically tailored for AI data centers. These presentations aim to demonstrate differentiated capabilities in power infrastructure construction and overall system operation.

stories.Headline: Emulate’s liver chip becomes first organ-on-a-chip accepted into FDA drug tool pilot
stories.Summary:
R3 Bio, a Bay Area biotech company, reportedly discussed ambitions to develop "bodyoids," non-sentient human clones with functional organs to be harvested for extreme life extension, earlier this year. The company also proposed developing monkey organ sacks for use in drug toxicity testing, according to reports. R3 subsequently denied it was ever working on such capabilities. Its website downplays "recent sensational media coverage." Its stated purpose is modelling human biology to advance non-animal methods in drug development.

Roughly 90% of drug candidates that make it to clinical trials fail to reach approval. One common snag is safety and efficacy issues that arise in human trials despite a drug clearing animal tests. Emulate was founded in 2013 by a team from Harvard University's Wyss Institute to develop organ chips, thumb-sized devices containing living human tissue. In 2024, the company's liver chip was the first organ-on-a-chip device accepted by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration's pilot program for qualifying innovative drug development tools. One study showed Emulate's liver chip correctly identified 87% of drugs known to cause liver injury in humans.

Lorna Ewart, Emulate's chief scientific officer, said organ chips will be important upstream to generate accurate datasets for AI programs to reference. She said they will be equally important downstream for testing and validating AI outputs. Ewart said the current era of non-animal methods is about the "co-existence of models" rather than universal replacement. She noted that "whole-body integration," simulating the body's complex and interconnecting processes, remains difficult. Pascal Descargues, founder of Genoskin, said replacing all animal studies on the FDA's timeline of three to five years "to make animal studies the exception" is not realistic.

Troy Seidle, former global head of animal-free science at Humane World for Animals, said "the science will simply supersede in the way that planes, trains and automobiles have superseded the horse and buggy." Seidle said even when a new method is validated, there is still a "base, emotional fear response" that "we've always done it this way." He said the high bar for validating non-animal methods is flawed because "we're trying to validate [NAMs] against something that's never gone through any kind of validation process, ever." Vivodyne, founded in 2020 by University of Pennsylvania bioengineers, uses robots, machine learning, human cells and organoids to generate biological data. Eight of the world's largest pharmaceutical companies have paid for early access to Vivodyne's platform, the company has said.

A 1983 Discover magazine cover story profiled early software designed to predict the toxicity of new chemical compounds by using pattern recognition. The article quotes a biophysicist warning that "buying and maintaining laboratory animals is quickly becoming a luxury many schools and research centers can't afford." Figures reported at the time were more than 60 million animals used in the United States annually for experimental purposes. The most comprehensive estimate available puts the number of animals undergoing scientific procedures at about 80 million a year, based on 2015 data, a 39% increase from an estimate based on 2005 data. In 2022, Congress passed a bill explicitly authorizing the use of certain non-animal tests in drug development.

Genoskin has seen a 10-fold increase in revenue since the 2022 FDA legislation. In 2025, after 14 years of operating on revenue and science grants, Genoskin raised $8.7 million in Series A financing, led by the Toulouse-based OCCTE. In 2021, Emulate raised $82 million in Series E financing, led by Northpond Ventures, bringing its to-date total to nearly $225 million. A September 2026 Market Glass report projects a 12.8% compound annual growth rate from 2024 to 2030 for the global non-animal alternative testing market, reaching US$4.5 billion. A study of drug development failure estimates the average cost of developing a new drug at $1 to $2 billion and 10 to 15 years.

Articles.Title: How AI-fuelled biotech is upending drug testing

stories.Headline: Jordan Belfort builds Tone, an AI voice platform that teaches sales tonality
stories.Summary:
Jordan Belfort, the self-proclaimed "Wolf of Wall Street," is building a voice-based AI platform called Tone, TechCrunch reported on November 16, 2026. Belfort pleaded guilty in 1999 to securities fraud and money laundering tied to Stratton Oakmont, the Long Island brokerage where salespeople pushed penny stocks in pump-and-dump schemes. He spent 22 months in prison and was ordered to pay $110.4 million in restitution to 1,513 victims. Belfort completed his court-ordered restitution obligations in late April of this year, TMZ reported in July. His co-founder in the business is longtime investor Shervin Pishevar, who has a controversial past of his own.

Tone imbues its voices with tonality that wins deals, Belfort says, for example by phrasing declarative statements as questions, which "builds engagement," and even whispering at times, which "implies scarcity of information." The platform is already being used by companies that have more sales leads than their human teams can handle. Tone is launching a self-service platform for content creators and authors who want to turn their books into "expressive AI-generated narration." Users can select from Tone's AI voices or, as a voice-cloning feature rolls out, create a clone of their own voice. Belfort says he has 30 years of super high-quality data and teaches the model one tonality at a time.

Belfort said he and Pishevar have been personal friends for a long time and were out for dinner one night when an AI company pitched him an AI that could do selling. He said he listened to it and it was awful, but it put the idea in his head. He said he thought he was just going to teach models how to sell but couldn't find a voice good enough, so they built their own. He said Tone's customers include law firms and health insurance companies, and that it does a lot in polling and automobiles. He said the AI takes a customer through an entire health insurance sale, asking qualifying questions like what type of insurance you want, your budget and your ages, then choosing a plan and explaining the features and benefits.

Belfort said Tone's latency is like 600 milliseconds, and that if the payment is too high it will say it can bring the payment down and explain how to raise your deductible. He said the AI never says "That's a great question" unless it really is, and that the trick is a model that can carry a perfect conversation, handle anything thrown at it, answer elegantly and return to the straight line without breaking rapport and without hallucinating. He said revenue is probably about a million bucks, $700,000 maybe, and that they have raised friends and family and seed, about $10 million. He said he still doesn't think Tone is quite as good as a top producer, and that a top producer in the field would outdo it call for call. He said he thinks that will change in the next six months to a year, and that Tone uses its own very small, very light models rather than frontier models.

Belfort said he did make mistakes, that it was a very, very long time ago, and that he has spent the last 20-plus years teaching people all over the world. He said he has been hired by companies all over the world to teach sales and persuasion, and that if some companies don't want to work with us, that's their decision. He said he doesn't think it's about replacing humans, and that what he sees most with customers is that they simply don't have the human capital available. He said they could get a lot more leads than they have people to call, or they need coverage at different times of day or in different languages, and that there's always going to be a need for great human salespeople. He said he doesn't think sounding human is really what this is about, that they'll all sound human in six months or a year, and that it's the application of tonality that makes Tone different.

Belfort said they have a patent on it, and that ElevenLabs is a great company and Cartesia as well, but those voices didn't work for us. He said the FCC ruled in 2024 that AI voices fall under robocall rules under the Telephone Consumer Protection Act, and that Tone only calls opt-in leads or existing customers. He said you're not going to use AI to cold call people, that they would not allow that, and that you'd get sued by every TCPA lawyer in the world. He said the exception is polling, where there's an exemption that lets you call private homes without opt-in. He said they could launch the cloning tomorrow but they didn't, and that if you create a clone in their system you speak into the computer, so they know who is creating it, and that person signs a consent.

Belfort said if someone wants to upload audio, which they don't recommend, you'd have to match a live voiceprint in real time. He said their VP of engineering is Ben Sussman, that he's a brilliant engineer, and that Belfort is the judge and the jury and the executioner of what sounds perfect. He said he'll prototype something in the most obscene way and his engineers rebuild it from scratch. He said Tone charges a combination: per minute for streaming, monthly subscriptions for the content platform, and some clients where the bulk of the money is made through success. He said that if the right offer came up, and it was substantial enough, and he thought it made sense, who wouldn't entertain a conversation, but that right now his plan is to raise a significant amount.

Belfort said he doesn't think they need to own data centers but they need enough reserve compute, and that he wouldn't think he'd be selling it anytime soon, but who knows what the future brings. He said he didn't watch the Paramount+ documentary about him released this summer, and that believe it or not he doesn't watch or read anything about him, good or bad. He said he never reads a comment, and that when you're well-known you have to live by who you are inside, and that he goes by his own internal compass. The article says it cannot independently verify that the technology works as described, since neither co-founder is an engineer. The article says it is easy to argue the market is already saturated with AI voice startups and technologies.

The article says Belfort keeps resurfacing, including in recent years as a Miami-based sales consultant and one-time host of crypto workshops at his Miami Beach home. It says a New York Times reporter attended a weekend workshop several years ago where the price of admission was one bitcoin or its equivalent value at the time of $40,000. It says Belfort acquired a Southampton mansion, a 167-foot yacht, and at least one helicopter, and that he destroyed the latter two while high on Quaaludes and cocaine, as depicted in Martin Scorsese's famous adaptation of Belfort's autobiography, "The Wolf of Wall Street." It says the victims ultimately received "far less" than they were owed. It says Belfort's system of influence and persuasion stems from a system he has been teaching since the late 1980s, and that he invented the phrase "goal-oriented communication."

The article says Belfort said he went to first principles as a non-engineer, asking how he would teach a human to do this, one tonality at a time. It says he said the key to all of this is data, and that even the littlest bit of corrupt data dramatically negates the progress you've made. It says he said there are about 15 very powerful tonalities that people use all the time, and that when you're not in person, body language collapses into tonality. It says he said he is the judge and the jury and the executioner of what sounds perfect. It says Pishevar has faced misconduct allegations that he denies.

It says the article's author sat down with WeWork co-founder Adam Neumann years ago, meeting him twice in the weeks leading up to a stage interview, once at a WeWork in San Francisco and again at his office in New York. The article says the author knew full well that the numbers SoftBank in particular had assigned to WeWork made little sense, but came away understanding why investors wanted to throw in their lot with Neumann. It says it is similarly easy to understand why people are enchanted by Belfort. It says doubts about the numbers rarely get in the way of a good pitch, and that when Belfort looks for investors to back him in this new venture, finding believers won't be too hard.

It says the interview was edited for length and clarity. It says Tone comes with added risk because of Pishevar's controversial past. It says the article's author, Loizos, has been reporting on Silicon Valley since the late '90s. More to follow.

stories.Headline: FBI warns hackers use Artex AI tool to compromise systems in under three hours
stories.Summary:
The FBI warned that hackers are using an autonomous AI tool called Artex to launch global cyberattacks. These campaigns targeted the financial industry in South Korea and customers of the American IT company ConnectWise. The agency released a flash cybersecurity advisory on Friday, November 13, regarding these recent threats. Some intrusions progressed from initial targeting to active compromise in under three hours. These attacks have occurred since the tool first debuted in July or at least August 2026.

Artex is an open-source penetration testing framework written in Go that connects to models from OpenAI and Anthropic. It also integrates with DeepSeek, GLM, Grok, Kimi, and other non-U.S. or open-source large language models. The tool targets financial services, government, tech, defense, law firms, and phone or internet companies. It was used to steal personal data from 68,000 people in South Korea and 2,250 ConnectWise customers. These hackers accessed Microsoft 365 cloud environments and breached the cybersecurity company Barracuda via an exposed credential.

The FBI stated that Artex allows hackers to move at speeds that make it harder for humans to keep up. The agency requested that organizations reporting incidents provide the time from initial activity to detection and containment. Arve Kjoelen, the chief information security officer at Barracuda, said defenders often arrive after the attacker has finished. A spokesperson for ConnectWise did not respond to requests for comment about the claims made by the FBI. The FBI recommends restricting administrative access and monitoring changes to privileged identities while preserving forensic evidence.

Microsoft says the hackers who targeted ConnectWise are likely Chinese and used the tool to steal customer data. Barracuda was breached by financially motivated criminals who found a third-party credential that the company had not revoked. The South Korean financial institutions were targeted due to weak defenses and a lack of multi-factor authentication. Large enterprises are more susceptible to these AI-powered attacks because they have larger digital footprints. CFOs are now urged to eliminate approval bottlenecks that delay the containment of machine-speed threats.

Artex uses AI agents to automate reconnaissance, vulnerability discovery, and exploitation activities that previously required substantial human effort. It scans networks for weaknesses and exploits simple bugs, such as stolen passwords, to gain a foothold. The tool generates noisy traffic and data that may trigger defensive alerts for a targeted company. Historically, sophisticated attacks required skilled operators to interpret results and decide which vulnerabilities to exploit next. The tool's developer made the software closed-source after the attacks, but previous versions remain widely accessible.

The FBI says the open-source version of Artex continues to circulate and remains available for use in cyberattacks. Researchers recently found hundreds of publicly exposed Artex systems online, including the one used to target South Korea. Organizations are urged to secure their applications and monitor for suspicious activity to prevent further autonomous intrusions. The articles leave open how many customers were affected by the breach at the company Barracuda. It remains unclear if companies can redesign their internal controls fast enough to stop these automated threats.

stories.Headline: OCC warns AI lets criminals carry out account takeovers and impersonation faster
stories.Summary:
The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency released its Semiannual Risk Perspective on November 12, 2026, to warn about evolving financial threats. The agency reported that criminals are now using artificial intelligence to execute account takeovers and social engineering with increased speed and complexity. These AI tools allow impersonators to target victims and businesses on a much larger scale than was previously possible. The report emphasizes that these technological advancements make it easier for scammers to deceive both individuals and corporate treasury teams.

To combat these threats, the agency suggests that banks implement human reviews and use communication methods different from those used in the initial request. Financial institutions should monitor for frequent password resets, rapid login attempts, and unusual transaction patterns to spot fraud. For supplier payments, banks must verify if the account name matches the payee and confirm that the supplier actually requested the change. The Federal Reserve Financial Services also launched a fraud mitigation resource center on November 9 to highlight pre-payment screening tools.

The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency stated that these controls are necessary because AI gives criminals the means to carry out impersonation more effectively. Other industry guidance from Nacha in October advised corporate teams to use trusted channels and additional approvals for urgent executive requests. While 89 percent of treasury executives in a September report called supplier checks a burden, 81 percent still planned to strengthen those processes. Additionally, 75 percent of those executives intended to implement more rigorous checks on bank accounts to prevent losses.

Recent data shows that 43 percent of scam victims authorized payments within one hour of first contact with a fraudster. A study of 150 senior executives found that 61 percent of firms only use real-time identity checks for high-risk or high-value payments. However, firms using real-time ownership verification detected fraud before funds moved at double the rate of those without such checks. Because 55 percent of victims stop answering unfamiliar calls after a scam, banks are encouraged to use secure app notifications for verification.

stories.Headline: OpenAI releases an image classifier and warning screens to combat child sexual abuse material
stories.Summary:
OpenAI announced several new tools on November 16, 2026, to combat child sexual abuse material. The company released an image classifier to detect abusive content, including images generated by artificial intelligence. These measures include new warning screens and temporary blocks to stop users from accessing or creating material that sexualizes children. The company also provided new guidelines for developers and specialized AI powered tools for law enforcement agencies.

The new image classifier, developed with the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children, is available to select companies through an API at no cost. Early testing showed the tool flags 48 percent fewer images while finding the same amount of abuse, making flagged images twice as likely to be abusive. ChatGPT will now show alerts to users attempting harmful prompts and suspend those accounts for 24 hours as a warning. Repeated offenses may lead to permanent account removal, while the company works with the Tech Coalition and ROOST to share the classifier.

OpenAI collaborated with researchers like Joel Scanlan at the University of Tasmania, the Lucy Faithfull Foundation, and Protect Children to create deterrent messages. The company stated that these tools address growing safety concerns and help developers register to report abuse to the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children. Law enforcement will receive training, a field guide, and dedicated plugins for complex data analysis managed by program administrators. These efforts follow lawsuits and warnings from Common Sense Media, which previously called the company's technology an unacceptable risk for teenagers.

The company has spent the last 12 months updating content guidelines and releasing a safety blueprint to prevent harmful content. This includes retuning models and launching a special version of ChatGPT specifically designed for teens. These changes come as other chatbots, such as Grok, have been used to create nonconsensual sexualized imagery of children. OpenAI continues to refine its technology to prevent the generation of inappropriate material and protect young users.

stories.Headline: OpenAI signs four independent assessors for first phase of embedded model assessments
stories.Summary:
OpenAI said on November 16, 2026 that it had signed agreements with four independent assessors, Apollo Research, METR, Transluce, and Goodfire, for its first phase of embedded assessments. OpenAI published the announcement on its website at 06:00 UTC. The agreements cover embedded assessments, which give independent experts deep access to a lab's internal models and systems. OpenAI said the assessments would examine model alignment and the effectiveness of safeguards over an extended period. OpenAI said the access is meant to be especially relevant to its safety cases.

OpenAI said assessors receive access to some of the same internal resources its researchers use, including model checkpoints, source code, training and evaluation data, monitoring systems, technical documentation, and discussions with researchers and engineers. OpenAI said its initial assessments focus on alignment and safeguards for models during training and internal use. OpenAI said these efforts support its commitments under the White House Accord on Super Intelligence, where it agreed to independent assessments of its safety controls. OpenAI said it developed protocols and processes with input from the assessors to balance deep access with security, confidentiality, oversight, and the independence and integrity of assessments. OpenAI said assessors who need access to sensitive confidential information will work on site at OpenAI offices and be provided OpenAI devices.

OpenAI said Apollo Research will assess whether models could covertly work against their developers' intentions and whether its safeguards would detect such behavior. OpenAI said Apollo will assess four claims in two stages: that training did not incentivize subversion, that strong evaluations and red teaming do not elicit subversion, that models have not attempted subversion during internal use, and that reasoning behind subversion would be detectable. OpenAI said it will provide Apollo access to selected public and unreleased models and training checkpoints, relevant training data and evaluation results, training intervention records, monitoring systems and flagged behaviors, and researchers who can provide context, alongside the tools and compute needed for independent testing. OpenAI said Goodfire will embed interpretability researchers and use the Goodfire platform to analyze model internals. OpenAI said Goodfire's main objective is training run monitoring, debugging, and alignment, and that its primary audience is internal OpenAI researchers.

OpenAI said it intends to conduct two assessments with METR focused on model alignment and monitoring. OpenAI said METR will assess misaligned behavior in its largest reinforcement learning run to date, including failures its existing tests and monitors may have missed. OpenAI said METR would independently set assessment priorities and iterate on searches, analyses, and elicitation experiments within the selected run and agreed access, resources, and safety arrangements. OpenAI said it recently worked with METR on a monitor stress testing exercise and has preliminarily agreed to conduct another monitor assessment, which it intends to be broader but which is pending mutual agreement on scope. OpenAI said Transluce will conduct an initial assessment of its post-training alignment evaluations, examining their quality and coverage, and that the two share the intent to conduct a follow-on assessment of approximately eight weeks in early 2027.

OpenAI said its Safety and Security Committee, an independent oversight committee of the OpenAI Foundation's Board, will have visibility into the embedded assessment and the ability to exercise oversight responsibilities before, during, and at their conclusion. OpenAI said the committee will receive unredacted reports, and that both the assessors and the committee will be able to speak with each other during the assessment, including privately. OpenAI said disagreements among OpenAI and any evaluator will be escalated to the Safety Advisory Group and OpenAI executives, who will have a specified time period to resolve them, and that the committee will be notified promptly when such disagreements are escalated. OpenAI said discussions with employees are off the record, meaning they can inform the assessments but cannot be published or attributed to employees. OpenAI said assessors can request OpenAI-attested statements verifying, correcting, or clarifying something they learned in conversation with employees, and that these statements are not attributed to individuals.

OpenAI said the assessments build on its priorities and principles for third party assessments and years of work with third party evaluators, including a recent pilot assessment of its internal monitoring systems with deep internal access and an investigation of the Hugging Face incident. OpenAI said it expects technical access challenges, space constraints, evolving security protocols, and other unexpected issues to arise, especially in the early stages of embedded assessments. OpenAI said it is working with its assessors to develop clear processes for conflicts and cool-off periods, including flexibility in mitigations and transparency in decisions to request recusal. OpenAI said assessors maintain independence in publishing their assessments, but that OpenAI will retain the right to redact confidential information, consistent with previous third-party engagements. OpenAI said it may also request responsible disclosure delays to allow time to act on findings that could pose security or safety risks and remediate issues that remain.

OpenAI said it will use what it learns to deepen its work with independent experts in the coming months. OpenAI said it expects this first phase of assessments to lead to longer-term, consistent embedded engagements over time that can continuously provide third party safety signals and recommended improvements on its most load bearing safety claims and safety cases. OpenAI said it will continue working with multiple independent third parties to help build a healthy assessment ecosystem with diverse expertise and approaches. OpenAI said it will support external assessments across a broader range of safety questions in the coming months and is exploring future embedded assessments that would examine compliance with its safety frameworks, as well as its organizational culture and processes. OpenAI said the scope of the METR alignment assessment is less expansive than what METR outlines in its alignment assessment proposal.

stories.Headline: Moody's reports US life insurers hold $85.2B in AI debt, up 24% since December
stories.Summary:
When Elon Musk needed help financing a large purchase of artificial intelligence chips earlier this year, his advisers created a financial entity that would borrow billions to buy the chips and lease them back to xAI, so that xAI was not technically the borrower and its official debt load looked smaller to investors. To help fund that arrangement, $2.4 billion of the debt was sold to Athene, an insurance company that manages life insurance policies and annuities for retirees, according to a Moody's Ratings report. The deal was part of an increasingly popular playbook of tapping insurance companies, historically among the most cautious investors, to make loans to tech titans like Mr. Musk and further fuel the A.I. boom. U.S. life insurers, including some of the largest like Athene and Corebridge Financial, held $85.2 billion in A.I. debt as of June 30, up 24 percent from six months prior, according to Moody's.

That $85.2 billion accounts for just 2.1 percent of life insurers' total debt, but their exposure is expected to grow quickly, and life insurers could hold up to $185 billion of A.I. investments by the end of next year, according to Moody's. The report was published by Moody's Ratings and covered by The New York Times on November 16, 2026, and it describes both the June 30 figure and the 24 percent rise from December 31. The articles do not name the analysts who wrote the report or give any statement from them beyond the figures and the description of insurer exposure. The articles also do not say what insurers or regulators plan to do about the growing exposure.

The articles do not identify who is responsible for overseeing this debt or quote anyone commenting on it, so no responsible party and no statements can be reported from them. The only named companies are Athene and Corebridge Financial among the insurers, and xAI as the borrower behind the $2.4 billion lease arrangement. The only named person is Mr. Musk, whose need to finance a large purchase of A.I. chips set the arrangement in motion. No further context or next steps are given in the articles beyond the Moody's projection of up to $185 billion by the end of next year.

stories.Headline: Samsung increases AI semiconductor investment through 2026 to meet infrastructure demand
stories.Summary:
Samsung Electronics accelerated its investments in artificial intelligence semiconductors through the third quarter of 2026, as revealed in a quarterly report on November 16. The company spent 56.9 trillion won on facilities and 41.8 trillion won on research and development to secure future growth engines. These financial efforts coincided with a rise in global market shares for the company's flagship smartphones, televisions, and semiconductors. The semiconductor business unit led overall earnings growth, recording sales of 356.3358 trillion won.

The facility investment plan requires 52.7509 trillion won, or 93 percent of the total, to be concentrated within the semiconductor division. This funding aims to strengthen next-generation memory technologies and expand production capacity for advanced system semiconductor processes. The company also signed a foundry supply agreement with Tesla worth 16.54 billion dollars that lasts until 2033. Market shares grew to 22.1 percent for smartphones, 29.5 percent for televisions, and 38.3 percent for DRAM.

Company officials stated that these investments are necessary to prepare for a mid-to-long-term increase in demand for AI infrastructure. They noted that the expansion of the AI ecosystem and premium products helped increase the market share of the Galaxy Z Fold 8 and Flip 8. The company also highlighted the importance of mass producing HBM4 and 1c-nanometer DRAM to maintain its top position in the memory market. They are currently expanding cooperation with major clients including Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, Hong Kong Techtronics, and Supreme Electronics.

The company continues to secure a stable customer base by signing multi-year supply contracts with global big tech and AI cloud firms. It also maintains a strong intellectual property portfolio, having registered 8,411 patents in South Korea and 8,470 in the United States this quarter. Total worldwide patents have now reached 302,751 since the first United States registration in 1984. Samsung will continue targeting the global number one position for televisions for a twenty-first consecutive year.

stories.Headline: Preferred Networks taps Samsung Foundry and Semifive to build 3D-IC AI inference chip
stories.Summary:
Japanese AI company Preferred Networks has chosen Samsung Foundry to manufacture the logic chips for its next-generation AI inference semiconductor, the MN-Core L2000, with South Korea's Semifive acting as turnkey partner. The two companies disclosed the collaboration on the 17th at SC26, the supercomputing trade show held in Chicago. Tokyo-based PFN is responsible for the processor architecture and logic design, while Semifive handles design implementation, memory supply, packaging, testing and mass production. The chip uses a 3D-IC structure that stacks the compute chip and DRAM vertically, which the companies describe as the first commercial application of such a design. Tape-out, the handoff of the completed design to manufacturing, is targeted for the first quarter of 2027, and the L2000 series is the successor to the MN-Core L1000, which is scheduled for launch in 2027.

According to PFN, the new chip targets more than double the memory bandwidth of the L1000 by creating hundreds of thousands of data pathways between the compute chip and the DRAM. Because the memory is attached vertically, components such as the interposer needed to connect chips side by side are eliminated, and the company expects manufacturing costs to fall as well. Vertically stacking chips still poses challenges, since heat dissipation is difficult and securing manufacturing yields is tricky, and industry observers expect considerable process tuning before 3D-IC reaches a stable mass-production stage. Cho Myung-hyun, CEO of Semifive, said 3D-IC is a next-generation solution that can overcome the supply constraints of HBM, and that starting with the collaboration with Japan's PFN the company will lead commercialization of next-generation AI semiconductors. He has previously described the technology as offering wider bandwidth and lower power consumption than bundling eight HBM4 chips.

The collaboration is a case of the foundry-to-design-IP alliance in the AI semiconductor supply chain being reshaped around a Japanese customer. With HBM procurement emerging as a bottleneck, the attempt to secure bandwidth through vertical memory stacking has now been connected to an actual mass-production line. That development is expected to make the push to reduce memory dependence a new variable in the competition for design services and foundry orders. Semifive plans to expand the technology's application beyond data-center AI chips to robots and smart devices.

stories.Headline: KMicro launches Microsoft ISOC readiness assessment to help leaders evaluate Defender security operations
stories.Summary:
KMicro, an AI consultancy based in Costa Mesa, California, announced on November 12, 2026 a new advisory service called the Microsoft ISOC Readiness Assessment, aimed at organizations evaluating the Integrated Security Operations Center in Microsoft Defender. Microsoft had introduced ISOC in public preview on September 23, 2026, combining SIEM and XDR capabilities in the Defender portal for eligible Microsoft 365 E5, E7 and Microsoft Defender Suite customers. Existing Microsoft Sentinel customers who meet the licensing requirements are expected to be able to opt in to ISOC beginning November 15, 2026. The assessment is meant to help security leaders decide whether ISOC fits their operating model before they commit to a deployment. The engagement examines an organization's Microsoft security footprint, current Sentinel state, SOC workflows, data sources, technical prerequisites and governance considerations against its priority business outcomes.

It confirms ISOC eligibility and identifies whether the environment is Defender-only, active Sentinel, inactive or orphaned Sentinel workspace, or a mixed security operations environment. It also maps priority threats and analyst workflows to ISOC capabilities such as case management, workbooks, user and entity behavior analytics, threat intelligence, natural-language playbooks, SOC optimization and unified hunting, and it prioritizes Microsoft-native and third-party data sources with a high-level view of volumes, retention and cost. The assessment ends with a recommendation and a 90-day action plan covering whether to activate available capabilities now, plan more deeply, continue the current Sentinel path, or address prerequisites first, and it is advisory and independent of any deployment commitment. Mazen Sadat, KMicro's CEO, said most enterprises already own more security capability than they use, and that the real question is whether ISOC is right for an organization and when, not whether it is impressive. He said clients want a clear answer rather than a sales motion, and that the assessment gives executives the knowledge to move with confidence and speed because they know where the value is and what it takes to capture it.

Peter Chen, a cybersecurity leader at KMicro, said security teams are being asked to connect more signals, investigate faster, cut tool and data costs and prepare for AI agents in the SOC all at once, and that ISOC can help with each of those only if it is adopted in the right order. He said KMicro helps clients see that order clearly so the first 90 days produce measurable progress instead of another stalled rollout. The assessment extends KMicro's Security & AI Assurance practice, which helps enterprises secure their environments and prepare governance, data and operations for AI adoption. Organizations that choose to proceed can engage KMicro for separately scoped deployment, migration, connector implementation and optimization services. The Microsoft ISOC Readiness Assessment is available now to Microsoft 365 E5, E7 and Microsoft Defender Suite customers.

stories.Headline: AvePoint expands Microsoft partnership to help organizations govern and secure enterprise AI
stories.Summary:
AvePoint announced on November 10, 2026, in a release its Japanese arm distributed on November 16, that it is expanding its strategic partnership with Microsoft to help organizations adopt, govern, secure and optimize AI across the enterprise. The company said the new phase builds on a partnership of about 25 years, during which AvePoint has won the global Microsoft Partner of the Year award six times. AvePoint also said it has already rolled out Microsoft Copilot to its employees worldwide and will now expand its use of Microsoft 365 E7 so staff can use advanced AI and agent features. The announcement was made by AvePoint, Inc., which is listed on Nasdaq under AVPT and on SGX under AVP, and by AvePoint Japan, based in Minato, Tokyo, led by representative director Ken Shiomitsu.

The expanded partnership covers governance, security, resilience and operations for tools including Microsoft Copilot, Agent 365, Copilot Studio, Microsoft Foundry, Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Azure. AvePoint cited its 2026 State of AI Report, which found that about nine in ten organizations had delayed AI efforts over data security and data management concerns. The company said its Cloud Backup Express, a launch partner product for Microsoft 365 Backup Storage, has seen its customer count grow 45 times since the start of 2026. AvePoint said it was included in the first Gartner Magic Quadrant for AI Agent Management Platforms and was also named by Gartner as a representative vendor for protecting AI-native workplaces, managing Microsoft 365 storage costs, complementing Microsoft Purview governance and reducing agent sprawl in enterprise applications.

It said about half of employees now use AI agents daily or weekly, and it will exhibit at Microsoft Ignite in San Francisco from November 17 to 20, 2026. AvePoint co-founder and CEO Dr. Tianyi Jiang, known as TJ, said the company has spent a quarter century helping organizations realize the value of digital transformation and that AI is now the next major technology shift. He said the expanded partnership with Microsoft will help organizations build the trust, governance and operational foundation needed to deploy AI at scale with confidence. Edwin Vargas, Microsoft's Managing Director for AI Business Solutions and Security partnerships, said realizing AI's business value at scale requires organizations to balance innovation with security, governance and accountability.

He said the partnership combines Microsoft's AI and security capabilities with AvePoint's strength in data governance and workflows grounded in business context, so customers can adopt AI with confidence and connect the teams using it with oversight. AvePoint said it will keep acting as "customer zero" for AI transformation, feeding its own deployment experience into product innovation and customer best practices, and that insights from its internal use of Microsoft technology continue to shape AgentPulse. It said AgentPulse applies governance workflows to agents and other AI assets, mapping them to business use cases, departments and owners so attestation and remediation go to the right business units. AvePoint, founded in the United States in 2001, operates in 11 countries and serves more than 28,000 companies and over nine million users, and its Japanese subsidiary, established in 2008, has more than 1,000 customers in Japan.

stories.Headline: Stripe completes its acquisition of OpenRouter to help businesses optimize AI model choice and costs
stories.Summary:
Stripe announced on November 10, 2026, in San Francisco and Dublin that it had completed its acquisition of OpenRouter, a platform that helps companies choose among AI models and optimize their token usage. OpenRouter is described as one of the world's largest platforms of its kind, dynamically selecting from more than 400 AI models offered by over 80 providers depending on the task at hand. Stripe provides programmable financial services, and it said the combination of its pricing, billing and payments infrastructure with OpenRouter's model selection and cost optimization would help businesses optimize AI use on both the revenue and cost sides. The announcement was distributed through Stripe Japan on November 16, 2026, and the deal itself was dated November 10, 2026, US time.

Stripe said inference costs are expected to become the largest share of operating expenses at knowledge-intensive companies as AI use spreads. It noted that coding agents, customer support bots and fraud detection each require different capabilities and response speeds, and each carries a different level of value for the task itself. Companies therefore need to evaluate not just the cost of tokens but the total cost of completing a task against its outcome, looking at current spending and future expansion. Stripe also said no single AI model is best for every task, so businesses need flexibility to switch models as new ones appear and prices change, and OpenRouter offers a neutral platform for using and managing multiple models across providers.

Stripe said businesses often manage pricing and billing separately from their procurement of AI inference services, which makes it hard to grasp revenue and cost together for each task. Procurement and control of AI inference services, along with management of usage permissions and spending, are becoming management issues that affect profitability and continuity, not just technical ones, according to the company. By understanding usage and spending by business unit, product and customer and linking them to revenue, companies can more easily make decisions based on the profitability of each task. Stripe and OpenRouter said they aim to help companies choose AI models suited to each task and optimize both revenue and costs, rather than simply picking the cheapest and highest-performing model.

Stripe describes itself as a company that builds programmable financial services, used by millions of businesses worldwide for online and in-person payments, embedded finance and customized revenue models. Headquartered in San Francisco and Dublin, Stripe says it processes more than 1.9 trillion dollars annually, equivalent to about 1.6 percent of global GDP. The company says it invests in business expansion and research and development focused on AI and stablecoins. The articles do not say what happens next beyond the completion of the acquisition.

stories.Headline: Tradr plans to launch two leveraged Anthropic ETFs on Cboe on November 23
stories.Summary:
Tradr ETFs announced on November 16, 2026, that it expects two new leveraged funds tied to Anthropic to begin trading on Cboe on Monday, November 23, 2026. The two funds are the Tradr 2X Long Anthropic Daily ETF, which will trade under the ticker ANTT, and the Tradr 2X Short Anthropic Daily ETF, which will trade under the ticker ANTZ. The launch date falls on the second trading day after Anthropic's expected initial public offering of its common shares on November 19, 2026. Tradr is a provider of exchange traded funds designed for sophisticated investors and professional traders, and its product line currently includes more than 75 leveraged ETFs.

The long fund seeks 200% of the daily performance of Anthropic, PBC, whose shares are expected to trade on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT, while the short fund seeks -200% of that same daily performance. Each fund resets its performance daily and is intended to be used as a short-term trading vehicle rather than a long-term holding. Tradr says the pair will let investors express either a bullish or bearish short-term view on Anthropic through a single strategy, without the hassle of margin or the complexity of options trading. The funds are meant to give traders a jumpstart on leverage in the event that options on ANT are not yet available.

Matt Markiewicz, Head of Product and Capital Markets at Tradr ETFs, said excitement among traders had been hard to miss since Anthropic first filed its S-1 registration statement. He said traders, whether bullish on Anthropic's growth story or skeptical of its valuation, are already thinking through how they will position ahead of the listing. He described ANTT and ANTZ as designed to let those traders express a short-term view in a single ticker. Tradr also warns that the funds are riskier than alternatives that do not use leverage because they magnify the performance of the underlying security, and that leverage increases the risk of a total loss.

The announcement gives no further details on pricing, fees or the size of the funds, and it does not say how the launch would proceed if Anthropic's offering or listing were delayed. Tradr directs investors to its website for detailed information on the Anthropic ETFs and the significant risks involved with leveraged ETFs. The firm says its strategies can be accessed through most brokerage platforms and allow investors to avoid the hassle of using margin and the complexity of options trading. Tradr describes its continuing mission as providing sophisticated investors with innovative trading tools that enhance their ability to express market views with precision and efficiency.

stories.Headline: MicroVision integrates its IRIS lidar into Kodiak AI sixth-generation driverless truck platform
stories.Summary:
MicroVision announced on November 16, 2026 a partnership with Kodiak AI involving the integration of MicroVision's IRIS long-range lidar sensor into Kodiak's autonomous driving solution. MicroVision, Inc. (Nasdaq:MVIS) is based in Mountain View, CA, and Kodiak AI, Inc. (Nasdaq:KDK) is a provider of Physical AI-powered autonomous vehicle technology. The announcement was issued from Orlando, FL and Mountain View, CA. MicroVision's IRIS lidar is currently integrated into Kodiak's sixth-generation autonomous platform. Kodiak will use that platform to launch its unsupervised driverless long-haul commercial service by the end of 2026.

IRIS lidar supports Kodiak's plans for scaling long-haul deployments throughout 2027. Kodiak's technology was already deployed in 37 trucks as of Nov. 3, in a customer-owned-and-operated fleet described as the largest of its kind in the world. Kodiak's autonomous driving system relies on a modular SensorPod architecture that integrates lidar, cameras, and radar into a compact, serviceable unit designed for rapid deployment and uptime in commercial fleets. MicroVision's lidar provides long-range perception for operating fully loaded Class 8 trucks safely at highway speeds, with reliable detection beyond 250 meters. Field validation across Kodiak's commercial operations demonstrated IRIS performance under extreme vibration, dust, weather, and lighting conditions.

Jamie Hoffacker, Senior Vice President of Hardware at Kodiak, said the key to deploying driverless trucks at scale is ensuring every component performs in the real world, not just in controlled environments. Hoffacker said MicroVision's lidar has demonstrated the performance and robustness required to support Kodiak's commercial operations today and plays an important role in enabling the Kodiak Driver. Glen DeVos, MicroVision CEO, said "This is not a pilot" and that it is a commercial operation running every day. DeVos said Kodiak has built one of the most advanced autonomous trucking platforms in operation today. DeVos said the partnership reflects what it takes to move from autonomy as a concept to autonomy at scale.

Kodiak's autonomous trucking platform continues to expand across multiple verticals, including long-haul freight, industrial trucking, and defense. Kodiak's commercial deployment in the Permian Basin is supported by a binding 100-truck order from Atlas Energy Solutions, with fleet scaling expected through 2026 and beyond. MicroVision's next-generation HALO lidar platform is aligned with Kodiak's future system architecture, supporting continued performance improvements and platform evolution as Kodiak expands its deployment footprint. Kodiak AI commercializes its technology through both a Driver-as-a-Service business model and strategic partnerships. Commercial partners and customers include Atlas Energy Solutions, IKEA, Bridgestone, Werner Enterprises, C.R. England, General Dynamics Land Systems, and Roehl Transport.

In 2024, Kodiak achieved a historic milestone, becoming the first company to deploy driverless technology in customer-owned driverless semi-trucks. The Kodiak Driver, a vehicle-agnostic autonomous driving system, combines advanced AI-powered software with modular hardware. Today, the Kodiak Driver operates in the long-haul trucking, industrial trucking, and defense sectors, and is already deployed in commercial operation with no one in the cab. MicroVision has engineering centers in the U.S. and Germany and offers both short- and long-range lidar solutions, featuring solid-state sensors with varying wavelengths, advanced sensor architectures, design-to-cost engineering, and open software solutions. MicroVision describes itself as defining the next generation of lidar-based perception solutions for industrial, security & defense, and automotive markets.

The press release includes forward-looking statements regarding Kodiak's expectations about the timing of launching driverless trucks for long-haul highways operations and the timing of completion of work on its highway launch safety case. The release states that actual events and circumstances are difficult or impossible to predict and will differ from assumptions. The release lists risks including the rapid evolution of autonomous vehicle technology, flaws or errors in Kodiak's solutions, supply shortages in materials necessary for production of the Kodiak Driver, and Kodiak's ability to raise capital in the near term and long term. Kodiak anticipates that subsequent events and developments will cause its assessments to change, and it disclaims any obligation to update forward-looking statements except as required by law. The release states that forward-looking statements should not be relied upon as representing Kodiak's assessments as of any date subsequent to the date they are made.

stories.Headline: Tiny Corp opens second tinybox red preorder at $89,000 after first batch sells out
stories.Summary:
Tiny Corp began taking preorders on November 5, 2026 for a desktop machine called the tinybox red that holds four of AMD's Instinct MI300X data center accelerators, and the first batch of 25 units at $60,000 sold out within three days. The cards inside are refurbished, they come without warranties, they are capped at 500W each, and they are linked only over PCIe 5.0. A breakdown posted by the AI Quanting account on X noted that the store page already showed the machine as out of stock a few days after the listing went live. Tiny Corp has now opened preorders for a second batch of 50 units at $89,000, which is about 48% above the launch price and roughly $29,000 more per box.

On paper the machine offers 768GB of GPU memory, 21.2TB/s of aggregate memory bandwidth and 10.44 PFLOPS of FP8 compute, which are exactly four times AMD's own per-card figures of 192GB of HBM3, 5.3 TB/s and 2.61 PFLOPS of dense FP8. The listing quotes the dense number rather than the 5.22 PFLOPS AMD lists with structured sparsity, so the published specification is the more conservative one. The host is a 32-core water-cooled AMD EPYC Genoa platform with 192GB of DDR5 RAM, a 1TB boot drive, four 1TB drives in RAID 0, two 10GbE ports and an OCP 3.0 slot. Two standard 1,700W ATX power supplies feed the 54V the GPUs need through a converter, so the box runs on one 220V circuit or two 110V circuits, and Tiny Corp claims it stays under 50dB.

Tiny Corp is the company behind the machine and it is the party taking the preorders, while the account AI Quanting on X is credited with spotting that the first batch had sold out. Tiny Corp says the second batch will be delivered in Q1 or Q2 2027, though it stops just short of committing to either date as a firm timeline. The company also claims the box stays under 50dB, which would make it far quieter than the rack servers MI300X cards normally live in. The cards themselves are refurbished and come without warranties, which is part of how four data center accelerators fit into a desktop box.

The context is that MI300X cards normally live in rack servers, and Tiny Corp has squeezed four of them into a box that runs off ordinary wall power. The first batch sold out within three days at $60,000, and the second costs nearly 50% more than the former. The second batch of 50 units is now on preorder at $89,000 with delivery penciled in for Q1 or Q2 2027. Beyond that shipping window, the articles do not say what happens next.

stories.Headline: OpenAI signs six-year deal with TensorWave for 457MW of AMD-powered AI capacity
stories.Summary:
On November 16, 2026, the artificial intelligence laboratory OpenAI signed a contract with the neocloud provider TensorWave for 457MW of capacity. This six-year agreement involves the provision of IT capacity powered by AMD Instinct MI455X GPUs across several different data center locations. The project will utilize Helios rack-scale systems and will be operated as dedicated, single-tenant capacity specifically for OpenAI. Operations are expected to begin during the first half of 2027 and should be fully deployed by early 2028.

The Helios racks, which launched in July, integrate AMD Instinct MI455X GPUs, 6th Gen AMD Epyc Venice server CPUs, AMD ROCm software, and AMD Pensando networking. A single rack provides 31 terabytes of HBM4 memory, 1.7 petabytes per second of memory bandwidth, 2.9 exaflops peak FP4, and 1.4 exaflops peak FP8. AMD claims these systems offer 15 percent more peak FP4 performance and 50 percent more high-bandwidth memory capacity than the Nvidia Vera Rubin NVL72 rack. Additionally, AMD asserts the hardware delivers 50 percent more scale-out bandwidth, six percent more HBM bandwidth, and 30 percent more tokens per dollar.

Piotr Tomasik, the president and co-founder of TensorWave, stated that the ability to reliably deliver hundreds of megawatts of compute will distinguish companies supporting frontier AI. He noted that this deployment proves AMD infrastructure can operate at the scale and reliability required by the most demanding AI firms. Uday Ruddarraju, the CTO for compute at OpenAI, explained that expanding access to large-scale compute is critical for building more capable models. He added that this agreement advances a previously announced partnership with AMD to help scale AI for more people and organizations globally.

This represents the largest deployment contract for TensorWave to date, following a 350 million dollar Series B funding round in June 2026. TensorWave claims to have secured 2GW of long-term data center capacity across the United States. In January 2026, the company also signed a 20MW capacity agreement with TecFusions for data centers located in Arizona and Pennsylvania. TecFusions recently ended its relationship with Fermi's Project Matador earlier this month.

stories.Headline: Nvidia unveils Rubin HPC GPU for agentic AI science workloads
stories.Summary:
Nvidia unveiled a new GPU called Rubin HPC on November 16, 2026, a chip supported by the company's Vera Rubin platform and designed for agentic AI-powered simulation and data processing workloads across science, engineering, and analytics, according to DatacenterDynamics. The chip giant said Rubin HPC will shorten the timeline between exploration and results for the scientists and engineers who use it. The new GPU features more than 50,000 CUDA cores alongside a sparse data acceleration capability that speeds GPU-to-GPU connectivity with seventh-generation Nvidia NVLink interconnect technology. Nvidia said the chip is meant to support agentic AI-powered simulation and data processing across those fields rather than to serve general computing alone.

Instead of increasing compute capacity alone, Nvidia said the new chip offers a balanced design that scales data movement and compute together, which accelerates recurring patterns of every simulation workload. Those patterns include sparse matrix operations, stencil computations, sorting and reductions, all of which the company says are common across data analytics, science, and engineering workloads. The sparse data acceleration capability works with the seventh-generation NVLink interconnect to speed GPU-to-GPU connectivity, according to the article. The report gives no pricing, availability date, or performance figures for the chip beyond the core count and interconnect generation.

Ian Buck, vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing at Nvidia, said that for agents tackling science and engineering, faster simulation means faster discovery. He said Rubin HPC accelerates the simulations agents use to test ideas and guide their next steps, helping scientists and engineers explore more possibilities and bring breakthroughs closer. The article attributes the balanced design description and the workload examples to Nvidia rather than to independent testing. Buck's comments are the only remarks from a named Nvidia executive that the article includes.

The article places the launch in the context of Nvidia's broader hardware lineup, noting separately that HPE has expanded its Private Cloud AI solution to support mixed Nvidia hardware clusters and launched a Vera CPU rack. It also lists unrelated items, including a University of Münster deployment of Zutacore waterless two-phase liquid cooling and a third-quarter 2026 global data center market report. The article does not say when Rubin HPC will ship, what it will cost, or which customers have committed to using it. No further details on availability or adoption are given.

stories.Headline: Silicon Box starts basic design for its first plant outside Singapore in Novara
stories.Summary:
Silicon Box’s planned packaging and test plant in Novara, Italy, has entered the basic design phase, with construction set to start in 2027, according to a press release from the company. The milestone was reached together with the design and engineering firms Stantec and Drees & Sommer, both of which were appointed in 2025. A week earlier, on 9 November, the project was formally presented at the site in Agognate, outside Novara, with a symbolic laying of the foundation stone. The project, which Silicon Box calls Vulcan Project, represents an investment of EUR 3.2 billion and will be the company’s first production site outside Singapore.

The plant will integrate chiplets from different manufacturers into a single package that works as one chip, processing them on large square panels rather than round wafers, which Silicon Box says gives higher output at lower cost. The target markets include AI, supercomputing, electric and autonomous vehicles, robotics, mobile devices and space technology, and Silicon Box says its team in Singapore has so far shipped more than one billion units with the technology. The investment is backed by EUR 1.3 billion in public funding, which the Italian government manages through its investment agency Invitalia under the national semiconductor programmes that form part of the EU Chips Act. The European Commission has also granted the project Open EU Foundry status, and the plant will cover a 60-hectare site and is expected to employ around 1,600 people at full capacity.

According to Silicon Box’s COO, Jae Hak “JH” Yee, the design phase is where the experience from Singapore will be built into the new plant. He said the Singapore facility has shown that advanced panel-level packaging can run at high volume and at high yield, and that the task now is to build that same discipline into Novara from the first drawing. Stantec coordinates the project and is responsible for the office building, outdoor areas, infrastructure, water and power supply, and permits. Drees & Sommer designs the production and utility buildings, including the cleanrooms.

Silicon Box describes the Novara plant as the first of its kind in the EU, and it will be the company’s first production site outside Singapore. The basic design phase follows the formal presentation at the site in Agognate on 9 November, and construction is set to start in 2027. The plant is expected to employ around 1,600 people at full capacity on a 60-hectare site. The public funding of EUR 1.3 billion is managed by Invitalia under the national semiconductor programmes that form part of the EU Chips Act.

stories.Headline: Prophecy Gov analyzes 10,000 comments and finds 90% of Americans detest data centers
stories.Summary:
A San Francisco-based AI startup called Prophecy Gov analyzed public comments from hundreds of local government meetings across the United States that discussed data center projects, and it launched a website called American Sentiment to display the findings, KQED reported on Nov. 16, 2026. The company said it captured more than 10,000 public comments from recordings of 906 local government meetings across 417 different government entities, a small share of the more than 90,000 local government entities counted in the 2022 census. The analysis found that 90% of Americans detest data centers, while 79% of self-identified union workers supported data center development and 60% of self-identified data center workers opposed data center projects. Commenters mainly spoke about distrust of tech billionaires, a desire for more transparency and fear for the collective climate future, according to the company. Prophecy Gov did not respond to multiple requests for comment from KQED, and the American Sentiment website carries no published methodology, so it is not clear how the company turned spoken comments into a statistical rating.

Jonathan Bash, chief executive of Locunity, a company that uses AI to turn meeting agendas and videos into real-time briefings and alerts, described the general recipe as collecting meeting recordings, using speech-to-text software to create transcripts, then using an AI tool to find comments about data centers, sort them by speaker and label them as pro or anti. Bash said he could not speak to Prophecy Gov's exact tech stack but was certain AI would be used at a minimum for transcription and sentiment analysis, and he cautioned that AI can mishear names and misconstrue sarcasm. He also said city council speaker data tends to overindex toward passionate, hyper-active community members, which he called valuable for an advocate, journalist or political candidate but less useful for predicting elections or reading residents' minds. Kyle Short, a teacher at Gilroy Unified School District who is featured on the American Sentiment website with a 2 out of 5 rating, said he did not know about the project before speaking with KQED but was flattered to be included and found it inspiring that people across the political spectrum have taken issue with how data centers have been rolled out. Short said he learned about the data center issue while trying to stop an ICE processing facility from being built in Gilroy, which in the past year became a potential site for both an ICE detention facility and a data center, and he argued that data center processing power can be used for ICE operations.

Prophecy Gov did not capture public comments from San Francisco or neighboring Oakland, where residents have advocated for a data center moratorium during city council meetings. Eisa Al-Shamma, an organizer with No Data Center Oakland and the Party for Socialism and Liberation, said dozens of residents have gone to Oakland council meetings to protest proposed data center development, and he said his main concern is who controls the data centers and how they are rolled out over the will of the people. Al-Shamma said he did not take issue with the American Sentiment project using AI, arguing that the problem is not the technology itself but how it is used and developed and who holds the levers of power. Members of No Data Center Oakland and dozens of Oakland residents and organizations showed up at the city council last Tuesday before a vote on extending the data center moratorium that passed in October, and the council voted unanimously to extend it through Oct. 5, 2027. Councilmember Carroll Fife, who proposed the moratorium, said she felt it was imperative to take immediate action to protect Oakland residents from what has happened in other parts of the country, calling the measure guardrails against an industry that has steamrolled individuals across the globe.

stories.Headline: Lam Research’s Chin Hock Toh says advanced packaging drives AI scaling through industry collaboration
stories.Summary:
Chin Hock Toh of Lam Research wrote about how advanced packaging is becoming a critical technology for scaling artificial intelligence on November 16, 2026. This shift allows the integration of compute, memory, and connectivity into next-generation systems to overcome performance and efficiency challenges. Advanced packaging now serves as a primary innovation engine rather than just a supporting function for semiconductor manufacturing. The process helps chipmakers integrate multiple technologies into optimized systems that deliver greater performance than traditional monolithic chip approaches. This evolution is reshaping the roles of various players across the entire semiconductor ecosystem to meet AI demands.

The technology requires high-bandwidth memory, chiplets, hybrid bonding, and 3D integration to solve the memory wall and rising thermal demands. Lam Research has invested in these areas for over 15 years and has shipped more than 500 SABRE 3D systems. The company recently opened a dedicated Panel Center of Excellence in Salzburg, Austria, to support future panel-level packaging productivity. These processes include TSV formation, electrochemical deposition, TSV etch, and wafer-to-wafer stacking for leading foundries and memory manufacturers. Such advancements are necessary because AI systems depend on how efficiently data moves between processors, memory, and networking components.

Chin Hock Toh, the director of Technical Program Management for Advanced Packaging at Lam Research, stated that no company can solve AI scaling alone. He explained that the industry's center of gravity is moving from chip design toward a more comprehensive system design approach. Toh noted that advanced packaging expertise is now a strategic capability rather than simply a manufacturing service for the industry. He emphasized that future progress depends on collaboration among chipmakers, foundries, memory suppliers, equipment providers, materials companies, and research institutions. Lam Research collaborates with leading universities and imec to accelerate the commercialization of these next-generation packaging technologies.

Outsourced semiconductor assembly and test providers, known as OSATs, are affected as they move beyond traditional assembly roles to become strategic enablers. These OSATs now help customers navigate complex packaging architectures, heterogeneous integration, and the scale-up of manufacturing for AI systems. The industry is also affected by the need for new materials and more precise manufacturing techniques to manage defects and yield. Designers are affected because they must now combine specialized components into tightly integrated systems to improve flexibility and power efficiency. These changes are driven by the enormous compute power and memory bandwidth required by modern AI workloads.

For decades, the semiconductor industry followed a formula of making transistors smaller, faster, and more energy efficient to achieve progress. However, the AI era is changing the definition of scaling by emphasizing integration as much as transistor density. Heterogeneous integration allows the combination of multiple semiconductor technologies into a single package to achieve higher performance and design flexibility. High-bandwidth memory specifically provides the necessary data flow to feed modern AI accelerators efficiently. This background shows that the industry is shifting toward system-level design to overcome existing computing constraints.

The industry will next explore panel-level packaging to enable larger package formats and higher productivity for future heterogeneous integration architectures. Future AI progress will depend on the ability to integrate more compute, memory, and intelligence into highly optimized systems. Lam Research continues to invest in panel-level processing technologies to support this transition for its customers. The articles leave open how long the adoption of panel-level packaging will take to become a standard industry practice. They also leave open how specific geopolitical tensions or trade regulations might impact the future sale of these equipment technologies.

stories.Headline: Micron pauses work on a 4.5 billion dollar high bandwidth memory plant in Taiwan
stories.Summary:
Micron Technology paused work on a planned facility in Taiwan, according to a report dated November 6, 2026. This company is the only large memory maker based in the United States and trades on Nasdaq as MU. The report stated that the project was valued at roughly US$4.5 billion for the construction. This specific site was meant to produce high-bandwidth memory and DRAM for the global market. The news arrived while the market for high-bandwidth memory remains unusually tight for many buyers.

The paused project in Taiwan required roughly US$4.5 billion to produce high-bandwidth memory and DRAM. Micron announced on November 12, 2026, that executives would attend upcoming investor events to meet shareholders. One such event is the TomorrowX Summit in Austin, Texas, on November 18 at 10:50 a.m. Mountain Time. The report from November 6, 2026, is the primary source for the details regarding the facility pause.

No available source identifies the meaning of a reference called US-Li mentioned in a headline fragment. Micron has not provided a confirmed reason for the pause or a statement on the length of time. The company did not tie the decision to policy, cost, or demand in any attributable on-record statement. Executives are scheduled to appear at the TomorrowX Summit, but the notice was routine corporate scheduling. This notice did not mention the Taiwan facility or suggest a response to the November 6 report.

Management may be pressed on spending, timing, and supply during the upcoming public appearance in Texas. AI server builders and gamers who feel DRAM pricing effects are among those affected by the pause. Buyers have little spare room because SK hynix locked up over half of 2027-28 HBM4 capacity. Toolmakers and contractors may reshuffle their schedules, which could potentially speed up the timelines of rival chipmakers.

Local governments in Taiwan may need to revisit hiring targets, infrastructure plans, and various project incentives. The pause removes a future flexibility point for moving capacity between HBM and ordinary DRAM production. The memory industry is a cyclical business where prices rise during shortages and fall when capacity floods in. Three companies, Micron, Samsung, and SK hynix, dominate the global supply of DRAM and high-bandwidth memory.

High-bandwidth memory is scarce because it consumes more wafer area than standard DRAM and adds yield risk. Counterpoint reported third-quarter growth at 369 percent, which was driven by rising prices and AI memory demand. A federal judge recently allowed a DRAM price-fixing suit to proceed, though it is unrelated to this. Analysts will parse the November 18 appearance for hints about the direction of the company's capital spending.

Investors want to know if the pause is a total cancellation or just a temporary timing delay. It remains open whether Micron will add this lost capacity at other sites or change customer commitments. The articles leave open whether the company will change its outlook on its share of the HBM market. No source has established the identity of US-Li or its connection to the memory maker.
