stories.Headline: IBM and Microsoft launch Imagine Enterprise with over 6,000 IBM Consulting AI agents and assets
stories.Summary:
IBM and Microsoft announced Imagine Enterprise, an AI agent platform, in a joint announcement posted to both companies' newsrooms on Nov. 10, 2026. The platform pairs IBM Consulting's more than 6,000 pre-built AI agents and assets with Microsoft's AI, data, cloud and security foundation. It gives enterprises a way to build, govern and run AI agents that support people carrying out industry-specific processes. Regulated industries are a particular focus of the offering. The launch customer is a financial services firm.

Imagine Enterprise starts with more than 6,000 AI agents and assets from IBM Consulting, a number the release gives without splitting agents from assets. Microsoft provides Microsoft Foundry, GitHub Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Studio for coordinating agents and enterprise systems. Its foundation covers Microsoft Fabric, Microsoft 365 infrastructure, Microsoft Entra, Microsoft Purview, Microsoft Defender and Microsoft Azure for data, identity, AI governance, security and cloud. IBM Consulting's agents are built on IBM Consulting Advantage, whose Process Studio, Context Studio and Advantage Core help organizations design, deploy and govern tailored agents. At launch, industry-specific frameworks cover financial services, insurance and retail, with manufacturing, energy, public sector and mobility named as possible later extensions.

Forward-deployed engineers from both companies support qualifying engagements, helping customers move from experimentation into production. Clients can get the platform in three ways: hand IBM Consulting the job of deploying and running it, co-innovate with IBM Consulting on enterprise-scale implementations, or choose self-management options. Mohamad Ali, senior vice president and head of IBM Consulting, said clients have stopped looking for AI that only lets people do existing work slightly faster. He said they now want an agentic business that brings human expertise and digital labor together at enterprise scale. Rodrigo Kede Lima, president of Microsoft Frontier Company, said organizations that win at enterprise AI will be the ones able to put their data, industry expertise and AI to work in action.

SEI, which provides financial technology, operations and asset management services, is exploring emerging and agentic technologies with IBM Consulting and Microsoft's support. SEI manages, advises or administers approximately $2 trillion in assets as of Sept. 30, 2026, according to its boilerplate in the release. Sneha Shah, SEI's chief AI strategist and head of SEI Next, said AI is evolving quickly and SEI's focus is on applying it with intention to strengthen trust and enhance human decision-making. She said the work lets SEI explore whether new capabilities might support critical processes and then grow responsibly over time. The release states no price for the platform.

A March 2025 arXiv survey of AI agents by Naveen Krishnan describes hierarchical agents, in which higher-level agents break complex tasks into smaller ones and hand them to lower-level agents that report progress back. The survey lists enterprise automation platforms that coordinate across specialized subsystems among its examples and names reconciling financial statements among complex tasks AI agents can take on. It cites Kapoor et al. (2024) to argue that agent benchmarks often focus narrowly on accuracy without enough attention to cost-effectiveness, reproducibility and real-world applicability. Jeff Defilippi, Arm's senior director of product management, argued that a single agent task can chain model calls, retrieval, database transactions, code execution, tool calls and state changes. Defilippi told The Next Platform that many agentic workflows have both a latency problem and a concurrency problem, and said successful task completion is the meaningful unit of performance.

Defilippi said that at low concurrency, waiting on a dependency has a large effect on an individual task's completion time, and that as more agents run at once, throughput and scheduling efficiency take over. Arm's advice is to test under realistic load and concurrency rather than relying on lightly loaded peak results. The Arm feature is sponsored, and Arm has a stake in how CPUs get judged. The release frames the platform as the alternative to starting from scratch, replacing platforms a firm already depends on, or spending months assembling the pieces itself. It says the platform connects to existing data, processes, systems and technology so a firm can start where it is and scale over time.

The articles suggest a pilot should pick one named process and agree on how it will be scored, using wall-clock completion time and success rate as more agents run at once alongside component metrics that explain any slowdown. They suggest a completion-time baseline taken before engineers arrive is the cleanest way to show whether adapted agents complete real work inside the firm's own data and controls. The release does not split its count of more than 6,000 agents and assets, so the number describes the size of IBM Consulting's starting library rather than a count of deployable agents. The release gives no price and does not say how many qualifying engagements exist or what qualifies. It does not state when the later industry frameworks might arrive.

stories.Headline: Protesters across four continents urge Trump and Xi to negotiate a treaty to stop the AI race
stories.Summary:
Roughly 150 demonstrators marched from the OpenAI headquarters to Veterans Plaza in San Francisco on November 14, 2026. This event was part of a coordinated effort involving approximately 20 cities across North America, South America, Europe, Africa, and Oceania. The protesters demanded that U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping negotiate a binding international treaty to stop the artificial intelligence race. They urged the leaders to discuss this issue during a planned November 19 meeting with Vladimir Putin at the APEC summit in Shenzhen.

The proposed agreement, created by the Machine Intelligence Research Institute's Technical Governance Team, seeks to halt the development of superintelligence until specific risks are managed. This framework would restrict the scale of AI training through FLOP thresholds and verify compliance by tracking the use of AI chips. The movement draws inspiration from the 2025 book by Nate Soares and Eliezer Yudkowsky titled If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies. These measures aim to prevent the creation of systems more cognitively capable than humans before safety can be guaranteed.

Founder Michaël Trazzi stated that he fears powerful AI could kill people before his young niece is old enough to speak. Former software engineer Zack M. Davis explained that individual companies or nations cannot stop alone without risking a competitive disadvantage. While the CEOs of Google DeepMind, Anthropic, and OpenAI signed a statement calling AI extinction a global priority, their firms continue developing advanced systems. Conversely, the Trump administration has focused on winning the global competition rather than accepting binding international restrictions.

The APEC summit is scheduled for November 18 and 19 in Shenzhen, marking the third meeting between Trump and Xi in 2026. While negotiators have focused on chips, rare earths, and Taiwan, the Stop The AI Race movement wants governance added to the agenda. The White House and Kremlin have already confirmed the trilateral meeting between Trump, Xi, and Putin. It remains unknown if either leader will present a concrete proposal regarding AI during these diplomatic discussions.

stories.Headline: Oracle cuts about 21000 jobs as AI adoption reshapes its workforce
stories.Summary:
Technology companies eliminated more than 200,000 positions worldwide in 2026, according to trackers such as TrueUp, as organizations restructured operations, trimmed costs, and redirected capital toward artificial intelligence infrastructure and capabilities. The United States accounted for the bulk of that activity. Many announcements explicitly or implicitly linked the cuts to AI adoption, elevated infrastructure spending, and the need to free resources for machine learning investments. Totals kept climbing with November announcements, exceeding the pace of earlier months even as overall U.S. announced cuts remained below 2025 levels in some broader measures. Oracle recorded the biggest single decline, with headcount falling by approximately 21,000, about 13 percent of its workforce, over the preceding year, and its annual filing noted that AI adoption contributed to the cuts while the company expanded spending on AI infrastructure, chips, and data centers.

Amazon eliminated roughly 16,000 corporate roles early in the year to reduce management layers, increase ownership, and cut bureaucracy, with additional smaller reductions later in stores and devices units. Meta cut about 8,000 positions, roughly 10 percent of its workforce, in May, canceled plans for approximately 6,000 additional hires, and recognized over $1 billion in related severance, while budgeting capital expenditures of $135, 145 billion for 2026, nearly double prior levels, primarily for AI infrastructure. PayPal reduced roughly 4,760 positions amid a multi-year transformation under new CEO Enrique Lores aimed at simplifying operations, removing management layers, and targeting at least $1.5 billion in annualized savings. Uber eliminated 3,300 jobs, about 10 percent of staff, to remove layers, simplify structures, and refocus investments, with earlier reductions in customer service tied to AI adoption. Microsoft cut about 4,800 roles mid-year and later offered voluntary buyouts to as many as 60,000 employees across divisions including Xbox, Windows, and finance amid elevated AI spending.

Canva reduced or relocated more than 1,200 positions, 22 percent of staff, while reorganizing product, growth, and platform teams to reduce specialization. Squarespace laid off about 300 employees, 19 percent of its workforce, to simplify operations and sharpen priorities in a market increasingly shaped by AI-assisted website tools. Netflix planned roughly 1,000 reductions, about 6 percent of staff, citing the need to prioritize resources amid slower engagement growth. Block conducted further cuts after earlier reductions exceeding 4,000, affecting Cash App and Square teams as part of ongoing AI-related restructuring. Additional reductions appeared at Apple, in Vision Pro and related groups plus Fitness+, at Dropbox, at Electronic Arts, and at others, often citing cost controls or shifting priorities rather than pure automation.

Meta's reductions hit support functions, non-AI product teams, integrity, and cybersecurity areas hardest, and an internal initiative exploring deeper team reductions, up to 60 percent in some scenarios through layoffs, redeployments, and unfilled roles, was scaled back after employee pushback and questions about realized productivity gains, with a planned second wave canceled. Smaller earlier Meta cuts occurred in Reality Labs as resources shifted toward AI wearables and features. PayPal reported more than 2,000 cuts and a greater than 25 percent reduction in managerial roles supporting near-term cost goals, while expanding AI use in areas such as customer service agents, and a third-quarter workforce reduction produced $152 million in restructuring charges. PayPal's international effects included approximately 220 roles in India, about 4 percent of local staff and lower than some initial reports, plus cuts in Ireland, Israel, and U.S. headquarters, and the firm has not disclosed a single comprehensive global figure but confirmed ongoing restructuring.

A recent analysis from Goldman Sachs indicated that workers displaced from AI-exposed roles since 2025 face longer reemployment timelines, roughly a month more than other laid-off workers, and are about 10 percentage points more likely to remain unemployed a year later. Goldman described these effects as mirroring patterns from prior waves of technological change over the last four decades, leaving long-lasting scars through slower earnings recovery and elevated risks of further unemployment. Separate projections warned that if tech-driven reductions spill into retail, finance, and other sectors, they could trigger an additional 1.6 million U.S. job losses, pushing unemployment closer to recession thresholds even as the broader economy has so far avoided formal contraction. A sharp technology selloff erased year-to-date gains at many hedge funds, with tech-focused equity long-short strategies falling more than 4 percent in a single session and ending roughly flat for 2026 after peaking near 24 percent earlier in the year.

Some multi-strategy platforms responded by cutting leverage, reducing investment teams, and parting ways with underperforming groups, with further staff reductions anticipated if declines persist. Trackers showed layoffs accelerating relative to 2025 in technology, with AI cited in a substantial share of announcements even as companies frequently listed multiple factors including reorganization and investment reallocation. While profitable firms dominated many large cuts, the combination of infrastructure spending, productivity assumptions, and market reactions continued to reshape workforces. The company has not framed every cut as AI-specific but continues heavy investment in the technology.

stories.Headline: Microsoft Copilot AI predicts Hyperliquid HYPE could reach $280 to $380 by January 2027
stories.Summary:
Microsoft Copilot AI predicted on November 15, 2026, that Hyperliquid's HYPE token could reach between $280 and $380 by January 1, 2027, with a stretch target above $450 in the most aggressive outcome. The prediction was reported by Ahmed Barakat in a cryptonews.com article last updated November 15, 2026. Hyperliquid was trading near $65 to $68 in mid-November 2026 after pulling back with the broader market. HYPE had corrected sharply from its late-October highs near $95 to $96 and was consolidating in the mid-$60s after testing support around $62 to $64. The article called the forecast pure speculation and entertainment, not a realistic base-case outlook.

The scenario requires Hyperliquid to obtain a major U.S. regulatory designation allowing its perpetual futures platform, or a closely affiliated entity, to operate as a fully compliant onshore derivatives venue accessible to a wide range of traditional finance participants. It also requires a surge in institutional volume migrating onto the chain and aggressive token utility expansions such as enhanced staking, revenue sharing or treasury mechanisms. Immediate resistance was clustered between $72 and $78, with a more significant supply zone near the prior peak. The $60 to $62 area represented the first major demand zone, and a sustained break below it would open the path toward the $50 region. A weekly close back above $75 to $80 would signal in a standard recovery that the corrective phase was ending.

The article stated that the catalyst would require extraordinary regulatory progress and execution for Hyperliquid at a scale that is currently highly unlikely. It described the regulatory and institutional breakthrough as highly unlikely but not impossible. It said the forecast remains pure speculation and entertainment, not a realistic base-case outlook. It said present price action reflects broader risk-off conditions and recent liquidations. It said Hyperliquid's position as a high-volume perpetual exchange continues to give it a distinct profile among large-cap tokens.

The article said momentum indicators had cooled considerably after the sell-off, leaving the asset oversold on intermediate timeframes and creating room for a sharp reversal if buying pressure returns. It said the combination of Hyperliquid's existing product-market fit and the theoretical potential for a transformative regulatory green light creates a setup from which a parabolic move remains possible. It said that under the extreme regulatory and institutional catalyst, intermediate levels would be cleared rapidly, allowing measured-move extensions and multi-cycle projections from the current base to support a far more aggressive upside trajectory. The article was fact checked by the CryptoNews Editorial Team. It carried a disclaimer that crypto is a high-risk asset class and that readers could lose all of their capital.

The article listed market prices alongside the prediction: BTC at $65,088.92, ETH at $1,822.50, SOL at $72.08, PEPE at $0.0000038, SHIB at $0.0000039, DOGE at $0.059 and XRP at $0.96, with ETH gas at 0.16 gwei. It gave a market cap of $2,779,914,586,326. It said Cryptonews was founded in 2017 and has 2M+ active monthly users around the world. It said the site has 250+ guides and reviews articles, 8 years on the market and 70 international team authors. It said Ahmed Barakat is a journalist and copywriter based in Georgia.

The article said the recent decline had formed a series of lower highs. It said the landmark catalyst driving the extreme upside is a highly unlikely but not impossible regulatory and institutional breakthrough. It said HYPE could still deliver one of the more explosive moves among major DeFi assets by January 1, 2027. It said the structural demand shock would re-rate the entire project far beyond current valuations. It said the prediction is an over-the-top bullish scenario.

The article did not state whether Microsoft Copilot AI gave any further reasoning beyond the scenario it outlined. It did not state any response from Hyperliquid or from Microsoft. It did not state what would happen to the forecast if the regulatory designation were refused. It did not give a date for when any regulatory decision might come. It did not state whether the $450 stretch target had any separate conditions attached.

stories.Headline: Empa researchers Turlo and Hu launch OptiMat Alloys, an AI agent that runs alloy simulations from plain text
stories.Summary:
Vladyslav Turlo and Yang Hu, researchers at Empa, developed an AI agent called OptiMat Alloys that can operate the complex computational tools of materials science and is controlled through simple text input, according to a Newswise article dated November 17, 2026. The tool is accessed through the OptiMat Chat platform, which lets scientists download an "AI materials scientist" onto their own computer. The agent selects appropriate domain-specific tools, executes predefined workflows, and summarizes results in publication-style figures, tables, and texts for experts to review. Users need neither to code nor to configure complicated settings, and they can formulate their query in plain language just as they would with a real computational materials scientist or with ChatGPT.

The work targets high-entropy alloys, novel materials made of four or more metals mixed together in roughly equal proportions, which have promising mechanical, thermal, and electromagnetic properties for uses ranging from structural and high-temperature materials to functional coatings, catalysis, and electronic or magnetic components. Hu, from Empa's Advanced Metallurgy & Manufacturing of Metals laboratory in Thun, said there are an extremely large number of possible combinations and that traditional methods of producing and examining a few varieties quickly reach their limits. Turlo, from Empa's Computational Engineering lab, said experimental materials scientists do not have the time to learn how to use the computational tools. At the heart of OptiMat Alloys is an AI agent that interacts with different domain-specific tools, and its results are stored in a database for traceability, reuse, and future benchmarking or refinement.

The researchers designed the agent to use their simulation tools for high-entropy alloys according to best-practice protocols, and they focused on reliability, traceability, and human oversight. The agent is designed to reduce hallucinations by using structured tool calls, predefined computational workflows, and stored calculation records, so the scientific outputs come from connected computational tools, databases, and validated procedures rather than from the large language model alone. Turlo cautioned that they by no means recommend creating scientific publications based solely on this data, and that the data are intended as starting points for expert interpretation and experimental planning rather than as standalone publishable scientific results. Hu said the agents handle routine calculations, which gives the researchers more time to focus on the truly interesting research questions, and Turlo added that computational materials science is a relatively young field with an extraordinary amount still to explore.

The researchers plan to add further agents to OptiMat Chat in future, such as those for ceramics and metal oxides or for amorphous materials, which will make the powerful tools of computational materials science more accessible in these areas as well. They see AI assisting with literature reviews, designing experiments, and generating data, while human experts will still be needed to interpret and validate that data. Turlo summarized that AI may be able to predict whether material A or material B is better for property C, but only human experts can dig deeper, validate, and explain why that is the case.

stories.Headline: Anthropic develops AI systems about twice as fast as a year ago, METR finds
stories.Summary:
Anthropic is reportedly developing its artificial intelligence systems around twice as quickly as it was a year ago, according to an analysis released Thursday by an independent monitoring group. The Berkeley, California-based nonprofit Model Evaluation and Threat Research reviewed Anthropic's internal data and interviewed staff. Anthropic invited the researchers as it prepares for its Wall Street debut. The findings were released amid debate over the potential for AI models to elude human control with catastrophic consequences. The analysis was reported by Scripps News on November 15, 2026.

METR's assessment was based on about 11 weeks of Anthropic's internal data, from mid-August through late October, as well as employee interviews. METR said it was given "unprecedented access to internal data" on Anthropic's AI research and development process. The group said Anthropic's redactions limited how it could communicate more detailed estimates of acceleration. METR also reviewed a public risk report Anthropic published in August and a private version, and said the public report "overall understates the level of acceleration that was occurring." METR said Anthropic appears to have made as much progress on benchmarks in the past year as between October 2023 and October 2025.

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for the AI industry to slow its work so safety measures can catch up during the research group's assessment period. In a Sept. 12 essay, he urged the AI world to "slow the pace at which we improve the capabilities of AI models." Co-founder Sam McCandlish said in a lengthy post on X Thursday that many of METR's conclusions match his own, writing that "AI is speeding up our research, but it's hard to say exactly how much." McCandlish, also Anthropic's chief architect, said the company plans to release a report with its own analysis of the speed of AI progress within Anthropic in the coming weeks. He said sharing "exactly what is driving the speedup isn't the right thing to do" because it is "commercially sensitive" and "risks handing out a roadmap for others to go faster."

METR said it believed much of the reason for the faster development is the help of AI itself, and Anthropic has said its Claude chatbot increasingly helps the company develop newer versions of itself. METR said it could confidently rule out the growth of computing power used in training AI models as the reason for the acceleration. The researchers said there were no "bottlenecks" such as restrictions on computing power or data holding back Anthropic's AI progress. METR said Anthropic researchers described significant "signs of life" implying AI could soon make highly significant and fully autonomous contributions to model training.

The San Francisco-based company is planning to go public later this month in what could be the biggest initial public offering of stock ever. METR has conducted evaluations on model capabilities for Anthropic, OpenAI and other labs for years. The nonprofit is funded through donations and does not accept compensation for its work, but AI companies it has partnered with have provided access and tokens. The findings are significant because details about the technology and its risks have been provided primarily by AI companies, which have been encouraged by President Donald Trump's administration to police themselves on matters of safety.

Amodei's September essay said AI advances have been driven primarily by recursive self-improvement, which he defined as "AI's growing ability to build the next generation of AI." In that essay, Amodei championed external evaluators embedded within leading AI labs and highlighted METR as an appropriate third-party evaluator. McCandlish said the work with METR began "well before and is separate from the embedded third-party evaluators that are part of our commitment to pacing the frontier." He added that "it's a good illustration of why we think evaluators are a good idea."

McCandlish acknowledged the redactions make it harder for others to "check METR's work," and said the company continues to weigh the pros and cons. METR said it could be overstating its findings because the acceleration might be limited to "well-specified tasks" that can be graded automatically or with a language model. METR said there were some internal disagreements and uncertainty among its team, but the group said it believed the company's rate of improvement had doubled. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said at the time that he also supported the idea of independent evaluators with employee-like access.

stories.Headline: NVIDIA, SK Telecom and Rebellions sign sovereign AI infrastructure agreement in Seoul
stories.Summary:
On November 9, 2026, at NVIDIA AI Day Seoul at the COEX convention centre in Gangnam District, Seoul, NVIDIA, SK Telecom and Rebellions signed a strategic memorandum of understanding to build sovereign AI infrastructure. Rebellions Chief Executive Officer Sunghyun Park, SK Telecom Chief Technology Officer Chung Suk-geun, Ashish Karandikar, Vice President of NVIDIA’s NVLink Fusion division, and SK Telecom President and CEO Jung Jai-hun attended. The initiative is backed by South Korea’s Ministry of Science and ICT under Deputy Prime Minister and Minister Bae Kyung-hoon. Rebellions will connect its next-generation Rebel R200 neural processing units to NVIDIA’s computing platform via the NVIDIA NVLink Fusion interconnect. Rebellions will develop rack-scale inference systems based on the NVIDIA MGX modular server architecture, while SK Telecom will deploy and validate the hardware across its domestic AI data centres.

SK Telecom plans to pair the heterogeneous systems with its proprietary foundation models, including A.X K2, and public-facing services under the government’s ‘AI for All’ project. The partners target commercial deployment of the integrated Rebel R200 systems in 2028. NVIDIA GPUs execute the compute-heavy prefill stage, while Rebellions’ Rebel R200 NPUs run the decode stage. NVLink Fusion is a scale-up interconnect allowing custom third-party ASICs and XPUs to communicate directly with NVIDIA GPUs and CPUs at NVLink bandwidth within a server rack. MGX provides standardized rack footprints, liquid cooling paths, and power distribution compatible with Open Compute Project standards, giving Rebellions access to established original design manufacturer supply chains.

Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of NVIDIA, said sovereign AI gives nations the power to turn their language, culture and expertise into intelligence. Sunghyun Park, cofounder and CEO of Rebellions, said the announcement marks a turning point, opening a new chapter for sovereign AI by connecting Korea’s AI silicon and models with global systems technology. Jung Jai-hun, President and CEO of SK Telecom, said linking SKT’s AI data centers, proprietary AI models including A.X K2, and public-facing AI services developed under the ‘AI for All’ project will strengthen full-stack sovereign AI competitiveness. Bae Kyung-hoon, South Korea Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Science and ICT, said the collaboration enables Korean-developed NPUs to enter the computing infrastructure market alongside NVIDIA through NVLink Fusion. Bae said the government will actively support this collaboration to deliver tangible results.

The disaggregated GPU-NPU model directly impacts academic high-performance computing centres, national laboratories, and university research computing divisions. Academic facilities face strict power and cooling ceilings, and running monolithic GPU clusters for conversational models wastes energy on memory-bound decoding loops. Offloading token generation to energy-optimized NPUs advances institutional goals for sustainable HPC by reducing power consumption per token while maintaining low inference latency. For AI systems researchers, NVLink Fusion offers an accessible environment for investigating heterogeneous memory hierarchies, KV-cache transfers, and mixed-precision execution without proprietary interconnect barriers. As research funding agencies increasingly demand environmental audits, calculating a rigorous compute FLOPs estimate alongside token-per-watt throughput will be vital for grant compliance.

Sovereign AI infrastructure allows universities to safeguard sensitive research assets, including clinical health records, genomic datasets, and proprietary patent disclosures. Serving models on domestic sovereign clouds complies with strict data protection mandates and aligns with broader national data infrastructure standards. Researchers deploying split architectures must record firmware and runtime configurations carefully to guarantee a reproducible AI experiment across heterogeneous clusters. The tripartite alliance follows SK Telecom’s June 2026 agreement with NVIDIA to construct gigawatt-scale AI factories in South Korea using NVIDIA’s DSX modular architecture, with an initial facility planned for 2027. Founded in 2020, Rebellions previously developed the Atom NPU and its flagship Rebel R100, which featured a chiplet architecture using fifth-generation high-bandwidth memory.

The consortium has outlined a four-stage roadmap toward production readiness. In 2026, 2027, Rebellions and NVIDIA will finalize the Rebel R200 physical design and validate NVLink Fusion signaling inside prototype NVIDIA MGX chassis. In 2027, SK Telecom will deploy prototype MGX systems within its domestic AI data centres to evaluate power efficiency, thermal stability, and performance on A.X K2 models. In 2028, commercial deployment of Rebel R200 rack systems will begin in SK Telecom data centres, supporting public services under ‘AI for All’ and offering compute to universities and enterprises. Following domestic validation, the consortium plans to market the MGX sovereign AI infrastructure package to global telecom operators and sovereign cloud providers.

stories.Headline: Microsoft opens a digital innovation center in Kuwait with the government to scale trusted AI adoption
stories.Summary:
Microsoft announced on 15 November 2026 the opening of the Microsoft Digital Innovation Center (MDIC) in Kuwait, established through a partnership between Microsoft and the State of Kuwait government. The center is designed to connect trusted technology, government priorities, customer challenges and the local innovation ecosystem in one collaborative environment. Government entities, customers, startups, developers and students will be able to experience Microsoft's AI, cloud, cybersecurity and digital capabilities firsthand there. They can also explore relevant use cases, build skills and identify pathways from ideas to implementation, according to the announcement.

The MDIC is meant to support Kuwait as it moves from AI experimentation toward trusted adoption at scale, with a growing focus on practical outcomes, national capability and long-term competitiveness. Developing national talent will be central to its mission, with pathways for citizens, government employees, students, developers and startups to build practical AI skills. Hands-on experiences will include workshops, demonstrations, open-house sessions, developer engagement and student-focused programming. The opening is described as the latest example of Microsoft's long-term commitment to Kuwait and its support for the country's digital transformation under New Kuwait Vision 2035.

Omar Saud Abdulaziz Al-Omar, Kuwait's Minister of State for Communications and Information Technology, said the center represents an important step toward a knowledge-based, AI-powered economy. He said stronger collaboration between government, technology leaders and national talent creates the environment needed to turn AI's potential into tangible outcomes for institutions, the economy and people. Naim Yazbeck, President of Microsoft Middle East and Africa, said Kuwait has a clear ambition to use AI as a driver of economic growth, better public services and new opportunities. He said the center is about helping turn that ambition into action and helping organizations move beyond experimenting with AI to delivering meaningful impact at scale.

Alaeddine Karim, General Manager at Microsoft, said the center reflects the company's long-term commitment to Kuwait and that its focus is not technology for technology's sake. He said the aim is to work alongside government, businesses and the ecosystem to solve real challenges, build local capabilities and translate AI into meaningful outcomes. He said Microsoft wants the MDIC to be where ideas move into action and where organizations can confidently take the next step in their AI journey. The announcement did not give a specific opening date beyond 15 November 2026, nor did it name further next steps.

stories.Headline: Google Cloud opens applications for a 15-week sovereign AI accelerator for European and Israeli startups
stories.Summary:
Google Cloud announced on November 17, 2026 an open call for applications to its Google for Startups Accelerator: Sovereign AI, which is available in Europe and Israel and supports startups building AI solutions for European regulatory environments. The announcement was made by Giorgia Abeltino, Head of Government Affairs and Public Policy for Google Cloud Europe, Middle East and Africa. The program is described as equity-free and runs for 15 weeks in a hybrid format with virtual and in-person sessions. Applications close on January 15, 2027, and founders can apply on the Google for Startups Accelerator page.

The accelerator is aimed at a small, high-touch cohort of late-seed to post Series A startups headquartered across Europe and Israel with strong traction that use AI for sensitive, regulated workloads. Target areas include government and public service technologies such as sovereign document processing and citizen service portals, with defense applications excluded, as well as healthcare and life sciences, regulated finance, and cybersecurity and data trust. Selected startups receive architectural mentorship, one-to-one pairing with Google Cloud engineers, and advisory support to prepare for EU AI Act Regulatory Sandboxes. Participants also get support to deploy across Google Cloud's tiered sovereign portfolio, from regional data controls and external key management to partner-operated clouds such as S3NS in France and Thales in Germany and fully air-gapped Google Distributed Cloud environments.

Abeltino wrote that artificial intelligence represents an estimated €1.2 trillion economic opportunity for Europe, and that enterprises and public institutions need advanced AI while meeting data governance requirements including the EU AI Act, NIS2, DORA, and national frameworks such as SecNumCloud and BSI's cloud security and sovereignty principles. She said the program wants founders to build in Europe with solutions made in Europe, and that digital sovereignty for startups should not mean settling for second-rate tools or lock-in to a single rigid stack. She described co-engineering with Europe's tech ecosystem so founders can scale on their own terms from day one, for instance by combining Gemini models, open-weight models like Gemma and Mistral, and verifiable data residency and cryptographic controls delivered with local European sovereign partners. Past participants, quoted in the post, said access to Google Cloud engineers who understand sovereign and regulated constraints saves young companies time and that the program helps build compliance answers into architecture from day one.

stories.Headline: CERT-In flags low severity emBridge flaw and eMudhra removes file browsing functions to fix it
stories.Summary:
CERT-In issued a vulnerability note on November 13 about eMudhra's emBridge digital signature utility, a client-side application that lets web portals communicate with digital signature certificates and hardware tokens installed on a user's computer. The agency said the flaw could let unauthorised entities on the same local area network access file and directory names on an affected device, and it classified the threat as low severity. Cybersecurity expert Karan Saini reported the vulnerability to CERT-In. CERT-In stated that file-browsing functions within the interface did not verify whether requests came from an authorised source, and that these functions operate with the highest system privileges on Windows.

An attacker on the same local network could use a malicious webpage to send requests to emBridge and map out file and folder names on the targeted machine. The affected versions are 5.9.1.x to 5.9.3.x on Windows, 3.2.4.x to 3.2.6.x on macOS, and 3.2.0.x to 3.3.0.x on Ubuntu and Red Hat Linux. CERT-In advised users to upgrade to version 5.9.4.x or later on Windows, 3.2.7.x or later on macOS, and 3.3.1.x or later on Linux. Several government portals, including the Ministry of Corporate Affairs' MCA V3 portal, the Directorate General of Foreign Trade and the National Single Window System, rely on emBridge for DSC-based signing, and the Income Tax Department also recommends it for managing DSCs.

The agency confirmed that the flaw does not provide access to file contents, permit changes or deletions, allow code execution, or expose cryptographic keys or token PINs. eMudhra published its own advisory on the CVE and said it fixed the issue on November 11, two days before CERT-In's note, by removing the file-browsing functions from emBridge entirely. The company said that with these endpoints removed the file enumeration capability is no longer available through emBridge, and it rated the flaw's impact and risk as low. An attack would also require several conditions at once, including an affected emBridge version, a malicious webpage on the same local network, the user opening it, and a browser without Local Network Access restrictions.

The company added that its firewall and local-only request handling block direct access from other machines. Saini posted on X that while the bug was trivial, eMudhra's own advisory had further downplayed it. eMudhra told Inc42 that every digital signature certificate requires the user to enter a token PIN before use, and it pointed out that CERT-In's note confirmed keys and token PINs had not been exposed. A company spokesperson said identifying and fixing vulnerabilities is a routine part of responsible software development, and added that large global vendors like Microsoft, Oracle, Google and Adobe addressed thousands of vulnerabilities every month. The incident follows a major cybersecurity event in October where weak private keys for eMudhra's intermediate certificate authority certificates were reported.

stories.Headline: Michael Anello shows how Drupal developers cut AI token costs with browser models and metering
stories.Summary:
Sessions at NEDCamp 2026 explored how developers can manage the costs and keep control of AI features built into Drupal sites, and speakers said cost and control should be treated as design inputs from the very start of a project. Michael Anello, in a session on Drupal AI modules worth knowing about, said Chrome's built-in model can be reached through developer settings and used by Drupal through the AI Browser Provider module, which cuts token costs for everyday summarising and drafting. He also demonstrated AI Metering, a tool that tracks token usage, estimates costs and enforces per-user monthly quotas. That module allows a local fallback provider such as Ollama when limits are reached, which offers an alternative to blocking editor requests, and the choice between blocking and falling back has a significant impact on the user experience.

Jacob Rockowitz, in a talk titled AI ate my Work, and I'm okay with that, discussed optimising coding agents by giving them small and predictable toolsets. He uses Git worktrees and custom DDEV commands as isolated playgrounds for agents, an approach that avoids hardcoded paths and reduces token spending by keeping agent context light. Jim Birch presented a company-wide AI governance system in his session on guardrails, governance and proof that a team still owns the work. His agency uses a PREP framework, meaning purpose, risk, evidence and person, to scope each AI use case, and the system includes a harness for tools, approved tools that do not train on company data, and managed settings. Birch also introduced ownership, where each AI-assisted piece of work receives a delivery record, a YAML file detailing the producer, reviewer, approvals and model used, which answers client questions about verification.

Fredric Mitchell, in a session on defending budgets, addressed budget defence in an AI-driven landscape and noted that AI overviews are eroding organic search traffic, which makes it harder to justify platform budgets based on traffic metrics. He proposed the Web Operations Maturity Model, a rubric that scores platform health across six areas, as an alternative. Ethan Marcotte's keynote, The Work We Want, explored the broader societal impact of AI and framed it within Ursula Franklin's stages of technology. Marcotte argued that AI is institutionalising control with a few firms, likening it to the historical trajectory of the sewing machine, and he suggested that AI limits function best when editors help set them, which gives those editors more control over their work.

stories.Headline: Peter Ward says profitability traps stop managed service providers adopting AI
stories.Summary:
Peter Ward, managing director of Dijital Team, told ARN that many managed service providers are caught in profitability traps such as underpriced agreements, hidden delivery costs and expanding service obligations, which limit their ability to experiment and adopt AI. He said industry data shows the average net profit for providers is 6 per cent, and that 25 per cent of MSPs are financially underwater and not making any money at all. Ward said service gross margin is the biggest driver in the MSP space, and that getting it right means everything flows through to the bottom line. He added that operating expenses in any IT business are fairly constant, so providers need to get the costs of tooling, labour and delivery right.

Ward said profitability is a key lever because the more profitable a business is, the more it can invest and grow, and that profit is needed to experiment. He said many organisations have moved from break fix to managed services and felt the impact of cloud, and now need to re-engineer and reskill to succeed in AI, which is very hard without a profitable business. He also said that for every extra $1 an MSP puts on its bottom line, it means $5 extra when the business is sold, which matters amid significant merger and acquisition volumes in the market. Ward's insights came from Dijital Team's conversations with thousands of MSPs at events and conferences, and he launched his book The IT Sales Playbook over 12 months ago.

Ward said many MSPs followed the processes in that book and built their ability to acquire new customers, which led him to write The MSP Profitability Playbook to help organisations turn back into profitability. The book includes diagnostic tools, practical worksheets, an owner scorecard and a structured approach to implementing changes over a 90-day period. He said that if all the boats in the harbour can be lifted, the tide rises together and that helps create a great outcome for everybody. In May, Dijital Team launched its Better Business Pathway enablement program, developed by customer enablement manager Diana Drury, which focuses on five operational challenges: service, finance, people, sales and go-to-market operations. Drury said at the time that the MSP and technology service provider market needed guidance along those five pathways, and that one of the biggest pain points she has heard is the unspoken struggle to figure out all of the shiny stuff and how to get it into a business and make it better.

Articles.Title: Profitability traps holding MSPs back from experimentation and AI

stories.Headline: Mohammed Bin Rashid School of Government launches fourth AI ethics cohort with IEEE
stories.Summary:
The Mohammed Bin Rashid School of Government launched its fourth executive education cohort recently. This programme focuses on artificial intelligence ethics in the age of agentic AI. The school collaborated with the IEEE Standards Association and its own research centre. Registration is now open for professionals to join this pioneering training initiative. The course will take place from 23 to 26 November 2026.

The training occurs at the MBRSG premises located in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. It prepares students for the IEEE CertifAIEd certification as an AI Ethics Professional. The curriculum covers accountability, transparency, privacy, and algorithmic bias through four days of training. A specialized workshop is scheduled for 20 November 2026 during Dubai Future Week. The programme supports a UAE goal to deploy agentic AI across 50% of government sectors.

Executive President Dr. Ali bin Sebaa Al Marri is responsible for the school. He stated that expanding agentic AI adoption requires governance frameworks that keep pace with technology. He noted that enhancing public sector talent ensures these technologies are deployed responsibly. Al Marri said building capacity to navigate transformations is a central pillar of the mission. He believes these efforts align with the Annual Government Challenge launched by Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid.

The programme targets government leaders, policymakers, and strategic planners from public and private sectors. It also affects governance, risk, and compliance officers and specialists in data and digital transformation. These professionals will learn to evaluate autonomous systems against international standards to identify risks. Participants will use ethical frameworks to support the safe deployment of these intelligent systems. The training helps them integrate ethical considerations when designing agentic AI within their organizations.

The school aims to strengthen national capabilities in AI governance within the public sector. This mission drives public policy development and aligns executive education with current technological shifts. The programme uses the globally recognized IEEE CertifAIEd standard for evaluating autonomous system ethics. It includes practical case studies on implementing generative and agentic AI within the UAE. These efforts reinforce governance practices rooted in accountability, transparency, and privacy protection.

Participants will receive a completion certificate from the school after finishing the four days. They may then pursue the IEEE CertifAIEd certification by fulfilling professional experience criteria. Candidates must also pass an IEEE accredited examination to become certified AI Ethics Professionals. The articles do not state the total cost of the registration for the cohort. They also leave open the specific number of professionals who will enroll in the programme.

stories.Headline: Han Won-seok admits using AI to cheat on state exams and turns himself in to Seoul police
stories.Summary:
Han Won-seok, aged 34, admitted to using artificial intelligence to cheat on a state exam. He confessed in a video posted Sunday on his attorney Lee Don-ho's YouTube channel. The man turned himself in to the Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency after facing public suspicion. He had publicized his high exam performance online during the previous week. This event marks the first known case of a successful state exam candidate admitting AI cheating.

Han used a micro-camera to take photos of questions during the Certified Tax Accountant examination. He sent these images to AI and checked the answers on his smartphone. He also confessed to using the same equipment during the Certified Public Accountant examination. In the tax exam, he missed only one of 160 questions on the first-stage test. He scored 100 in tax law, while the average examinee score was 30.18 out of 100.

Ha Joon-kyung, a policy chief at Cheong Wa Dae, said agencies must prevent AI cheating. He stated that authorities should use all possible methods available at the current level of technology. Ha also requested that test management not create unnecessary anxiety for students using medical equipment. The Human Resources Development Service of Korea said it would file a complaint against Han. They will consult the Finance Ministry and the National Tax Service on follow-up measures.

The Democratic Party of Korea said those responsible must be held accountable in accordance with the law. People Power Party spokesperson Choi Bo-yoon criticized the government for failing to develop technology-based solutions. Choi noted that radio-frequency detectors failed to find AI glasses during a mock test by HRD Korea. Online commentators called for scrutiny of other tests due to unusually high scores this year. One candidate achieved the first perfect score in the 19-year history of the Legal Education Eligibility Test.

Han previously attributed his results to good fortune and his specific study methods. Critics noticed his study materials showed little wear and his handwritten notes contained a misspelling. HRD Korea had stated on Friday that its grading review found no irregularities. Camera footage from the examination room did not show Han wearing suspected AI-powered glasses. He was able to take the examination in front of a proctor without being detected.

The government will deploy personnel to detect AI cheating and strengthen training for proctors. Cheong Wa Dae will investigate other suspicious state qualification exams to see if AI was used. Attention has shifted to the Suneung exam this Thursday, where 550,000 students are expected to sit. The articles leave open whether previous examination results should be scrutinized for similar AI cheating. It remains unclear if the government can develop effective detection technologies before future national examinations.

Articles.Title: AI cheating case raises scrutiny over test administration ahead of Suneung

stories.Headline: AI cameras detect nearly 19,000 potential driving offences in a two week West Midlands trial
stories.Summary:
An artificial intelligence trial uncovered nearly 19,000 potential driving offences during a two week period. The trial took place in March and used AI powered cameras to detect dangerous road behaviours. One image showed a driver drinking from a bottle of wine while another driver inhaled from balloons. Cameras also captured drivers holding mobile phones and people failing to wear their seatbelts. One shocking image showed a front seat passenger holding an unrestrained small child on their lap.

Cameras were installed outside Ladywood fire station in Birmingham and Fallings Park in Wolverhampton. Ladywood saw 11,045 potential seatbelt offences and 1,163 potential mobile phone offences. Fallings Park recorded 6,030 potential seatbelt offences and 757 potential mobile phone offences. The West Midlands Combined Authority funded the trial with the police and fire service. No enforcement was planned as a result of this specific two week AI camera trial.

Road Safety Commissioner Mat MacDonald said the findings highlighted a huge problem with regional driving behaviours. He stated that the results pointed to a widespread culture of potentially lethal behaviours behind the wheel. MacDonald, an NHS doctor, said he was not surprised by the high number of mobile phone users. He noted that it is almost impossible to walk a street without seeing someone dialling and driving. He expressed hope that this technology could eventually be rolled out more widely in the region.

Police and crime commissioner Simon Foster said the trial findings were deeply concerning for the authorities. Dr Christophe Bastien of Coventry University said the technology offers an objective way to understand motorist behaviour. He noted that risky behaviour remains more common than many people think based on these results. Bastien said AI systems are not perfect and should support rather than replace existing police enforcement. The trial affected drivers in Birmingham and Wolverhampton who were captured by the AI sensors.

Road safety data from 2025 linked unfastened seatbelts to 133 deaths on roads in the UK. The same 2025 data showed that mobile phone use was linked to 32 deaths across the country. Mat MacDonald was appointed as the new road safety commissioner in January 2025. He previously served as the chairman of the campaign group known as Better Streets for Birmingham. The AI cameras were trained to recognise specific patterns like drivers using their mobile phones.

The trial was stopped earlier than planned because of the high number of detected road offences. Officials are now talking about the resourcing needed to make this technology viable on the roads. MacDonald said the ultimate goal is for the number of camera activations to reach zero. Foster is evaluating the results to see how AI can be used for future police enforcement. The articles leave open whether the technology will be officially adopted for permanent road enforcement.

stories.Headline: European leaders discuss AI risks to elections at Dublin summit
stories.Summary:
European governments are concerned that states or organised actors could use artificial intelligence to spread misleading content and manipulate public opinion, even to influence election results, according to a report by Filip Polo in Politis. Cyprus' 2028 presidential election is not outside the scope of these concerns over foreign interference and electoral manipulation through artificial intelligence, the report said. Fabricated videos, images and audio recordings that appear authentic can be mass-distributed to mislead voters and shape public opinion. Officials argue the risks go beyond false news, since an organised campaign can damage candidates' credibility, confuse voters and set the election agenda. The issue was discussed with particular emphasis at the informal European Council summit in Dublin on 13 November, where European leaders held a dedicated discussion on artificial intelligence for the first time.

President Nikos Christodoulides told the summit that the malicious use of technology to influence elections threatens all EU countries and that prevention must be in place before interference occurs. Speaking on the sidelines in Dublin, he referred to recent incidents involving schools and to election developments in Romania and other countries, saying the threat concerns the whole European Union. Asked whether Cyprus is also at risk, he said that once such phenomena are recorded in other member states, all countries are vulnerable. He noted that 2027 will be a year of elections across Europe, making it more important for citizens to be informed and for governments to adopt preventive measures. He said authorities should not simply analyse malicious actions after they occur but should have a framework in place so such actions cannot take place.

At EU level, efforts are under way to introduce specific measures to prevent and counter disinformation and electoral manipulation, and these initiatives are expected to apply to Cyprus as well. Leaders also discussed Europe's position in the global race for artificial intelligence, noting a strong research base and dynamic start-ups but heavy dependence on non-European providers for advanced models, computing power, microchips and cloud infrastructure. Arthur Mensch, co-founder and chief executive of France's Mistral AI, presented the prospects for a stronger European ecosystem, and Geoffrey Hinton, awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 2024, highlighted the broader challenges of the technology's development. On 10 November, the Council of Ministers approved Cyprus' first National Artificial Intelligence Strategy, with a horizon extending to 2032, aiming to make the country a trusted artificial intelligence hub in the Eastern Mediterranean. Christodoulides said the technology sector contributes around 15% of Cyprus' GDP and announced a visit to the United States at the end of November to attract companies and encourage the return of Cypriot professionals working abroad.

stories.Headline: Demis Hassabis warns poorly monitored AI systems risk an accidental oil spill style incident
stories.Summary:
Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis warned on the Masters of Scale podcast that the AI industry faces an accidental incident similar to an oil spill, according to a TechGig report published on November 17, 2026. He said poorly monitored AI systems could cause serious damage, and that companies are rapidly building advanced AI systems while safety measures are not keeping pace. He suggested companies should increase investment in AI safety and ensure AI agents are properly monitored rather than operating without human oversight. Hassabis highlighted the risks of the next AI development phase, where systems improve themselves without human supervision, a process he called closed-loop recursive self-improvement.

He cited DeepMind's AlphaZero as an example of recursive self-improvement, noting that it learned to play chess by self-training and quickly surpassed human ability. Hassabis said the process works best in areas like mathematics, coding and games, where AI can verify its own answers. Today's AI tools can boost human engineer productivity by three to five times, but human review and oversight are still involved, he said. The greater risk emerges when AI systems improve autonomously without human checks, which accelerates development but makes control harder, according to his warning.

Hassabis also expressed concerns about AI agents and cybersecurity, suggesting that better engineering could have prevented recent incidents. He advocated for increased AI safety investment and robust monitoring of AI agents, rather than letting them operate without human oversight. The report did not name any specific incident, company or date beyond the podcast appearance and the November 17 publication. The articles did not say what happens next or what action, if any, regulators or companies plan to take.

stories.Headline: Avanade finds New Zealand firms face pressure to accelerate AI adoption but struggle to prove financial returns
stories.Summary:
New Zealand organisations are under growing pressure to accelerate their adoption of artificial intelligence, but most are struggling to show a financial return on those investments, according to new research from Avanade, a Microsoft specialist. The Build Beyond Limits: AI Reality report was based on a survey of 3,600 business decision-makers across 11 markets, including Australia and New Zealand, and it found a widening gap between how organisations see their AI maturity and how far they have actually changed their operations around the technology. Globally, 77 per cent of organisations described themselves as established, advanced or AI-first in their AI journey, and 72 per cent said they were confident their teams were using AI effectively. However, only 18 per cent said they had fundamentally reshaped the way teams operate around AI, and in Australia and New Zealand 84 per cent said they had not fundamentally reshaped how they work with what AI makes possible, including new ways of working, products, services or business models.

The research found that 88 per cent of respondents in Australia and New Zealand said their organisation needs to accelerate AI transformation urgently, even though 68 per cent reported that AI investments have yet to generate financial returns that justify the expenditure. Only 43 per cent said they use business value and return-on-investment metrics to assess AI progress, while 66 per cent had not formally calculated AI's financial return and had it reviewed by finance leaders or senior management. Budget pressures are also emerging, with 26 per cent of organisations in the two countries citing limited funding or pressure to demonstrate ROI quickly as a major barrier to becoming an AI leader. Just 23 per cent reported transformational improvement in what employees could achieve, and the same proportion reported such improvement in operational efficiency and business cost reduction, while 39 per cent said they believe colleagues are using AI in ways compliance teams would not approve of, above the global average of 32 per cent.

Doug Robinson, chief executive of Avanade Australia and New Zealand, said the high adoption rate was a positive sign, telling Reseller News that most clients said they were going great until asked about return on investment, when two-thirds said no. He described a move from hobby AI to enterprise AI, saying people have used the technology first and then brought it to corporates, and that a lot of shadow AI is developing in organisations before they realise it can interrogate corporate data as well as their large language models, which is where the return starts coming. Robinson said the 16 per cent who have already materially changed their business is the number to watch, and he expects it to grow from 16 to 32 to 60 per cent as AI becomes enterprise ready, with ROI following. He said New Zealand organisations are not short on AI ambition but are short on evidence, and that you cannot accelerate adoption responsibly if you cannot say what your AI investment is returning, which most currently cannot.

stories.Headline: Jeff and Sandy Teper give NYU Stern $5 million to launch an annual student AI startup challenge
stories.Summary:
Jeff Teper, Microsoft's Executive Vice President for Apps and Agents, and his wife Alexandra "Sandy" Teper have donated $5 million to New York University's Stern School of Business to establish the Teper Innovation Challenge, an annual competition for students. The gift, reported on November 15, 2026, creates a contest designed to help students develop AI-powered startups and solve real-world business problems. The initiative will provide hands-on experiential learning opportunities for undergraduate and graduate students, with more than $100,000 in annual prize funding for winning teams. The competition will formally launch during the spring 2027 semester, featuring separate tracks and awards for undergraduate and graduate students.

Student teams in the Teper Innovation Challenge will develop AI-native solutions to business challenges, giving them opportunities to experiment with emerging technologies and explore entrepreneurial ideas. The annual competition will encourage students to build and test their concepts, evaluate results, and develop practical applications for artificial intelligence. Beyond the competition, the Tepers' contribution will expand access to frontier technology for Stern students and support the thoughtful integration of advanced AI tools into the school's educational experience. Jeff and Sandy Teper both graduated from NYU Stern, with Jeff earning his bachelor's degree in 1986 and Sandy graduating in 1985, and they met while attending the school.

Jeff Teper currently serves as Microsoft's Executive Vice President for Apps and Agents, and he previously launched and grew SharePoint into a billion-dollar business. He has led teams through major technology transitions involving cloud computing and artificial intelligence, and he was among the inaugural industry leaders to join NYU Stern's Tech Board. Over the years, Teper has hosted Stern students at Microsoft in Seattle, sponsored experiential learning projects in New York City, and advised faculty developing one of the first agentic AI courses at a business school. The new challenge expands his involvement with the university by providing students with opportunities to develop practical AI-building skills.

NYU Stern Dean Bharat Anand said the gift will give students opportunities to experiment with emerging technologies and develop entrepreneurial ideas. The university believes advances in AI are making it easier for individuals to transform ideas into tangible products and businesses. The Teper Innovation Challenge is intended to encourage students to explore those opportunities while learning how artificial intelligence is changing business and the economy. Jeff and Sandy Teper said they had an incredible experience at NYU spanning software engineering and business during the personal computer revolution, and that with the even larger artificial intelligence transformation they are thrilled to support Stern students as they explore, collaborate, and create opportunities in this next wave of technology and the economy.

stories.Headline: Jamaica's government signs MOU with investors to explore AI infrastructure

Prime Minister Dr Andrew Holness announced on Sunday that the Government has approved the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding with a group of investors to explore the establishment of artificial intelligence infrastructure in Jamaica. He made the announcement while speaking at the Jamaica Labour Party's Special Delegates Conference at the Montego Bay Convention Centre in St James on November 15, 2026. Holness did not provide details on the MOU during his address to the party conference. The Prime Minister said Jamaica is to explore the establishment of AI facilities as part of efforts by the Government to maximise economic opportunities and position Jamaicans to participate in the industry.

Holness said the Government recognises the revolution being brought about by AI and wants to position Jamaica to benefit from it. He said the goal is for Jamaica to have a footprint and not only be a consumer of the technology, but to be part of the creation of the technology. The Prime Minister said his administration intends to pursue this so that children can have jobs in the new economy that will be created using artificial intelligence. He said the AI task force established by the Government is providing advice on what needs to be done in this regard.

Holness argued that Jamaica cannot be left behind in the global AI thrust, describing the moment as the cusp of another transition and revolution in technology. He said this revolution is going to increase the productivity of mankind far beyond what can even be imagined now. He repeated that Jamaica cannot be left behind again. The Prime Minister did not give a timeline for the exploration or name the investors involved in the MOU.

stories.Headline: Majority of Australians believe AI risks outweigh benefits according to Lowy Institute poll
stories.Summary:
The Lowy Institute conducted a mini-poll in October 2026 to determine how Australians feel about artificial intelligence. This research found that 65 percent of the population believe the risks of the technology outweigh the benefits. This level of wariness is unchanged from a poll in March but is up 13 points since 2024. Only 33 percent of the surveyed residents feel that the benefits of the technology outweigh the risks.

The survey of 3,028 residents found that only 23 percent are comfortable with businesses using AI sourced from China. Comfort with AI sourced from the United States is slightly higher, with only 36 percent of Australians feeling comfortable. These figures contrast with a December 2025 National AI Plan that aims to make Australia a leading destination for data centres. The Productivity Commission estimated that AI could add more than AU$116 billion to economic activity over the next decade.

Charles Lyons-Jones, a Research Fellow at the Lowy Institute, noted that Australians stand out internationally in their concerns about the technology. He explained that the public is alert to risks, such as China's National Intelligence Law requiring companies like DeepSeek and Zhipu to cooperate with state intelligence. He also noted that government policy may be outpacing public sentiment regarding the hosting of infrastructure. The author suggests the government may face a trade-off between public sentiment and geostrategic imperatives.

Job losses are a major worry, with 76 percent of Australians saying AI will lead to fewer jobs over the next 20 years. This figure is the joint-highest of any country surveyed and is well above the median of 46 percent. Additionally, 52 percent of respondents expect AI to widen the gap between the rich and the poor. These concerns are shared by people who view cyberattacks from other countries as a critical threat to national interests.

The poll occurred against a gloomy economic backdrop where six in ten Australians were pessimistic about economic performance over five years. Inflation remains above target, and the Reserve Bank has raised interest rates three times since March 2026. The Reserve Bank also flagged that AI-related investment could push up input costs and add to capacity pressures. Furthermore, the bank has cut its productivity forecast for 2026 while data centre construction adds to price pressures.

Data centre companies raised at least AU$35 billion in 2026, which is an increase of 46 percent over 2025. The government continues to set expectations for developers regarding innovation, jobs, water, energy, and the national interest. However, the articles leave open whether public sentiment will swing to support American AI as the build-out accelerates. It remains unclear if the government will change its strategy to better align with the views of the public.

stories.Headline: South African author Coral Hart publishes nearly 400 AI-assisted romance novels since February 2025
stories.Summary:
Coral Hart, a South African author with around 14 years of experience in publishing, has released nearly 400 books since February 2025, or roughly one book every other day, according to reporting from the Straits Times cited by Futurism. She initially wrote a few dozen romance novels the traditional way before switching to a blend of ChatGPT, Claude, and Grok to generate her prose. Hart uses more than ten pen names to conceal her identity when she actually sells the books. She told Agence France-Presse that ChatGPT is really good at dialogue but terrible at prose, while Claude is terrible at sex drives. Grok, she said, builds the spicy scenes even though it is completely unhinged at other moments.

Dividing her output of 370 total novels by the days since February 1, 2025, gives a rate of one book for every 1.75 days, or about four books per week. Hart said recent advances in large language models mean she can now draft the whole book in one sequence. She has received tens of thousands of hate messages about her process, yet she thinks of herself as something of an ambassador for it despite the infamy. She told AFP that for the last 16 years nobody had asked her what her creative process was.

Hart also said the technology is here and will not be switched off or unplugged because a bunch of authors said so. Hart is the person responsible for the books, and she has defended them as selling well and as the product of a workflow she is happy with. She described herself to AFP as an ambassador for AI-assisted writing, and she brushed aside the criticism from authors who want the tools shut down. The articles do not say what happens next beyond her stated intention to keep going.

stories.Headline: Huawei unveils architecture to network one million AI processors into a single supercomputer
stories.Summary:
Huawei detailed its Peerium architecture and UnifiedBus 2.0 interconnect on November 11, 2026, to network one million AI processors. The company designed this system to coordinate a massive number of accelerators into a single unified supercomputer. Technical reporting and analyses from Live Science and CASRAI confirmed these architectural details in mid November 2026. Huawei first unveiled the concept at the Huawei Connect 2026 summit before providing further engineering briefings. SDxCentral reported on these expanded briefings on November 4, 2026, regarding the million chip scaling targets.

The system uses UnifiedBus 2.0 to link up to 1,000,000 Neural Processing Units across various hardware tiers. It replaces 196 kilometers of copper cabling in a 4,096 NPU pod with cable free optical LinkBlades. The Atlas 950 SuperPoD integrates 8,192 Ascend 950DT accelerators into a liquid cooled block with unified memory addressing. Inter chassis scale out uses LinkDevice ports at 1.6 terabits per second to achieve 280 terabits aggregate capacity. The UBG Switch allows radix fan out up to 1,024 to scale the fabric to one million NPUs.

Liao Heng, chief scientist for HiSilicon, said the infrastructure is tailored for frontier artificial intelligence models. He noted that six or seven Chinese laboratories target models with 10 trillion to 40 trillion parameters. Rotating Chairman Eric Xu stated that unifying one million processors is the baseline requirement for future training efficiency. ICT Business Group CEO Yang Chaobin said Huawei is opening the UnifiedBus standard to open source communities. Yang mentioned collaborations with the OpenJiuwen project and the DeepSeek Harness optimization framework for international developers.

Independent semiconductor analysts said that coordinating hundreds of thousands of processors introduces severe fault tolerance and thermal overhead. They noted that mean time between failures drops dramatically, which pressures checkpointing systems and automated task rescheduling. University supercomputing directors are affected because future facility designs will require specialized optical liquid cooling infrastructure. Compliance managers must track evolving restrictions as policies now evaluate shared computational access to advanced clusters. Research institutions face a bifurcation of software stacks between Nvidia CUDA and Huawei Ascend or CANN.

Huawei adopted an interconnect centric philosophy to counteract United States Department of Commerce export controls on advanced foundry nodes. These restrictions target sub 7nm processes and high bandwidth memory modules for Chinese entities because domestic foundries face limits. Peerium compensates for these barriers by clustering larger quantities of accelerators through ultra dense packaging instead of per die scaling. This approach diverges from Western standards like Compute Express Link, PCIe Gen 6, and Ultra Ethernet Consortium specifications. Early CloudMatrix 384 implementations packed five times the accelerator density per rack compared to conventional Western equivalents.

Huawei is currently operating an initial Atlas 950 SuperCluster with 256,000 computing cards in Chinese test environments. Commercial shipments of modular Atlas 950 SuperPoD systems will begin for enterprise and institutional customers by early 2027. Engineering teams are now testing Atlas 960 and 960E architectures that integrate Near Packaged Optics to replace transceivers. The articles leave open how the system will handle the 100 trillion parameter threshold projected for 2030. They also leave open the specific results of the ongoing field validation for first generation Peerium systems.

stories.Headline: Start-ups and venture capital firms hire ecosystem leads to build human networks
stories.Summary:
Start-ups and venture capital firms have been hiring people for roles with titles like “start-up ecosystem lead” and “ecosystem growth manager,” jobs that focus on building and maintaining relationships among various parties on a company’s behalf, according to The New York Times. The people in these roles often spend their days planning events, orchestrating partnerships, supporting clients and leading trainings, the article says. The tasks themselves are not really new, but the framing of the work as “ecosystem” building is new. The article was published on November 15, 2026.

Yoni Rechtman, a partner at the venture capital firm Slow Ventures, said that when companies talk about ecosystem they mean cultivating and tending an extended network of partners, distribution channels, supporters and advocates, not just customers. The firm Andreessen Horowitz defined ecosystem as “the bottom-up vector of trust in venture,” and its ecosystem lead described his role as expanding and reinforcing the many networks spanning the firm. Natalie Sportelli has held the title “start-up ecosystem” at Clay, an A.I. sales tool start-up, since January, and her recent projects included putting together product demonstrations for a partner’s portfolio companies and coordinating product coaching sessions with customers. She also collaborated with other start-up program leaders on a panel in London about building A.I.-native sales organizations.

Networking has long been crucial in tech, an industry where warm intros, founder dinners and alumni communities are central to the culture and to deal making, the article says. Lately, start-ups and venture capital firms have sharpened their focus on human connection by hiring for these ecosystem jobs, so the people ushering in the artificial intelligence revolution are doubling down on in-person ties. Ecosystem roles exist on various teams, including marketing, partnerships and sales, and the job’s specifics vary from company to company, Sportelli said. The article does not say what happens next.
